text: I am truly empathetic, when I think about what it must have been like when my great-great grandfather passed through Ellis Island on his journey to America. Cold and hungry, he stood on his feet for hours waiting in line, desperate to pass through the doors and onto the promised land... I can only imagine it must have been akin to my experience standing in line outside pancake pantry in the middle of January. Yes, I have stood in line outside of Pancake Pantry like the rest of the herd. No, I will not do it again! I must give the servers credit for being friendly and prompt even when they are flooded with massive hoards of people every weekend. I think their pancakes really good and I especially love being able to have a variety of fruits and sweet options to add to my pancakes. My usual order are the chocolate chip pancakes. text: I want to understand. I really do. Will someone please explain what happened in the years since I stopped clubbing? I have never, ever, been to a club that was a "club" - as in you had to be a member - but you don't have to pay anything to join (no cover or membership fee.) We had to sign some sort of release or form or contract before we could enter - I don't know what it was. I was so dumbfounded and confused, but aware of the line behind me to get in - that I signed and rushed up the stairs. The decor is hard to figure out. Clearly this was once a nice victorian brownstone - but it's been adulterated to a sickening degree. There is no more opulence, in my opinion. The walls are decorated with ugly murals. The floors are trashed (as you would expect in a bar.) The carpet is nasty. We get to the 2nd floor bar - and I order a drink. Vodka and soda. Hubby orders a beer - and the bartender says "but that's not free." I guess we'd stumbled into a happy hour - no cover, free well drinks and miller lite. (I can see you college kids tripping over each other to get there PRONTO!) I was handed my drink in a plastic cup (just like when I was in college) and hubby stuck with his pricey (not free) Yeungling. The DJ. Seriously, he was SO BAD. He really wanted to be clever and original with his spinning - but what we got instead was awkward transitions, overlapping songs with different beats that DJ AM wouldn't attempt to force together. I wanted to dance! But instead I'd stop mid-beat to try to figure out exactly what dude was up to and how I should be groovin' next. Maybe I just got an off night. I'm certainly not complaining about no cover and free drinks. But I was thoroughly confused by the "club" thing that apparently EVERYONE can join without a fee. I guess that paper I signed was freeing O.N.E. Rittenhouse from any liability should I have too many free drinks and get behind the wheel of my car.

text: I have been to this place two or three times in the last couple years. To the credit of this place, their food is good, and the family style portions are fun when you go with a crowd. It looks like the size of a party room at a Pizza Hut or a Chuck E Cheese or something like that. That room can fit around three dozen people, and unfortunately it's hard to hear the people you eat with, because the acoustics really don't work in your favor. And if ANYONE in that room starts getting loud, you need to either be a great lipreader with your neighbor, or be telepathic, because normal conversation will be hard. For another thing, when the place is packed, service is much slower. The last time (and by that I mean the previous time AND the final time) I was there, I was about 30 min late meeting up with my friends. They were all ready to order, and I hadn't seen the menu yet. But the funny thing is, we didn't order for another 15-20 minutes, because it took that long to get a server to take our order. The food did not come out for an hour, though to be fair it was definitely good when it did come out. But one of our friends never got her food, not even after the rest of us had almost finished our meals. It came out of the kitchen maybe 20 minutes after we got our food, and when she expressed her disappointment in a polite way, the server did not seem to care, and she did not offer an apology. For that, we chose to leave less than the 18% gratuity already added into the check for parties of I believe 6 or more. It seems the majority of people who have reviewed this place like it a lot, and more power to them. But it's all about what you think of your own experiences. And by that standard, I will have to be bribed substantially to set foot in that place again.

text: I want to share with you my experience at Splash. I found this place online when I was looking for a restaurant that was not standard chain fare. I made a reservation for 6pm (I think they opened at 5pm for dinner). I was a bit surprised that when we asked for a booth, we were placed all the way in a corner when 99% of tables and booths were empty. Kind of felt like they were expecting a rush (which never came). Upon being seated, we were greeted by our server who was great. I would say he was the best part of this restaurant by far. Now don't get me wrong, most of this review will sound bad, and it sort of deserves it , but it wasn't all horrible. Service was great and overall, the look of the restaurant was more than adequate. I saw reviews regarding the strip mall thing, but it was no biggie. Overall the food was a bit pricy for what we got. I have paid over $75 for a steak at other places and left feeling like I underpaid, but here, I felt I was not getting my money's worth. We started with crab cakes that were tasty, but seemed to be more filler than crab. It had a unique taste and so my only complaint with the appetiser would be that it should have had more crab. The flavor was good though. Dinner consisted for Tuna (which was about $32) with spinach and a risotto of the day. The person I was with had the sea bass which had a balsamic flavor that was set upon tomatos and topped with melted mozzarella. For me, the tuna was not cut properly and there was a bit too much connective tissue on the bottom. It was cooked great, but the sesame seed crust was a bit too heavy. The spinach was not a sweet flavor, but something was added that made it taste bitter and not to my liking. The sea bass went over well with my companion initially. Although it was large and he could not finish it, he did enjoy it. Dessert consisted of a creme brulee. It was a bit thick (not deep) and lacked true flavor, but was not bad. Once again, like the entire meal, it was ok, but nothing special. The entire time I expected to be blown away by something, but never came close to even mild excitement. For half the price, I would be back more often (and that is including the fact I drove 30 miles to get here). It was unfortunate that the price of the food did not match its quality and for this reason, I rate it poorly. The risotto was served mildly warm...and mine was cool, the food was only ok, and the biggie, my companion actually got sick from the food. He spend last night vomiting up his dinner. Since we ate everything the same but the fish, I can only assume that the sea bass did him in. My recommendation is if you have money to waste, go ahead an try it. Luckily I didn't expect this to be my one nice dinner for this year. But to anyone that saves for a expensive night out, I can say there are plenty of better places to try first. Unfortunately due to the bit of food poisoning, we will not return to this place. If it hadn't been for that, I may have given them a second chance .

text: It's rare in St. Louis to find the sort of place that's on every corner in California. Places like Real Food Daily, Juliano's Raw or every fifth store on any given street that deals in organic foods, healthy beverages and items that require little to no thought whatsoever. You don't have to check labels or constantly ask the person behind the counter, "Does this have sugar/wheat/yeast/white flour in it?" I actually had no idea what OR really was. I'd heard about it in passing but never knew it was this special haven for the physiologically challenged and/or health-conscious set. First off, you can't really use cell phones here. I think there's one table designated for cell use. Then there's an ad selling that diode reducer or the device said to make your cell less harmful to you. It's very tiny inside in terms of seating options, but it's a glorious treasure trove of healthy items like xylitol, pamphlets and books about iridology and food combining, all manner of supplements and even some sort of salt said to be particularly nutrient rich. There's a giant board listing all the lovely food and beverage options, and even a board that recommends beverage pairing/food combining suggestions. I got a bowl of squash and lentil soup with ginger. It was tasty and filling. And I got a peppermint tea. Very simple fare for my first go around, but I've heard the spring rolls are the best in town and aim to try those next.

text: Great Museum! Located in Jackson Square next to the St. Louis Cathedral, the Louisiana State Museum consists of two buildings - the Presbytere and the Cabildo. This is one of the first things that I did in NOLA and it was definitely a worthwhile experience. Plan to spend a 2-3 hours taking in the history of this great city and state. Exhibits include an overview of the founding of NOLA, the antebellum period, the Civil War, and Reconstruction. Highlights inlcude a walk through the room where the Louisiana Purchase was signed, a display on Andrew Jackson and the Battle of New Orleans, as well as the death mask of Napoleon Bonaparte. The exhibit did end rather abruptly - I thought there would be a lot more about 20th century history including displays on Huey Long. The price of admission is extremely reasonable and includes a visit to the Mardi Gras Museum next door. While not nearly as comprehensive as the Presbytere, the exhibit is a fun showcase of Mardi Gras costumes, floats, and history. Overall, a must see for a first time visitor to NOLA. The Louisiana State Museum will help you get a terrific overview of the city's history, cutlture, and heritage.

text: A wealthy friend introduced me to Rescue about 5 years ago. I've gone every couple of months for every service they offer except massage. It's best described as an urban spa, which means exactly that. Do not expect a series of rooms to chill in the dark before and after the service. The space is dressed in white and is quietly and appropriately busy. Generally, it delivers what it promises to deliver. For those coming from the West Coast and all of its water-centric Asian spas and onsens, you will find none of it here. It's taken me years to find a Korean spa nearby and I drive 45 min to get to it. For facials, I really like Monica. Like Danuta (the owner) and Nives (the make-up and brow tech), Monica is originally from Eastern Europe. She does a very, very good job. I have my first appt with Danuta in March (she is usually booked months in advance) and have high expectations for the results. For waxing, I like Tirzah. I've had waxes with every person on staff I think. Recently, I've noticed that when I get a Brazilian, I actually have to ask them to do anything "in the back." What's happening here? Isn't that what differentiates a regular bikini wax from a Brazilian wax? I really don't want to have to *ask* for it. Like, ever. I've had my eyebrows shaped (not waxed; I break out) by Nives and Erica. Nives has a fabulous sense of style and her make up application is worth paying for, just to learn what's what. I came in a couple of times for brows, and she did an amazing job, commanding my brows to grow in and reshape themselves. 6 months later, Erica essentially destroyed what Nives had done. I will not go back to Erica. For nails, the only tech I like is Anna Maria. She's really good. My only gripe is that the benches are not comfortable to sit on, but I think they've just remodeled that space. Going for a pedicure in February, so we'll see.

The pumpkin curry tofu was out of this world!! They give you a choice of mild, medium, or hot, so we played it safe and got the medium. It wasn't that hot so we'll probably go hotter next time. Anywho, it had large chunks of just regular fried tofu (just the way I like it!) fresh basil, red and green peppers and yes, pumpkin! I've never actually eaten cooked pumpkin before but it was cut up similarly as to how you would cut up a cantaloupe. It even had small green edges and every time I bit into it, I expected a hard, undercooked piece just as though I was eating an unripe cantaloupe. But NO! It was sooo soft that it melted in my mouth and was so sweet. Oh my goodness, I can't stop raving about it. The fried tofu app was about $2-3 and the pumpkin tofu was about $11-12, so between my boyfriend and I, I think our total was $16 with tax and everything. $8 a person is not that bad these days for a solid and very local meal such the one we devoured from Circles!

Add to that ZERO supervision from their parents and you have the makings of a pre-school riot in the middle of a fine dining "Grill". Seeing my displeasure one of the kids, a cute little girl, said "I'm sorry if we're being too noisy" and then proceeded to pull the rip cord on her over the top rope battle royal toy, which then spun out of the big bowl she was using and onto the ground hitting my foot. My recommendation for Davids is to bring the kids... all of them! Bring their toys... musical instruments, skateboards, pogo sticks, hula hoops, roller blades, jump ropes, hockey sticks etc... because it's not a place for a nice romantic dinner... But it could be with a little parental influence. text: Furnishings: cute. Table toys: cuter. Service: great! Vegan burger: glue! Bite down and a crisp shell gives way to a sudden gloppy load in your mouth. Granted the vast majority of restaurant veggie burgers are made from box mix, so perhaps anything that's not an obvious mix nets an instant A+ rating. I respectfully disagree. To be fair, the bun, plus tomato and onion I had added were all very fresh and perfectly good. Coke: fed from the bar lines. Not gross tasting like Royal Tavern's perpetually funky soda lines. Just kinda 'eh and diluted, without discernible Coke flavor. Spanish fries: that's a big Don't, 10-4. Unless you like your old bay seasoning by the tablespoonful. In which case, have at 'em. So I liked the place well enough, and really the service was my-t-fine. But the food -- or at least the thing I choose -- was grody. text: Oh no! I love Tiffin. When they had their buffet I would go every weekend, sometimes on both Saturday and Sunday. I order from Tiffin several times a month. They make fantastic, fresh, and healthy Indian food. So when Tiffin Etc was introduced (with e-mails and launch parties galore) my girlfriend and I couldn't wait to give it a try. Too bad the food was delivered ice cold, tasted bland at best, and was in no way of the quality that I would have expected.We ordered a large Murg Makhani pizza, a Seekh Kebab, and an Aloo Paratha. The pizza was the best of the bunch, though that doesn't mean that I'd rush out to eat it again. The idea is interesting, and based on other reviews on yelp I thought that it would taste sort of like an inspired Nan covered with tandoori chicken. What we got was a dinner plate sized circle of undercooked dough covered with a few pieces of chewy, mildly flavored chicken. The kebab was like something from a food cart that you know to avoid because it always has short lines. Bland minced meat with a few onions thrown in, luke-warm in a cold, too-thin wrap. The paratha tasted like they forgot to add any spice, and maybe any potato. Basically a close to empty thin pancake. I suggest to pass on trying Tiffin Etc. text: It had been quite a while since I had been to Catelli - and decided it would be great for Valentine's dinner. I was expecting a bit less because of the day-- but over all, especially in food department, they came thru shining. We check in and had about a 5 minute wait for our table - no big deal given it was Vday. Our waiter greeted us, noticing we had drinks already. He was very friendly and chatty - though for the rest of the evening, he seemed to always be about a step behind. They had a set limited menu for Vday -I knew that going in, but the selection was large and there were also 4 specials. I didn't have a problem finding something I wanted- and my guy was overwhelmed with the selection and specials. I started with a cream of wild mushroom soup which was completely delicious and he got the lobster bisque which he describe as 'like silk, wonderful'. We went on to apps- I am VERY particular about eggplant- so ordering the eggplant rolletine was a fence sitter, but WOW - done to perfection, I mean perfection. I rarely say that about eggplant. He got the seafood ravioli special as an app and loved every bite. For entrees he went with the veal chop, which he said was done perfectly and he didn't need a knife...served over lobster mash potatoes. I ordered the Ravioli in a pepper blush sauce, which comes with lump crab meat that I ask them to hold off (being a veg) they had no issue with that, in fact they brought it out on a separate plate so my hunny could enjoy it : ) The sauce was excellent and I enjoyed going in with the fresh baked bread to finish it off. The dessert tray came and was full of a ton of things I love... but at the waiter's suggestion I skipped the creme brulle, the crepes and the key lime tart and I went with banana bread pudding, since I love banana and bread pudding. We ordered coffee also -- which came right away - unlike our dessert. When it finally came, it was sadly our only food disappointment of the evening...all I could taste was cinnamon, fresh shaved cinnamon, but it took over the whole dessert. I could not get a taste of banana or creaminess that is usually in bread pudding thru the whole thing.. My second cup of coffee never came - and our waiter didn't realize it until after he brought our check, ran our card...etc.. So the waiter being off and the badly done dessert kept this from being a 5 star experience for me, but over all I truly enjoyed it.

text: I am laughing at some of the recent reviews; our experience there last Saturday was so bizarre, I'd assumed it was uniquely our own. But, apparently, it was the norm. Here is our story: we went in around 6 just to grab something quick to eat because we had a late lunch. We each ordered calamari marinara, and we just ordered ice cream for our little guy. We waited 40 minutes before we finally got the hostess over to find out what was wrong. She rambled on unintelligibly, and then went back to her job. We finally got the nice waitress over, who astoundingly told us that they had "a new chef" and he didn't know how to make our orders. She was shocked and embarrassed that no one had told us, or come over to give us a chance to order something else. Long story short : after sitting there for an hour (having eaten salads and bread and iced teas), we walked out without dinner. We were so astounded that we laughed rather than get angry. I tend to agree with the comment from a previous poster about the seating arrangements. When we arrived, the main part of the restaurant was empty, but they sat us in the small, very flourescently-lit annex with the handful of other diners. We had a bad feeling immediately upon entering. I'd eaten there 10 years ago when I last lived in Nashville and very fondly remember a fantastic lasagna. That was what brought me back; but I'll never go back again.

text: Owned and operated by South Philly trash and lit up like a shitty traveling carnival attraction, going to Geno's is through-and-through a bad experience. The way the employees seem to resent their customers for bothering them by patronizing their establishment, and especially the obese man/woman character who slices the bread for the sandwiches complete the carnie vibe. I'd give the food a C-, and definitely not worth the $9 or whatever it is they charge now. For my two cents, it is better than Pat's, whose meat I find to be dry and undigestible. To be sure, you will get a better steak from ANY other sandwich shop in Philly (besides Pat's) or any other city for that matter. There is something humbling about going to Geno's. Usually when I'm there it's at an hour when most decent people are asleep (Geno's is open 24hrs). You get into a long line with money in hand, for fear of not being prepared to get out of the cashier's sight the moment they shove your overpriced pile of meat in your hand. Then there's the ridiculous streamlined ordering system (the "wiz wit or witout" shit) which I suppose originated naturally by regulars, but now feels contrived because it is mandatory. I want to gag sometimes when I hear myself say it. You slink off, happy to be out of eye-shot of the miserable people making sandwiches inside. Then there's Mr. Geno's steaks himself, Joey Vento. A real-life Jed Clampett, Mr. Vento comes off as a lovable lug who made it big. He seems like a nice guy, aside from his divisive political views which he has no qualms about sharing. That doesn't bother me. I imagine that if Jed Clampett went on a racist tirade about terrorists and Middle Eastern Oil, he'd be forgiven on the grounds of being a rich, overindulged rube, too. Yet another aspect of Geno's that is in bad taste is the police and firefighter theme. Being a person who hates cops, and ESPECIALLY over-the-top, tasteless pandering, this really gets me. There is a giant plaque of Daniel Faulkner's surly mug (cop who was allegedly killed by Mumia Abu Jamal 30 years ago) right out front. As if this wasn't enough to dissuade anyone from going to Geno's, consider the case of the gentleman who was beaten up by Geno's goons after discovering meat delivered surreptitiously in the middle of the night was labeled as coming from some South American country from a year previous. Granted, he got beaten up for keying Geno's Hummer, but he discovered year old meat from a different continent all the same. Go America

text: Love this place. Great decor, friendly staff, good food. Everything you could want from a neighborhood bar, and then some. Other less frequent events like the Old City Sideshow or Belle & Sebastian Dance Party are worth checking out too. Check their website or facebook for up to date events, there's almost always something cool going on. * I know I mentioned the decor, but it bears repeating. The inside of this place is awesome. Steampunky and cozy, warm and woodsy. * This place gets PACKED on Friday and Saturday nights. Great DJs and a pretty fun crowd (obviously it's Old City, gonna have your share of douchebags and douchettes, but still). But if you're a regular, they'll take care of you. On more than one occasion I've been a few heads back from the crowded bar and one of the bartenders has noticed me and made my usual drink before the afore-mentioned douchey people. text: OH EM GEE. My friend told me about this place when i told her i was heading to the city around my birthday. After perusing the menu we decided to go with the Mediterranean pizza and the BLT pizza (the latter catching my eye immediately). The latter however had what appeared to be house smoked bacon, fresh shaved cheddar cheese, micro greens, roasted tomatoes and a garlic aioli drizzle on top. text: OK folks. I cannot stress this enough. If you are anywhere near Yemanja Brasil on a Friday between 5pm and 7pm--YOU MUST GO FOR HAPPY HOUR!!!!!!!! Phew! The nachos were pretty generic--corn tortillas, fake cheese, jalepenos. The wings were excellent. Just spicy enough to make you sit up and take notice but not hot enough to make you curse the cook. The upstairs is also decorated beautifully. Lots of tables, some couches, fireplace, some great local artwork and interestingly enough, a foozeball table is tucked away in the back out of sight from most of the tables. text: Unfortunately I had a serious traffic accident on December 26th. As a consequence of this accident I had a painful chest, and a swollen right wrist and leg. Pennsylvania Hospital was the place were I was taken. The emergency room seemed quiet for most of the evening. They called me twice up front for triage and registration. After about two and a half hours, I was taken to the back where patients are seen. The only person that actually spoke to me was the nice cleaning lady that had just prepared the room for us. I laid in bed for another two and a half hours, during that time I had the pleasure of hearing all the personnel of the hospital telling each other about their holiday experiences and gifts. Funny enough, in the room next to mine there was a woman wailing for hours and when I say wailing I mean that the loud painful and desperate screams could not be ignored by anyone in a two mile radius. text: I have been to this place three times now, each time having a better experience than the last. The first time I visited was just a few weeks after they opened during the summer. We sat on the patio during a lovely, perfect summer evening. Our waitress greeted us promptly and handed us our menus. Their offerings were sparse, but succinct - I knew this ahead of time, per previous reviews. We ordered the margherita pizza and the "four cheese" pizza. A quick 15 minutes later, our pizzas arrived piping hot and looking outstanding. I will be honest, when I first saw them, I was a SMIDGE disappointed - they were a bit smaller than I anticipated, and everything seemed unevenly distributed over the pizza. Upon first bite, however, I knew I was in for a treat. The pizza has that perfect crust, in my opinion - slightly crisp, chewy, and just flexible enough to be folded over and eaten "New York-style." Tangy sauce, fresh mozzarella, and a true wood-fired taste really sent this pizza over the top. Both the margherita and the four-cheese were delicious, and after each piece came the difficult choice of which kind to choose next. Fast forward a few months, to a few weeks ago. We decided to walk down, since it is just a block or so from our house. This time we sat inside at the counter, as it was chilly and crisp outside. We had a good view of the wood-fired oven, and began a nice conversation with the pizza-maker (a big, super friendly Italian guy from NYC). This time we ordered the Italian sausage pizza and the pizza topped with feta cheese, gyro meat, tomatoes, lettuce, and tzatziki sauce. The sausage pizza was delicious, with true spicy Italian-sausage thrown liberally on top. However, the real standout was the "gyro pizza", as we called it. I HIGHLY recommend this pizza! Folded over, it was akin to eating a hot, fresh gyro with crispy chewy crust. Completely to die for. Last visit was a few days ago with my neighbor, and I suggested the "gyro" pizza to split, and we both ordered a salad. The caprese salad was outstanding, and beautifully presented - sliced tomatoes and fresh mozzarella, stacked, drizzled with olive oil and balsamic, topped with fresh basil, and served with a couple of bread points. She apparently enjoyed her caesar salad, as well, because she cleaned her plate... and I swear a frown crossed her face as she took her last bite. A glass of Peroni and a pizza later, I cannot recommend this place highly enough. I challenge you to set aside your notion of what "pizza" is in St. Louis, and expand your palate to include the wood-fired, Italian way.

text: This is a rather long review, but I think it's important for people to read for their own health before they choose Fringe Salon I made a first-time appointment with Roberta for a cut and a color for my shoulder-length, thick, curly hair. During this period I mentioned once or twice that the treatment was rather painful, but Roberta did not really assess my head to see whether the chemicals were causing any damage. After she washed the excess color off, my hair was a very bright, brassy blonde and I told Roberta that I was not happy. She argued this fact, stating that I was just not used to my hair being all one color (she also tried to tell me that it was the same as my previous color). I finally convinced her to put a rinse on my hair, which was turned out so ashy that it made my hair look almost grey. By that point the salon was closing but, contrary to the rest of her behavior that day, Roberta kindly stayed to finish the cut, which turned out to be very flattering. The worst part of this experience was the day after when I found that I had blisters all over my scalp. A different stylist who fixed my color (at another location) told me that the blistering was so severe that she was surprised I hadn't gone to the ER. This second stylist also said that if she had done to any of her customers what Roberta had done to me that she would have been fired for rudeness and sheer negligence. Funnily enough I tried to blame myself for this awful situation, but I was reminded by a hair professional that if Roberta had not thought that she could do what I asked for, that she should have refused. Please be wary that at least one of the stylists at Fringe does shoddy work, and does not care about their patrons! UPDATE: Erin is correct, Roberta did try to contact me once after my appointment, but that is only because I missed the followup appointment (that I would have had to have paid for) to fix the poor job that Roberta did. Also, due to the intense pain I was experiencing from the blisters, I was unable to wash my hair for a week. In my eyes the bond of trust that you're supposed to have with your stylist was already broken. In fact, since my review, instead of contacting me to tell me how sorry they are about the poor service and about receiving such damaging scalp burns, Roberta personally messaged me to tell me that I had flamed her on the internet, and that she had done nothing wrong. text: The hotel is very nice, but the service was beyond terrible. My boyfriend and I stayed there and we have never been treated so poorly by staff of an upscale hotel. I'm guessing the reason for this is because we are in our early-mid twenties, but our experience was bad enough that I wrote to the better business bureau. We had a bag full of Christmas gifts magically disappear from our room and when we reported it to the front desk, the head of security said that I was lying or had misplaced the bag. We checked out immediately and filed a report with the police, as the bag contained a brand new iPod, over $200 in gift cards, and several other moderately expensive gifts. The head of security would not let the police come to the hotel because, he said, it would look bad for business and instead only spoke with them over the phone. A few days later their general manager said that one of the cleaning staff had accidentally thrown away the bag of gifts but they did nothing to compensate us. I don't know if that's the truth or the gifts were stolen but I can't believe they would do nothing for their error. We have stayed in many hotels and resorts all over the world and have never experienced such disregard for customer service. Only stay at this hotel if you lock up your valuables and don't mind rude and incompetent attendents. text: REAL authentic Mexican food in St. Louis??? I couldn't even believe my eyes when I saw the food from this place, and it tasted amazing. The Carne Asada (beef) Torta was phenomenal. The bun was excellent, and toasted just right. I didn't like the red salsa very much, it had a weird smokey flavor that overwhelmed the spiciness. The green salsa was amazing, so much flavor and so good. The Beef Tacos were also delicious and had tons of flavor. The Horchata was incredibly good and cut the spiciness of the food just right. They also had great looking agua frescas and Mexican Coke. The prices were very reasonable, around $5.50 for a Torta and $1.75 for a taco. The service was very good as well. They have plenty of outdoor seating, which seemed really nice, but the inside is tiny. They have a counter that runs along the side of the building where you can sit, right next to the kitchen. It can feel like you are literally in the kitchen.

text: Upon walking in to Arnauds, I felt like I was entering a prohibition-era speakeasy. As if I would know...except for what I've read in history classes and seen in the movies. Based on my extensive viewings of The Untouchables, I feel my expertise is pretty well rounded. The fact that Arnauds is red-headed-stepchild connected to Remoulade is comical...similarities, there are none, except they're both within a block of about 5 strip clubs. Dinner and a show? SLAM...duh duh duh, duh duh duh... Anyways--for those who've been to Remoulade and are dissuaded from trying Arnauds, dont be...Arnauds is a great place to eat. The waiter and various servers were well versed when it came to describing the menu and how the food was prepared, wine selection and how to eat bread. Douchebag Matt was cutting the bread loaf with a knife when I was advised that in New Orleans, they tear pieces off. Time to fill the va-jay-jay with cement and be a man. I started with the Arnauds Salad--a mixed green medley with creole mustard vinaigrette dressing...destroyed it. Followed that with the Breast of Chicken Rochambeau--isn't that the game where you take turns kicking your friend in the balls? While that's not how I felt after eating it, I was pleasantly surprised that the bearnaise and bordelaise sauces satisfied my palette, not to mention the potato chunks underneath.... To finish, I had Strawberries Arnaud...Fresh strawberries in a marinade of port, red wine, spices, sugar cane syrup and citrus finished off with Brocato's French vanilla ice cream and whipped cream. Yep, I copied that right off the web site b/c there's no way a man of my caliber would remember such intimate details about dessert. I do tear bread, after all. You'll like it... I highly recommend this dining destination next time you're in town. It's a nice break from the fried crawfish shrimp etouffee jambalaya red beans and rice alligator sausage that you can find on every shiftee-low-down-gritty-and-grimy corner of the French Quarter. Your arteries will thank you. And Onyx should thank me for incorporating that old school crew into my review. Twice.

Eating outside is a huge recommendation on the patio with the well tended garden and the overall cozy feel of the place. The service is friendly and the food is very good, but nothing spectacular. Each bite is full of flavor and unless you're a picky eater, it'll be an amazing tasting experience. The sangria had a very fresh and fruity taste to it without tasting like juice. Went on a Friday night so we could catch the Flamenco/Spanish guitar performance which was great. The atmosphere, the crowd, the service and the quality made this place one of my favorite in Philly. The chef-owner went through El Vez and Alma de Cuba and finally branched off to bring us Amada. He's planning to open more Nueva Latina themed restaurants soon! Cant wait!

They're both great, but they get old after a dozen or two times. Also, if I was going to be dining with my parents & slightly-less-than-normal aunt, I would need a place capable of continuously supplying me with beer....lots of beer. Finally, I had a chance to try the Race St. Cafe! I've been wanting to get there for a while...seemed like such a cool place. Well, it was the perfect idea. From the minute I walked into this place, I knew I was going to like it. Easy going, nice people, cool atmosphere, and...lots & lots of beer. Dad & I quickly ordered...Oktoberfest for me, and I think a #9 for him (at first he was thinking Coors light...but after a seriously disappointing grin from me, he changed his mind). The menu was adequately sized...not huge, but very good, with great variety, and well-priced. Perfect for this place! All in all, the meal was great. I'll definitely go back soon, hopefully without the parents. This is one of the few bars in the city that I know of that are perfectly fine to go to alone (if necessary). Being that many of my friends are reluctant to go out in the city (or even leave their damn house)....this is a big plus. It's nice to escape the ridiculousness that Old City can be sometimes. Race Street Cafe does a nice job of being different, and different is always GOOD.

text: Here's the deal. I don't want to stand in line, pay prices equivalent to a full service restaurant, fight with 20 people for condiments and then fight for a table. A tasteless burger (referring to the patty) with bacon and cheese can be found anywhere. Menu; 5/10 The price points are not clear and too high, they have signature burgers such as the bacon cheese burger but do not have any price next to it and an ambiguous and small list of condiment prices (which are ridiculous). Honestly, In-n-Out blows this place OUT OF THE WATER. The choices in meats are a redeeming factor but again, there is much obfuscation in ordering. Ordering; My wife and I had about 30 seconds in line before we were before a register. It was too fast and for about 25 bucks, I want a waiter, not a rapid order, pick up food, put on condiments, find a table experience. Table, hard to find inside. Not fun walking around a restaurant you don't know trying to find a table with a full plate of food. Eating; Burger patty was basically flavorless, bacon, cheese, condiments were decent. Fries semi mushy (nothing special, not even close to the "World's Greatest Burger". Eating Part 2; 4 employees came around (within 5 minutes) during our meal to ask us about our food. It wasn't even quality control, it was just uncomfortable. Refill my drink, get me condiments (which they don't do) but just leave me alone and let me eat. Bottom Line: I wouldn't return. So many better burgers, restaurants, and experiences elsewhere. Go to In-N-Out, Carl's, or even Burger King, this place isn't worth it.

The service department quoted me $3500 for a new transmission plus parts and labor. I found another facility- a transmission specialist a few miles away who were able to do the same work with the same parts for $1500. When I told Pacifico I'd be paying to have another tow truck retrieve my truck from their lot, Reggie in their service department arrived at the magic figure of $200 for "Electronic Transmission Diagnosis." I asked about what that meant and his response was the same verbal garbage that gave service shops a bad name for the last 50 years. He could've been reading a passage from Harry Potter. Another gentleman named Joe who worked at Baja came over and explained that all the margaritas are made with fresh squeezed juice, YUM! It seems to be the secret to a perfect margarita. My guess is that this place is great for bringing a bottle of wine and spending a lot of money on the entrees and more experimental dishes/specials. text: I came to Buck's based on positive recommendations from others I know, and the fact that they're relatively close to where I live so, in this hot summer, it's not much of a bike ride to get back over there to pick up the car. When I dropped it off, I mentioned what the issue was (noise when starting and the a/c condensation flooding into the floor) and gave my keys. He handed me a paper with a charge of $46 on it and told me to sign it. I understand that you're using their techs' time to check out your car's issues, but I've never had to sign off on a preemptive charge. Whatever though, I guess it's understandable. Should have left there though and refused it. Even though it wasn't a killer walk (maybe a little over a mile), I was offered a ride home and decided to take it. However, I wasn't told that the guy was going 5 miles in the wrong direction FIRST before dropping me off, then winding through a speed bumpy trailer park. Walking would have been a little bit longer in time, but not by much. About 4 hours later, I got a call from them regarding the work. The work I had requested was done but they had other issues for me: CV boot replacement and that I had to "clean" the bottom of the car. Total cost for the CV boots was about $430 for parts and labor, this on top of the approximately $90 I paid to resolve the issues I brought it in for, plus that $46 charge that I originally signed off on. I balked and said I would just pick it up and think about it, because they said they had to order a part from Phoenix to fix it anyway. So I brought the car back home. A few minutes later, Buck's calls me again: the tech had left his flashlight in my car and they wanted it back. They also said that the shield had been left off but they would put that back in when I brought it back. Sure enough, I look inside, and the plastic shield between the center console and passenger floor is off and laying on the floor. It took me just a couple of seconds to snap it back on, but why the hell leave it off? I don't understand that one. The flashlight wasn't in there either, so I don't know what was going on there. The kicker though was that I took it to my repair place the next day (place that I trust) and had them look at the CV boots. Initially they told me $89.95 over the phone but, after looking at the work, they wanted $218 total because there was more labor involved. So, essentially, I paid half of what Buck's wanted for the exact same work. And I got a look at the bottom of the car that they wanted to clean: I don't see it. It's dirty down there but, shit, it's the bottom of a car. Nothing that would impede anything. Lesson here is ALWAYS shop around. I called 4 different places before taking it in to my place. Most are willing to give you a rough estimate if you know exactly what's wrong but, of course, they won't know exactly how much until they actually see it. But I would say leave Buck's off of that call list.

text: Not quite a three, but much better than a two. Two and three-quarters? My wife and I were looking for a quick little weekend getaway from Chicago to celebrate our anniversary. We settled on St. Louis, as I had lived there for a number of years and she hadn't ever had the opportunity to visit. Lafayette Sqare, the neighborhood within which the B&B is located, has come a long way. Kathy, one of the owners, was very keen on letting us know all of the amenities that the neighborhood had to offer. Initially very welcome information, but more on that in a moment. The B&B itself? I'll dissect it into three parts: Bed, Breakfast, and Booking. Bed: We felt that the room was a fantastic value. We had a fine queen bed, beautiful marble-tiled bathroom, wonderful view of both the small and peaceful garden in the adjacent lot and of the Arch. The remainder of the appointments in the space were welcome as well. The modern conveniences...a mini-fridge, telephone, alarm clock and LCD TV were unobtrusive for the most part. The decoration in the home was considered carefully, with some tongue-in-cheek portraits of dogs wearing military uniforms hung in the staircase, complementing the otherwise fairly consistent Victorian-era decor. Amusing. Considered on the whole, we really enjoyed our room. Breakfast: Not great, but not terrible. Perhaps the home was catering to a different sort of visitor who didn't have such a rigid schedule, but when we were told breakfast would be served at 9 and to "please ensure that we were there on time." We assumed that meant pretty close to 9AM, and with a full day of sightseeing planned, we also hoped that would be the case. Due to what we were told was the humidity in the area having a negative effect on the quiche/souffle rising in the oven, we were not invited to the breakfast table until 9:50. Coffee was available and the rest of the guests were enjoyable to speak with, but neither my wife nor I really wanted to be continually told, "It'll just be a few minutes" and then have breakfast nearly an hour later. The breakfast was pleasant enough...a small quiche with some ham, cheese and sprigs of rosemary on top. The side was about a half-dollar sized portion of hashbrown, and two strawberries that had been chocolate-dipped. No real complaints, just nothing we felt we could rave about. Coupling that with the fact that it came so much later than we anticipated, we skipped breakfast on Sunday in favor of striking out and finding somewhere else to eat at...you know...an ordinary breakfast time. If you have the time to wait though and enjoy a couple hours of small talk with the other guests, then perhaps this may be for you. Also, grab your appropriate grain of salt--I am basing my opinion on one breakfast. In speaking with some of the other guests, I believe that our experience was not the norm. (Both the quality and timeliness.) Booking: The last area we feel compelled to comment on was with the booking of the visit. We explained that we would require a late check-in on the online booking form, and the owners were very accomodating, telling us that they would leave us a key in a predetermined location. Great. Easy enough. We received a call to our cell phone from one of the owners around 7 PM asking: "Where are you?" Fair enough question. I told them where we were and that we planned on arriving at the time we had previously agreed upon. I was told: "No, you should be here in about an hour and a half", and got a weird vibe from the tone...like one part travel advice and one part command. Ever feel like you're talking with somebody but not really communicating with them? This was that moment. She just couldn't understand that we were going to take our time to get there, as previously arranged. We arrived at about 10 P.M., greeting some of the other guests who were playing a board game in the parlor, and went straight up to bed as we had an action-packed Saturday planned. The next morning (while the humidity was causing the quiche to not rise) we received what we felt like was another interrogation about what took us so long to get there. Again, for the security of the B&B and the comfort of the other guests, I completely understand why they want people to arrive within a predetermined window, but if a late arrival was going to be a problem, I suppose we would have just appreciated hearing that up front, and we'd happily have found somewhere else to stay with no hard feelings. In sum: +1 star for the room and home. +1 star for the centrally located and easy-to-find location. If you've never been to St. Louis before and have no idea what you want to see, these folks are great. If you know what you want to see, just realize that the owners are very proud of their neighborhood, and will try hard to keep you there regardless of whether or not you had other plans! ;o)

Ok, the hotel wasn't spotless - the hallway carpet was stained, and the walls had marks on them and stuff. text: Sushi Land, a suburban BYOB, serves sushi and other kinds of Japanese cuisine - we shared a bowl of Agedashi tofu which was interesting. It's a clean, modest-sized venue that can handle about 40 diners. The decor is simple and appropriately Japanese-themed. While interaction with our servers was kept to a minimum, service was friendly when we dealt with them. A few of us dined here this past weekend. I went for the Villanova roll ($8.50), made of spicy tuna, crunch, unagi, and tobiko goodness, and the Cliff House roll ($9.50), with spicy crabmeat, shrimp tempura, salmon, avocado, and tobiko. Both rolls were pleasantly fresh, with a crispy consistency that was fun to bite into, and I loved their tangy, mildly spicy flavors. (Our server told us the chef made the rolls extra attractive because he saw me taking photos!) We all had sushi rolls, and all enjoyed them. Don't feel like driving downtown for Zento's sushilicious creations? Sushi Land will quell any suburbanite's sushi urges, and for a reasonable amount of money. Worth a try!

text: I've never been one of those people who swear that Blueberry Hill is the greatest thing since like the arch. Yeah, it's a good place to drink and eat fried stuff late at night, the dartboards are fun, and all the memorabilia is pretty cool, but it's never been my first choice for a meal. But, I have a friend in from out of town and she wanted to meet there for lunch today. I was actually pretty okay with it, thinking maybe it was high time I gave Blue Hill another try. After all, 136 yelpers can't be wrong. I did remember one horrible burger experience with that blob of soft cheese. Never again. It was grainy and bright orange and a strange hummus-like texture. So, this time, I went with the 5 oz hickory burger, which sounded to me like a bbq burger. It was not. My big mistake was forgoing cheese or bacon, thinking my burger would be covered in sauce. The was in fact no bbq sauce to be found and the burger was pretty dry. There was this teeny tiny little thimble-sized cup of some pink stuff. Apparently that was the hickory sauce? It looked like thousand island dressing to me. And, if that was was made this burger the "hickory burger," you would think you would actually get enough to spread fully on the bun. Also, the bun, while good, was way bigger than the burger. Note to Blueberry Hill, order some smaller buns for the smaller burgers so they don't look so tiny! We also got fries which reminded me of dorm fries from college. The highlight of the meal for me was a diet Fitz's root beer. I don't drink soda, so this was a real treat. But, the food was just not awesome. Maybe I'm missing something here, but Blueberry Hill burgers just don't do it for me.

text: Harrahs was going to be our annual anniversary spot. We were married in Reno and spent our honeymoon at Harrahs. I was unaware that not only were they going to take out the room rate, but 3X the room rate - in case we stole a pillow or something. Had I been informed of this, I would have gladly have paid in either cash or a Visa. I found out that my account was overdrawn the next day when I was trying to buy a small gift. It took over a week for them to release the hold on my account after calling them several times and getting the run around each time...it seemed it was always someone else's screw-up. Also, a friend wanted to pay for our room and went through endless circles with Harrahs reservations in order to do so...it took him several hours on the phone and could not find one person willing or capable to do that for him. text: First off, had this been written a couple of years ago, it would have been easily five stars. But things change, and change fast in the restaurant business. Shortly after the old chef left (which was about two years ago IIRC), I had gone back craving the restaurant I had grown to love only to find that everything (on the menu at least) that I loved had been taken away. It was like waking up next to your long-time S.O. one morning and discovering that she had been replaced by Janet Reno. I tried to stay optimistic after learning that my beloved bisque would no longer grace my palate and seeing that the former novelesque menu had been reduced to a single page (it may have grown more since then). However when the roast chicken that I had ordered arrived far too dry and with none of the flair I had come to expect from Bella Brava's dishes, I knew that it was time to file for divorce from my favorite restaurant. I've heard some good things since then and really hope they've improved themselves but I haven't been able to bring myself to make it back there again yet.

text: Often before visiting restaurants, I like to browse the dinner and wine menu online to get a feel for what I may enjoy later that evening. The food was good, no doubt, but all things must be considered when giving a review - Value, Service, Decor/Comfort etc. The consensus of our party of 6 was that the appetizers far outshone the entrees. The specialty drinks were good but at half the cost of the liquor bottle, they should be phenomenal. The seating was very low, which became uncomfortable later in the evening as everyone started stretching their legs out into the middle of the seating area. The service was unobtrusive - no problem there - but any recommendation requests were always met with the most expensive option. I can forgive that, my taste is often bigger than my wallet. If you are looking for a nice dark place where you can impress your date with how much you are willing to spend, this is your place. By the look of the crowd in there on a Saturday night, those people are becoming few and far between.

Also, any mention of Phat Bites would be incomplete without discussing the unbelievable salad offerings. The Chinese Chicken Salad is, in a word, incredible, as is Pesto Bowtie. Another little tidbit for you : Phat Bites is a "sister" restaurant of Ellendale's, so there will often be hot offerings from the Ellendale's buffet available a la carte as well.

text: Le Castagna is a pretty nice Italian restaurant on Chestnut, near the corner of 20th. The decor is modern high class, and the food is yummy Italian. My friends and I went there for Center City Sips, and we had a nice time. The restaurant is very spacious, although I thought that the bar area was a bit too small. The bartender was a bit on the snobby side. It was hard to get her attention to get a drink, but the guy who brought us our appetizers and cleared away our plates was really nice. The wine was very good, although the mojito I had was not very good. Too strong, and the mint was yellowing on the edges, so it wasn't that fresh. After the mojito, I stuck to red wine, which was very flavorful. The appetizer specials were good - flatbread pizza and bruschetta (2 artichoke, 2 mushroom, and 2 tomato pieces). I'd be interested in going here for dinner sometime. Because I was there for Center City Sips, I don't know how expensive their food normally is, but I think it's probably not terribly expensive, although probably slightly pricey.

text: I will agree here with the general consensus of the group. The atmosphere is nice and the place is cute but the food is disappointing. We stopped here for lunch on a Sunday afternoon and ate outside. The staff was very friendly and helpful going out of their way to find us an umbrella when the sun came out and made it uncomfortably hot. I ordered a special cocktail and it was tasty and well mixed if (unsurprisingly) over-priced. When the food came is when things went downhill. I had a burger which was completely uninteresting and bland, the roll was disproportionately large so that all I tasted was bread (and it wasn't great bread). My wife had a Chicken breast sandwich which suffered from what seems to be the Solaris' trademark, blandness. I can't recall what my brother in law had but he was also disappointed. The only person who enjoyed their meal was his fiancee who had a ceaser salad which we all tried and agreed was good. There was one other thing I thought notable. When they bring you bread, they brought a variety including corn bread and some chocolate muffins which were pretty good and a nice touch. All together however I would say this place is simply in need of a new chef to liven up their menu.

text: There are some theoretical positives. For one, the beer selection is extraordinary. It's had little care, or updating, and now just about any gourmet bottle one may drool over - Victories, Red Stripes, Dunckels, and Weizens, oh my! - is severely skunked. I asked for a Flying Fish bottle and was handed a warm glass with which to "Enjoy!" it. I tasted it and gagged. Upon a further bit of examination I found, believe it or not, a 16 month old expiration date. Think about it, a kid was born and has learned to babble, stumbled around, and chatter since this beer EXPIRED. So, I ordered another beer. How about a Red Stripe? A refreshing taste of the Caribbean in its own little grenade-shaped bottle. What's that? Expired in January 2008? Okay, fair enough. How about a soda? It's flat? Well, I give up. The funny thing is: THE WINE IS ALL NEW. Literally, no vintages (at least not that the waiter could tell me about) to enjoy. The menu was a disaster. On the back, printed cheaply in a home laser printer, was a list of the month's events. The management not only got the date of Mother's Day wrong, they got the DATE OF 'NOVA GRADUATION WRONG! This is the one weekend of the year that pretty much puts the local restaurant business in the black and they thought to themselves, "Well, it's close enough. Whatever. Maybe it's the same as last year? Should we double check? No, let's have a skunked Red Stripe." Service was slow. Though, can you blame them? If I worked there I'd be embarrassed at the pitiful investment of care by the ownership. I wouldn't WANT my visitors to see me either. Some food came out hot (soup) and some came out room temp (burger and fries). Apparently they haven't learned the diner rule of HOTFOODHOT! The place was nearly empty on a Friday night - obviously. It's days are numbered, the staff seem to be on life support, and the best we can hope for is that the ownership sells it to someone who'll give the venue the attention it deserves.
label: NEG

text: Our dinner was a heavenly, leisurely affair, lasting an amazing 4-5 hours[1], with no lulls in delivery. Philip, Ben, and Jean-Paul provided top-notch service in an unobtrusive manner. As soon as we finished a dish, they asked if we were done before taking our plates, and we never were rushed. I was impressed with the evening's little details, including an unexpected free gelato dessert (and a muffin to go) and a (much-appreciated) walk through their kitchen, with Ben as tour guide. A few other tables were there for Wednesday's wine dinner ($85; special), but we decided to order a la carte. The menu changed since I last saw it; besides the typeface design, there were overt Asian-influenced dishes. To start, we shared Kumamoto and P.E.I. oysters with caviar ($36). My entree, a Muscovy duck breast with rhubarb ($34) was perfect, along with the matching side, a leek casserole with spinach and croutons. The sommelier had paired a glass of wine for each course - the Riesling and Monbazillac were highlights - after all that, I was ready for a nap [2]. Lacroix is committed to excellence and their flawless execution in everything they do makes them worth visiting for any special occasion. (Don't have a special occasion? Make one up!) Highly recommended - tell them I sent you, and ask for Phillip. [1] It'll rain BEER before I'm disappointed there. We were the roughly the first to arrive, and almost the last to leave. [2] Suites at the Rittenhouse range from $700 to $3000 a night.

So, expect to pony up some bucks if you want to catch a quick one before you start to fly. The eatery area in between A-B-C is a nice spot to hangout. There are tons of decent food options that are not all corporate and fast food. Since I travel fairly often, I look forward to my trips in and out of BNA. I was impressed by the "beer bible" listing all the unusual offerings and the history and ingredients of brewing. Service was friendly and sincere, if a little scattered. Given how loud and crowded it was, I give them a free pass. I'd definitely like to come back!

text: Having been repeatedly disappointed by this restaurant over the years, I thought about giving it yet another chance. Well, nothing has changed: hard grease ladened room temperature garlic rolls that were rationed out by the disinterested wait staff (my teenage sons repeatedly and politely asked for more after receiving their two initial rolls without success), room temperature salad with too little dressing, warm wine glasses with the taste of detergent still lingering on the glass, and the still present overly salted, cooked, and oiled pasta that I hoped had been remedied. This is an essentially tourist ridden restaurant with poor food that tries to compensate by providing very large family style portions to patrons that have forgotten what real Italian food tastes like. Unfortunately, the formula doesn't work especially as the prices have crept up to an astronomical $25 per large pasta plate!!!!! Save your health and try many of the other downtown Italian eating establishments: The Chase, Ca' Dario, even Bucatinni. My biggest question is how long will unknowing out of towners wait in line for this food??? I am never going back.

That good egg on Broadway is a bad egg. The management should not allow such eggs to be used. They appeared to be unhealthy. Let's hope management cares a bit more in future.

text: As soon as I got home from dinner at The Fountain I went straight to my kitchen to make a sandwich, because I was starving. The portions here are minuscule. I had the Pick Two with the potato/pickle soup and half an egg salad sandwich. I think it cost $7.99 but was more like $4-5 worth of food. The soup was very tasty but came in a tiny bowl (less than 1 Cup) and my sandwich should have had twice the amount of egg salad filling. The other diners in my group felt the same way: too-small portions for the prices. One of my fellow diners had a salad that was too heavy on the onions with very wilted and "rusty" lettuce. For dessert I got the "world's smallest sundae", which was totally pointless: literally 1 spoonful of sundae for something like $1.99. You might as well just splurge for the regular-sized dessert items. I do not recommend this spot for large groups. As I have unfortunately encountered with many establishments in STL, the place has the seating space and tables to accommodate large groups, but the kitchen cannot properly handle so many orders coming in at one time. In our group of 12, two of us didn't receive our meals until most of the people in our party were finishing their food. I think the kitchen misplaced or lost our orders and our waiter had to put in new orders for us. When we first sat down our orders were taken promptly, but after receiving our food our waiter seemed to forget about us. We had to flag him down to get our check, and he told us they were so busy we should go up to the counter to pay. It was confusing. I don't think it was our waiter's fault, he seemed pretty stressed and running around very busy, having to make drinks as well as wait tables. I got the impression that he was doing the bulk of the work in the restaurant while some other staff were not pulling their weight. The decor is impressive - I am a big fan of Art Deco - but decor alone does not make a good restaurant. I would be willing to return here just for drinks or dessert and preferably sit at the bar, but I know not to expect much.

So the woman on the phone says, "Oh I'm so sorry! What's your name? I'll credit you a...." Wait for it... wait for it... "I'll credit you a TOPPING." Wow. A topping? I have a pizza that tastes nothing like what I wanted it to that was 20 dollars and you'll give me some free tomatoes next time? I will tell you that in this area, there is a Dewey's Pizza, a Pi, La Pizza, Katie's Pizzeria, and even an Imo's. text: Elmwood Fitness at Heritage Plaza is small, but has an ample selection of elliptical machines, treadmills, stair climbers, and a few bikes and other machines. I enjoy using the weight equipment upstairs and the elliptical machines (each with its own television!). This club offers a variety of classes including Bodypump, Bodyflow, yoga and Zumba, as well as spinning. There is a tiny lap pool (which also hosts water aerobics classes). The locker rooms and facilities are adequate. There are personal trainers and a massage therapist on staff. This club offers childcare during the day. There are also classes and social activities (such as coffee & doughnuts) for seniors. Because the gym is small, it often seems crowded. I am usually able to get on a cardio machine without waiting, however, with the possible exception of the first few Mondays after the New Year or Mardi Gras. If you are primarily a member of this club, you may use the Elmwood in Harahan on the weekends. This is a great benefit- the Harahan location is much larger and nicer, and has an outdoor pool. The only day you would "have" to use the other gym is Sunday, as Elmwood at Heritage Plaza is open on Saturdays.

text: I visited the Gaylord Opryland hotel/resort/conglomerate a few weeks ago when I was visiting Nashville with my boyfriend. We stopped by to see the hotel, but didn't stay there as guests. (If you're flying in for a weekend, I really recommend renting a car- I have no idea how we would have gotten around otherwise.) Parking was outrageously expensive so we parked in some shopping center across the street and walked in. It was maybe a 10 minute walk, but you're mostly walking through nicely manicured Opryland foliage so it's a nice walk. The hotel was a sight to behold- HUGE glass ceilings, indoor river, many, many restaurants inside which had an "outdoor" feel because of the massive atrium. We took a boat ride given by "Delta River Boat Tours" which was a cute little boat on a track in their indoor river with a sweet southern tour guide letting us in on all the "fascinating" facts about the hotel. She told everything as if it was the most amazing fact that had ever left her lips: "Here we have the original interior wall of the hotel... it was built in NINETEEN SEVENTY SEVEN!" (So old!) or, our favorite, "Here in the hotel we have an INDOOR SWIMMING POOL, so that you can swim ALL YEAR ROUND" (You mean, INSIDE the building? Impossible!) Anyway, it was hilarious. Seems like a nice place just to see/have a drink/ maybe dinner if prices aren't insane. Extra star for our tour guide who we still laugh about.

text: I decided to check out the witch on a Tuesday night as they advertise 4 courses for $20! Can't beat that right? The menu was the chefs special tasting. Some stuff was on the menu, some wasn't... but it was all fabulous! We walked in and we were instantly surprised by how big the place is. We got a great table and we were instantly given menus and we were told that a bottle of wine was only an additional $20! Serve it up! It was actually pretty good wine too. To the people who complained about the decor- I thought the place felt very upscale. I didn't notice anything particularly witch-like about it. There were no pictures on the walls. I think they must have been between artists. They must allow local artists to display their art and sell it. I find that a very cool touch. We Course 1- I ordered the beet salad. When it came out, I was shocked! It was 4-5 slices of beets, and a similar sized piece of goat cheese. It was delicious though. The onyl thing that would have made it better was if there was more of it! What I was forgetting was that I still had 3 courses to go! Course 2- I ordered the risotto. What came out was kind of a surprise... a golf ball sized friend ball of risotto on top of a curried tasting sauce. Again- I was shocked by how small it was... but again... 2 courses to go. Overall- this dish was excellent. I enjoyed it a lot! Course 3- I ordered the stuffed tomato. It came out on top of a bed of wild rice. Everything was cooked perfectly. Its rare to get a stuffed tomato that isn't mush. This was soft, but not stewed. It was filled with zucchini and it had a sharp cheese melted on top. This was delicious as well. Course 4- I had the banana cake which was great! Not too much detail. Just a perfect piece of banana cake with a blueberry sauce. All in all, I would defintily come back here! The service was great, the food was fresh and tasty, and the atmosphere was excellent. There are plenty of nicer places in the city, but for its location, and the price... I was really pleased!

text: Outstanding. Go there. Period. 5-stars is rare for me... you have to earn it. I'm a foodie and Amada may be one of the best restaurants that I have been to. Out of all of our meals from a week in NYC, Philly and DC this was the best (almost tied with Peasant in NYC) and any return to Philadelphia would have to include this one. I have great memories of this restaurant despite the fact that I was getting a fever in the process. The tapas of goat cheese and basalmic-marinated strawberries was refreshing. The garlic shrimp was very good, not great. The one tapas we almost didn't order of seasonal mushrooms from the grill was outstanding in it's simplicity (olive oil and lemon) and was devoured. We ordered too much food which did include the Valencia Pallea - which is the best (and authentic?) rendition of that dish we've ever had. The steak Frittes is a strip steak with fries. I ordered it medium rare. While it was more medium than medium rare, it was great. It was juicy and flavorful. I don't know what the dressing was, but wow, was it good. Our server was friendly and attentive. text: Let me first say, to be fair, I HATE chocolate (that's right), so from the get-go, I knew this was probably going to be a bleh time for me. Everyone I know is all about the dessert here. I would rather eat ice cream, cake, or cookies than a meal any day, but a pot of chocolate just isn't for me. Can't they have one different thing? text: My husband & I went here this weekend for our one year anniversary dinner - and had a great time! We came an hour early and sat in the bar. First of all, the atmosphere was just so cool. The bartenders were exceptional. And the Mademoiselle was deeelish! I'm a sucker for the elderflower liqueur. We tried the rose flight as well, and their special drink. We tried some cheese & olives that were good, and then we were on our way to the table. We had a white flight (contained Gewürztraminer - the others were very fruity, floral as well), and the bubbly flight. Yum! We tried the mushroom garden - stuffed morels, tempura beech clusters & shiitake, and the green tea cream put it completely over the edge!! I wanted a second of this!!! We had a soup flight of carrot-habanero, tom ka, and spring onion. Tom ka was by far the best! I suppose our server told the chef it was our anniversary, so we got a delicious small spoonful each of an effervescent tangerine-ish palate cleanser before dinner! I had the halibut & my husband had the duck. Both dishes were great, on the small side, but with everything else we had they were perfect portions. Then for dessert, our server brought us two glasses of bubbly on the house - we felt so special :) - along with our saffron ice cream dessert. There were several other confections on the plate but I was way-to-full to even go there. Loved the coffee in our own french press - coffee was wonderful. text: 5 stars?...Well I rate by the "It Is what it is" rule...and if you go to Gene's because it is what it is, you'll be getting genuine 5 star fulfillment. One of the more minor post Katrina tragedies was the closing of Verti Martes overnight shift. When I worked there a million years ago, they didn't even have a lock on the door (the day of the French Quarter bloackout, they left a semi-crazy cook in with a hatchet to deter the non-existent looters...but I digress). the lack of late night Verti Marte could crush a drunk Po' boy lovers soul...but there still is Genes. Genes is big and pink and filled with New Orleans, its another place not for the faint of heart...at 3 AM you'll be waiting with gangsters, musicians, surly cops and professional drunks of all shapes...but, yeah, they do all know something. If you rate a Po boy by how greasy it is...how easily the roast beef tries to slither out of the bread with every bite, Genes is the place. Crunchy french bread meets an incredible goopy mayo cheese lube that has the meat sliding all over the place...and at 3 AM, if you can keep it together or not, there is no better taste in town. Roast beef Philly is my choice, but they also have a great hot sausage, and video poker to boot...obviously you are feeling lucky; you stopped here, didn't you? If thats not enough, the next building over is Gene's daiquiri stand. Worth the short walk from the Quarter any hot afternoon. There's more booze in a large Genes daiquiri then in 5 on bourbon street; and that is before you pay the extra buck for an additional shot of some 190 proof firewater in there. With all the sugar It's like slurpy and crack cocktail, but without having to sell your mommas TV. Visitors to New Orleans, get out of the Quarter and into Gene's and your a step closer to understanding the town.

text: I have heard all the hype about Charlie's and have even ventured in a few times but it wasn't until recently that I bought my first pair of jeans there. This is exactly what occured after I told the sales woman that I was looking for a pair of skinny jeans. She handed me a pair of sevens. I looked at the pair she handed me, dreading the idea of coming out of the dressing room because they probably wont' fit but to my surprise, they fit like a glove, perfection! I was amazed! I tried on a few more pairs after but that pair was the one. I was even lucky enough to find a coupon online for 10% off which they honored. I recommend Charlie's to anyone who is willing to invest in a good pair of jeans. They may be pricy but after years of trying brand after brand in search of the pefect fit, I can say I will go no where else but Charlie's now! Getting a few good pairs of jeans that are pricy but fit well is a far better investment than spending tons of money on cheaper jeans that don't fit and flatter!
label: POS

text: Home Depot used to be a quality store. But that was years ago. Now this store is dark, the aisles are cluttered with pallets of products. The employees all walk around like unhelpful drones, all wearing their grimy, unwashed aprons. It is really a pathetic excuse for a business. This location in particular will most likely be run out of business very soon since Wal-Mart and Petco left the plaza. The whole strip is mostly empty, and the fact that Home Depot has turned into junk will not help them survive in this economy. I don't know what the higher-ups at H.D. are thinking, but they obviously aren't thinking of running a quality competitor for Lowe's or even Ace - where the oldsters shop.

text: Man...it's a damn shame I'm not a guy who can pull off cowboy boots. Visiting this place makes me want to buy a turquoise pair of snakeskins and trot around like a real live cowboy. Too bad I'm not that cool. I don't frequent boot shops, so I don't know if the prices here are typical or not. I can tell you, however, that I didn't see a single pair of boots for less than $150. Most authentic-looking cowboy boots run somewhere around $300, but the sales lady told me every pair in the store was buy-one-get-two-free. Sounds like a pretty good deal to me. Boot Country also has a pretty large selection of rodeo and Western style shirts. Most of them were about $50, but everything on the men's rack was 50% off. The staff was very friendly and helpful, and they don't seem to mind letting crazy tourists try on their merchandise and pretend to be Roy Rogers. As you can probably tell, I'm not really the cowboy type. This store kind of makes me wish I was, however. The whole place smells like leather, and their boots range from rough-looking shit-kickers to nice and polished boots you could wear to a funeral...if you're an old oil magnate or the owner of the Dallas Cowboys. Pretty cool spot to look around even if you can't swing one of their fancy pairs of kicks.

text: My fiancée and I visited this restaurant on Saturday night and were very disappointed. Major complaints: 1) Temperature - It was freezing cold. We had to put on our jackets. Also the bathrooms are not heated at all. So if you have to go, hold it. The server knew it was chilly and said it would warm up. It didn't. I had to retrieve our coats b/c it was too cold. 2) Food was bland. We ordered the Bouillabaisse and the Salmon. Both had good/decent quality ingredients but the preparation was terrible. Both lacked flavor. The Rouille sauce for the Bouillabaisse had little if any flavor. The Salmon hadn't been seasoned at all and was overcooked. The menu selection was good as it had a wide range of prices for meals so you could spend $12-15 for an entree or $25 for an entree. 3) Wine - The selection was ok. But for a place that was suppose to be a wine bar it had a pretty small selection. My fiancee's wine was pretty good. However, I had a cabernet that had been opened some time ago. It lacked the sharpness of wine that was opened recently. It was flat. The service was good. Our waiter was very nice and the food came out quickly. The decor is not very winebar-ish which is actually good for me. It feels more like a sports bar and has no pretentiousness. I think that is a great feature of the place. I wish them well, I hope they can turn it around but at this time I could not recommend for anyone to try it out.

No diagnosis, just given a 'script for some pain pills and referred to an OB/GYN. Now almost 4 years later I have been diagnosed with problems with my large intestine. From what I know now I had a raging infection, and it basically went untreated because of their inability to rule out even something rare for someone my age. Good catch there NNMC, not. NNMC would be a last resort for me based on that. I'd rather go to Renown and not have my insurance cover it than risk more negligence.

text: Vegetarians should run, not walk to this restaurant. Even if you aren't a veg, you should jump at the chance to eat here. The dishes are hearty, flavorful and creative. Each of the vegetables were perfectly cooked and the tofu well-seasoned. I had the steak and potatoes. While the seitan steak reminded me of a pork chop in flavor and texture, it was still amazingly prepared. The Yukon potatoes was actually smashed (not mashed), which was fine. The grilled asparagus, carrots and peppers were sublime. We were to full for dessert but we got the lemon cake to go. This was one of the best veg places I've eaten at in a long time.
