text: Good service is nice, poor service is endurable, and no service is... wait, no service? What kind of dismally incompetent restaurant falls into that category? You can probably name a few, but here's another one for your list: Char's Thai. The restaurant was less than half empty when we arrived for dinner but, after fifteen minutes of quality time with our menus, we still had to intercept a waitress and ask to order. Twenty-five minutes later our fried tofu appetizer made a memorable appearance--not memorable on account of flavor, which it lacked, but because it proved that they actually had a kitchen. I lost a few dollars on that bet. Our entrees showed up ten minutes later with a half-hearted apology: apparently the kitchen was "busy." Maybe they growing our food, or reading War and Peace, or learning the dulcimer, but they sure weren't hurrying. In all fairness, the yellow curry with chicken was tasty and compared favorably to other Thai restaurants in Tucson. The pad see ew had a good, deep flavor, though it came with regular broccoli instead of gai lan and was heavily peppered with carbon flakes from a dirty wok. Predictably, we had to scavenge the empty tables for sriracha. Char's Thai might be worth a visit if you live nearby and have a long life ahead of you. Otherwise, skip it.
label: NEG

The only thing that kept them from 5 stars was that I found them expensive compared to other pizza places. However, they worth it. GREAT PIZZA!!!!!!!!

text: First of all, I like Starbucks. It is consistently decent coffee, no matter where you are in the world. I've had it in the bowels of southern Virginia, I've had it in the bizarre no-man's-lands of Austria, it's always the same, and it's always just fine. So you'll get no Starsucks hatery from me. That said, I have never, ever, anywhere in the world, encountered a Starbucks as shitty as this. They are incompetent and they are slow. You can stand there witha line out the door, and watch the 5 baristas behind the bar talking, looking confused, trying to get other people to do their stuff, and generally displaying zero ability to multitask. They never have two baristas on the machines, and I've rarely seen any barista make two drinks at a time. For perspective, my brother is a Starbucks barista, and he regularly has 4-5 drinks going at a time. Why? Because he's competent, and he knows how to get some speed on it. Just today, at a slow point with only one person ahead of me and two behind me, I went to get an Americano. I stood in line waiting for the cashier to finish talking to the man in front of me about parking spots, while literally holding his change in her hand and just talking to him, for minutes. When she finished, she turned around and recounted some of it to the barista behind her, ignoring the line, for another full minute. Once she finally turned around and I got to order, pay, and stand at the bar waiting for my drink, I was treated to the stoned-looking barista strolling around working on the latte of the guy ahead of me, getting it just right, joking with him, and getting him some ice water, all while my cup sat empty. It's nice that she engaged him, but anyone with a clue and some hustle would have had the espresso brewing into that cup while they were doing all the rest. I was a bartender and a barista, and the appalling slowness of all of these people would have gotten me fired from ANYwhere. As a result, I now go to the Starbucks at 19th and Chestnut. They are speedy and competent there, and when I joke about the 18th and Market one, they laugh knowingly and tell me how often they hear that. It's not just me. Avoid this branch, go another block to 19th and Chestnut and patronize good service.

text: Emilio's is a pretty little place right across from the harbor. We were a a bit early so were asked to wait at the bar. I ordered a drink from the creative cocktail menu and was served an amazing huckleberry martini from the unfriendly bartender. Our table was ready after I had a few sips of my drink. Unfortunately, one of my pet peeves came up: the host asked us to pay our bar tab and then he would show us to the table. Why can't you just add the drinks to the food tab? ....and please place my drink on a tray and bring it to my table - don't make me carry it. Menu was beautifully presented with first courses $10, pasta/pizza for $15, and main courses $20. I did like the pricing idea; very straight forward. I had the ahi tuna cones for my first course, which unfortunately were very boring. The tuna was just barely marinated with soy and piled into a sesame cone that was so sweet it tasted like candy. I ended up pulling the tuna out of the cones and that was much better, especially since the portion was very generous. My hon of hons husband fared much better with the goat cheese fondue served with grilled brushetta and an arugula salad. The goat cheese was melted in a smoky tomato sauce and we mopped up every bit of that sauce. For my main course I had the pasta with fruits de mer, which again was disappointing. There were plenty of mussels and clams, but I do not like having clams with broken shells in my bowl. The sauce was good, but I was really put off by the broken shells and couldn't eat too much. HOH fared much better, AGAIN. He had the 6 hour cooked pork, which was just delicious, served with butter beans and porcini mushrooms. Service was just OK and would've been better if they had another food runner or waiter. Too bad my excitement about seeing the well crafted menu was not fulfilled by the overall experience. 2.5 stars.

text: I stayed at the Ambassador hotel while I was in New Orleans for a convention. I'll admit, I had little to do with the booking of it, so I can't say much about how the place advertises itself. And I can't complain too much, since I didn't do any research to find anything better. That being said; if this place bills itself as anything other than "rustic", then they're lying. Sure, the place looks pretty nice from the outside. It has the classic feel that fits in pretty well with the rest of the area. The bar/restaurant that is open to the street looks like it would be a nice place for a drink. Even the lobby, while certainly worn-looking, isn't as scary as it could be. The rooms are an entirely different story. See, apparently we reserved the Cave Room. It was located in the middle of the second floor, therefore we had no windows. Okay, that's not entirely true, there are windows in the wall, but they open on to the hall outside. The two lights that were present in the far corners of the room may have combined to about 7 watts. And not that we reserved a suite, but the simple layout of the room gave very little space for movement or anything much if you weren't sitting on the beds. Hot water was in short supply, but it's not like you would want to stay in the bathroom for too long. It looked like someone tried to kick through the adjacent wall into our shower stall. I should have gone next door and told them it wasn't any better over here. Give this one a pass, there are a number of significantly better options in the area for comparable prices. If you have to go here, make sure you at least get a room that has a window that faces the outside world (not the hallway).

text: The far Northeast is blessed to have this gem to call its own. Why you ask? Well, simple - Taste King may follow the same old Chinese restaurant formula that most do: Large portions of flavorful food for low price but the big difference here is that Taste King has been doing so for well over 11 years. It has the details down to a science. The owner understand that his business and livelihood relies heavily on large parties brought in regularly by the large Soviet community local to the area and has learned that service, quality and serving size is vital to those patrons. Whats this mean to the average Yelp er? 4.5 Star prices for 4.5 Star Chinese food and service. So, whats the catch? Having to listen to the occasional group of fifty-year olds with horrendous Russian accents try to sing happy-birthday to a nephew or niece as the child shrinks into their seat wishing death not only upon him or herself but upon his or her entire lineage. So is it worth the auditory torment? I think so. Taste King is the only place i know of in the Northeast my better half and I can split a order of General Tao's Chicken, both have Hot and Sour soup plus get a complimentary plate of ice cream and end paying just over 20$. (tip and all) Note: The Restaurants highlights really are its seafood dish like its clams casino & seafood soup. I'd suggest trying both. O and if you later decide on booking a large party, keep in mind that this place will do more then just what's on the menu, just ask to speak with someone about it. The Chef has talent.

text: Santa Barbara Roasting Company, known as RoCo to locals and fans, is the only coffee shop in Santa Barbara I know of that roasts their own coffee beans as well as serves coffee. Most of the others ship it in from elsewhere, like Starbucks and Peet's. RoCo kicks their butts, even with the foo-foo drinks (you know, the more milk than coffee, with tons of flavorings)! The original location, where they roast, is in a little shopping center (State St and Guiterrez St) next to a Time Bike shop and an art gallery, with a great bakery (D'Angelo's) around the corner. The coffee, people, atmosphere and charm of the original location can't be beat. The Paseo Nuevo location serves great coffee, but lacks the space and charm, but what can you expect for being in the middle of an upscale shopping mall? Besides coffee, espresso, and hot and cold coffee-based drinks, RoCo also serve a variety of pastries from a local bakery which are really good. They offer free Wi-Fi Internet, which can be a little poky at time, but hey, it's free, so no complaints. Honestly, the only place I've ever had better coffee than RoCo's is at Barefoot Roasters in Santa Clara. But RoCo is more fun, funky, and has a way cool logo, so I still consider it my favorite coffee shop of all time. Coffee lovers, tourists, beach bums, and college students all converge at RoCo in harmony. Join them and see why I miss it so now that I moved back to Silicon Valley.

text: Disappointing. I was excited for this meal as I hadn't had good italian in a while, and in particular to try their tiramisu. The food was "ok", but I've had much, much better at half the price. We were there early on a Wednesday night (around 6pm or so), and other than the patrons in the bar we were either the first or second diners to arrive. We had the Veal Parm, a chicken dish that I don't remember the name of but with a white wine based sauce, and a bowtie pasta with salmon dish. The veal parm was over salted, yet the chicken and salmon dishes were virtually unseasoned and tasteless. I'd like to chalk this up to the cook but it was Tony himself in the kitchen so I have to assume this is representative of the food. The odd thing, is that the basic pasta sides that came with our dishes were very good (much better than the entree's). The meat sauce on one was a good representation, and the 'butter and garlic' sauce on the other was phenomenal....however it clearly was a clam stock base, and not simply a butter and garlic sauce. Not that I minded, it was great if you like a clam sauce, perhaps one of the best I've had. Only bright spot would be the mussels they had as a appetizer special that night. Who knows, maybe they got some of the broth from the appetizer in the garlic and butter sauce. The biggest letdown however was the Tiramisu. From what I've read they are supposed to have one of the best in St. Louis. This is my favorite dessert on the planet, and I'm a pretty good judge of quality Tiramisu if I do say so myself. And frankly it's one of the reasons I went in the first place. The mascarpone is virtually missing (cost cutting?) so you end up with what tastes like Cool Whip as they've obviously whipped sugar into the egg whites instead of just using the mascarpone to sweeten it, and there's no discernible alcohol whatsoever (Marsala or otherwise). I really wanted to like this place, mainly because it's difficult in my opinion to find a decent place on The Hill that is relatively casual and that I can take my whole family. But alas poor Yorick, tis not to be.

Not so much. Well, though I don't know who else was eating there (nor do I really care), all that matters is they had a solid burger with equally tasty fries. I got the burger without the injected cheese that smells like the feet of someone averse to washing them for months on end. I also passed on the tomato given that I preferred my burger sans salmonella. The caramelized onions were great and the patty was just right for me cooked medium. text: Formerly known as Red's (what's with the similar name?), Ed's Rec Room offers something for everyone. Located near the Jubilations Dinner Theatre on the second level of West Ed, the rec centre houses a family bowling alley, as well as a restaurant, lounge, arcade and billiards. It's mainly the bowling I come for, even though I'm not much of a bowler. But it's one of those things that are always fun, even if you really suck at it like me. Tuesday nights are cheap bowling nights at Ed's, what they call Toonie Tuesdays (like at KFC, only with bowling balls), and it's half the weekend rate. Monday nights are all-you-can-bowl nights, when you can pay a slightly higher flat rate and bowl til your arms scream no more. My favorite nights though, are the cosmic bowling nights (Monday, Friday, and Saturday nights), when they dim the lights and have the disco balls spinning, and everything is glowing in the dark. It's really cool! I don't think you're able to reserve a lane, especially on weekend nights, but you can try. It would certainly be helpful, since they're usually busy. The service is okay, they help you with the basics, but if you ask more from them, they might get a little snappy. The last time I went, the guy was pretty sarcastic with us because there were so many people demanding his attention. If bowling's not your thing, there's always the lounge and arcade or billiards. I haven't tried any of these other activities Ed's offers, as I'm pretty happy with my bowling. But maybe I'll try the restaurant one of these days, just to see what it's like.

text: Once you get past the obstacle course that is finding this place, you'll really enjoy time spent at Yazoo's tap room. While it gets crowded, you can usually find a seat in the room adjacent to the tap room, or out in the courtyard. As for ordering, get the sampler ($6 for 5 tastings) and pair it with the cheese platter. Yum. While, I'm not a big fan of all their beers, I do love trying them in rapid succession. The only problem is that they don't have any means of identifying which beers are which once they've poured them (most places use a place mat with writing on it). So, it can be hard to remember what's what. Also, be sure to get a growler - it's a relatively cheap way to enjoy a good amount of beer...I would suggest their hefeweizen or the dos perros.

I always thought this place was a missed opportunity. To have a great restaurant in the park would be novel and a destination dining experience. text: I walked by Mace's on the way to the Franklin Institute and immediately loved the look of it. I said "wow, doesn't that place look cool? If we have time I want to stop in there." Obviously not consulting Yelp was a mistake. From the looks of it, I was expecting more of a gastro-pub, and was startled to see such low prices. The highest priced item on the menu is $10.50! We walk in and it feels like a cozy irish bar with a small downstairs area with a few booths and a couple TVs, and then an upstairs area. I was excited, until I saw the very small and average beer list. I opted for a Yuengling, one of the two most exotic brews they had. Also ordered some fish 'n chips, hoping the food would outdo the beer selection. The food came out and it looked not unlike something you'd find at McDonald's.. My "chips" were crinkle cut fries that probably came out of a big Ore Ida freezer bag, and the fish had that bizarre, tell-tale processed trapezoidal shape that you'd expect from Long John Silvers. Michelle's "grilled chicken sandwich" was almost indistinguishable as a grilled chicken sandwich. It was all white and gooey and had a couple tiny chunks on it. It kinda looked like a patty of tartar sauce. I appreciated the friendliness of our waitress, but the limited beer selection, and poor food was a turn-off. text: So soon after my first review, I really feel the need to revisit this. But I want to be very clear about the topics I'm addressing. Mongolian BBQ - 4 Heat Lamp buffet - 2 Standard menu - 3 Chinese menu - 4 Bar/Happy Hour - turning that bad boy all the way to 11!!!! Happy Hour is M-F, 4-7 pm. The special is half price appetizers. No deals on the drinks, but they are roughly $7.50 per serving, which is a good price. The Zombie came in a cool Fu Manchu mug. The Chi Chi came in frozen coconut mugs, that were still cold nearly an hour later. The Scorpion Bowl aka Parents Liquor Cabinet (costs $15, serves 2+) comes AFLAME, and with crazy long straws. Mai Tai was big and delicious. King Kong Bundy (sp?) was dangerous. I don't believe there is any other bar in town that serves up these tiki-style cocktails with the kitsch style. With my little group, we were able to sample nearly every appetizer on the menu. I'll go through the whole list. * Chinese Chicken Salad - did not try * Fried Wontons (10 pork, or 8 cream cheese) - ordered both. Simple, fun to share, lots of dipping sauce provided. * Egg Rolls (4) - appeared vegetarian. Standard. Let these cool down before eating. * Paper Wrapped Chicken (4) - actually foiled wrapped. Stuck to foil. Meh. * Fried Shrimp (4) - good. * Bar-B-Q Spareribs (4) - yummy and filling. * Bar-B-Q Pork - did not try * Fried Dumplings {Pot Stickers} (6) - SKIP! But filling. * Sa-Tay Beef Sticks (6) - winner. * Chinese Country Style Chicken Wings (6) - good! * Assorted Appetizer {2 pieces each of: Egg Roll, Paper Wrapped Chicken, BBQ Sparerib, and Beef Stick} (8) - winner! Came in a kitschy platter with a mini hibachi flame to heat things up. * Fried Shrimp Balls (4) - has potential. Some of ours were too salty. * Salt & Pepper Sauteed Mushrooms - yummy! Great to share. * Bon Bon Ji Chicken - WINNER! Shredded chicken in a citrus peanut sauce with greens. Can take a while to prepare, and worth the wait. * Swa-Ni Pork - WINNER! Thin-sliced pork in spicy garlic sauce. Now, don't expect the party to fall in your lap. You need to bring your own. Ming Dynasty is not the place of beautiful people, unless it's Goleta's own special brand of beautiful people, which is folks in costco clothing and a mullet or two. And that's part of its charms. Also, the bar only has two scorpion bowls, so you gotta share and play nice with others. We had a blast. LOVED the happy hours. We will be back.

text: Snack Bar is a place I've been wanting to check out since it first opened, however I never had the opportunity until recent. We were able to get sitting in the out cove of the restaurant (when you go, I advise you to make reservations-we lucked out!) and our server was quick to get us started with drinks and always keeping an eye on how our table as doing.Our friend ordered the calamari-it was delicious! I must say all of our meals where so tasty-the portions weren't small (however I also tend to not like big plates of food, so the portions were perfect for me) and the dessert (I had the chocolate mousse with my partner, our guest had the cheesecake) was exactly what we needed to cap off the night. The meals did not leave any of us feeling "too" full and the mood of the night was perfect. Great conversation, great food, great service-I feel like it can't get much better than this. Pros: -quick service -friendly staff -delicious food and perfect portions -key location for tourists or out of town guests who'd like to see Rittenhouse area. Cons: -small restaurant (note: I like this about the place, but I could see how people might not like that all) -portions may be too small for some, depends on if you're need that feeling of being "stuffed" which I prefer to avoid -street parking is cheapest, but I'm sure there is an expensive garage in the area (expensive...geez, the parking garages here are definitely not as bad as NYC! ha) Overall, I'm giving the restaurant 4 stars. If it were BYOB it'd be 5, but I like that there's a menu that's not overwhelming, you can still hear your guests over the crowded room and you'll leave with a smile.

text: I have eaten here 3-4 times, and today I met a friend for lunch. Much as I love good seafood and wish this place was delicious, it has mostly disappointed every time. THE PROS Their New England Clam chowder is good, I'll give them that. And they have nice fresh chewy rolls , good salad and coleslaw and decent strong coffee served in a nice big cup. I did have broiled scallops there once there were reasonably yummy. THE CONS Today we had two sandwich items: The Lobster Roll ($22+ market price) sandwich was dreadfully disappointing, not at all like the fresh sweet New England lobster roll my mouth was watering for - the lobster was a bit fishy tasting, a bit chewy and not well seasoned. The Tuna sandwich was not good either, it was ground tuna and cooked to a well done, well breadcrumb- filled borderline dryness with a spiciness that was just sort of - there-, just - hot-, not a lovely, complex compliment to moist juicy tuna like we hoped for. The fries were over cooked, the coleslaw good. I've also had the "fish and chips" for dinner, both the fried fish and french fries were so dried out one could practically crumble them into dusty crumbs and blow them away. I had the same thought the last time we ate there as I had today. Whoever is cooking must either be young or just fairly unsophisticated in that they haven't reached that point yet where they realize that killing the food by overcooking it really does make a difference to taste and texture, Our waitress was personable and excellent and we gave her the money to pay our bill when she brought us coffee with a generous nearly 25% tip. When we flagged her down to ask for more water and a little more coffee about 20 minutes later she brought it without looking at us or saying a word, I guess once the tip is received it's "game over" and the charm gets turned off. By the time you order a drink, a soup, an iced tea (for $3.50), entrée and dessert you can spend a fortune and the food is very hit and miss and often badly cooked. So if you plan to eat here, I'd say you're safe with the scallops, the clam chowder and maybe some kind of salad. In my opinion this place is not worth the money and today was my last visit.

text: Oh Satsuma. I like you. Ugh), Satsuma is my favorite place as of now to chill out, have a salad, drink some tea, and plan for a week of kindergarten lessons. The decor is seriously incredible and super random, very New Orleans--mismatched chairs and tables, a tiny garden and patio, a carousel unicorn, local art hanging on the walls (it acts as a gallery as I'm seeing pieces get sold all the time), and dirty fancy hipsters making your sandwiches and coffee. Even the bathroom is pretty, with frames and an old nursery diaper things holder (I don't have kids so I don't know what you call that thing that sits next to a crib) housing cleaning supplies. Foodwise! Pretty standard, pretty good, pretty affordable. I usually stick with tea (yerba matte, they don't have too many herbal options sadly), but I've had their beet salad (mixed greens, sprouts grown outside that still had dirt on it, gold and red, chevre and tasty vinaigrette, pine nuts!) and tried their veggie sandwich. They were very vegan conscious for my homegirl when she asked for no cheese, informing her that the sauce had dairy and they could replace with a vegan pesto. What more can I say? text: If you're looking to do some secret cupcake browsing in Philadelphia, Philly Cupcake is not for you. Upon entering, you will realize that your every action, word, and quite possibly thought will be observed by the staff, because this place is tiiiiiiny. Nonetheless, you will also be amazed at how friendly and attractive the staff are (is? are?). They will go out of their ways to ensure that "this isnt your first time being here," and to assist you in choosing an item for yourself and/or your dog. Since dogs eat cupcakes, yes they do indeed. The aroma of this taste smells like they bottled the personal scent of Willy Wonka and sprayed it into the ventilation system. It's overwhelmingly delicious smelling, enhanced yet by the small size of the place. It's also rather visually appealing inside, if somewhat emasculating for a man to enter by himself, which I have done on a number of occasions. The cupcakes look beautiful. Almost too beautiful--it pains me a little to have to personally destroy each one that I buy. But this is the inevitable tragedy of the life of a cupcake. I admit that I am something of a n00b when it comes to gourmet cupcakes. Cupcakes to me have always been the ones that people brought to kids' birthday parties or homeroom in 7th grade. The ones, hopefully, with funfetti. But these cupcakes are definitely delicious. I've had four kinds so far, but I'm not going to go into the details of the cupcakes because that would be boring, at least to me. I will say something about the pricing, which is pretty much the only reason that this place didn't get 5 stars. They have "regular" cupcakes for $3 and "fancy" cupcakes for $4. Like I said, I admit my amateur-ness in the world of gourmet cupcakes, but that seems a little pricey to me. They also have other sweets like cookies and brownies, but really, this place is called Philly Cupcake, not Philly Brownie, so make the right decision. And, for real, they actually do have cupcakes for dogs, which seems pretty silly to me but I do love dogs so respect for being dog-friendly. I did not, however, try the dog cupcakes, so I can't comment on whether they are delicious or not. All in all, definitely worth a try, at least once. They are not the best cupcakes I've ever eaten--that title belongs to my friend Jennie's cupcakes, but they are probably the second best cupcakes I've ever eaten.

text: A couple weeks ago, we tried Taco Mamacita. As native Southern Californians, we appreciate good Mexican food - even good Tex-Mex food. This was just average. You pay for the decor. However, you can eat at the bar. Can't lie, prices are o.k. and so is the food. I wanted to love the fish taco and I wanted to like the Oy vey, the brisket taco, but neither was anything special. My Other Half chose the roasted Peruvian chicken. While tasty, the poor little chicken was missy breasts. I'd like to see this bird fly... Honestly, if we went back, I'd go for the guacamole and chips (chips and salsa you pay for - $2.50). AND, the margaritas. Really good. Although, my Other Half was a tad miffed. They didn't carry a Mexican beer. They said they were waiting to get approved to start serving it. Whatever. How do you open a Mexican restaurant and don't have a Mexican beer on tap? One more note - the crowd tends to skew to the 20-something crowd. Not too many families. Not too many old folks, however it does accommodate large groups. So, it's loud. The decor is funky, a mix of repurposed doors and tin with high ceilings and lots of natural light. Now, If only the food was better. Or, at least interesting.

For drinks I got a beer and she got one of the cocktails off of the list, which was pretty good but I don't remember the name. Something with gin is all I know. We got our food and after taking a bite realized that it was luke warm. We gave everything back to the server who said that it might come back hotter than we would want, and I replied that at least it would be hotter than it is now. During this time we ate our sides which were good. The collared greens and potato salad were gone fast, but the mac and cheese was a little bit off. It tasted gritty. It seemed that one of the cheeses they used did not melt and created little sand like grains. We got our food back and began to eat. First off, the ribs. I understand that they are supposed to be smoked but the dry rub they put on it was overpowering. It tasted very peppery. The bbq sauce they gave us to put on the ribs was very spicy. I love spicy but it would be good to have another sauce that was sweet so a person could have two choices. Also the meat was very dry. The sausage was bleh. It tasted like they had just put ground beef into a casing and served it. There was a lack of flavor and like the ribs, the meat was very dry. The place just opened so I think we'll be back in a few months to see if anything changes but for right now I am staying away.

text: I have to qualify this review by saying that I REALLY wanted to give Clubhouse Inn & Suites four stars. Unfortunately there was one problem that dropped the rating to two stars. Stayed here during a recent work trip to St. Louis. Although it was a work expense, I was still on a budget. Since I am familiar with St. Louis, I was aware it would be about a half hour drive to downtown, and that was okay with me. The Clubhouse Inn & Suites was a huge value for the price. For $48/day (discount package deal with airfare from travelocity.com) I got a nice room with two queen-sized beds which seemed reasonably clean, free wireless internet, and free buffet breakfast each morning. The buffet breakfast was much more than I was expecting, including eggs, sausage, biscuits & gravy, cereal, milk, juice, coffee, fruit, bread/toast, danishes, and bagels. I'm probably forgetting something. There was even a waffle station with pre-measured batter in cups and a waffle iron. The food itself was mediocre, but the variety was impressive. The free wireless internet was great, until it stopped working the last two nights of my four night stay. Oh well. Check-in was easy, check-out was easy, and the folks at the front desk seemed quite nice. There were other amenities I did not use, such as the fitness room (it looked very basic), the outdoor pool (too cold in March!) and the indoor jacuzzi (well, I didn't bring a swimsuit, and I was too busy anyway). But the main reason I gave Clubhouse Inn & Suites a two star rating is that one night I got back to my room only to find that the housekeeping had not completely closed my door! My door was slightly ajar, and I opened it with just a gentle push, without needing my keycard. I believe it was a sloppy mistake by housekeeping. All of my belongings were where I had left them. But as a woman traveling alone who considers safety to be a HUGE priority, I was kind of freaked out, and I checked the room (closet, bathroom, tub) to make sure nobody was in the room waiting for me! Of course, nobody was and I was fine. Still, I just couldn't give them more than two stars.

text: One of the places that you REALLY must visit in Tucson. I'll start with the good first, since the good is really what makes this place shine and saves this place from getting a 3 or 4. The food is simply amazing. I dare you to find a place that has better wings than this place. There is just no way to explain how AMAZING the wings are. I mean, wow. I went to this place almost 2-3 times a month for 2 years once I found out about it. Unfortunately, I moved from Tucson, but I still fantasize about this place. The deep dish pizza is good, I'm not a huge fan and neither is my GF, but my mom LOVES it. She made me take her just for the pizza every time she came to Tucson. The thin crust pizza was amazing, I didn't think it would be and not many people try it, but damn, its GOOD. The salad is amazing as well, its simple, but amazing, some sun dried tomatoes, onions, olives, and green salad with that delectable ranch just makes me happy. Hot sticks or BBQ sticks or cheesy garlic sticks make an awesome addition. The wings. I already mentioned the wings, but I think it deserves it own section. Hot, is WAY hot, maybe 'hotter than your sister'. Unless you start coming here more often, you'll need to stick to medium for a bit. The BBQ is also very unique. Most wing places just use regular ass BBQ sauce and it stiffens up your wings, but the BBQ at rocco's is very saucy, and stays moist and keeps your wings warm. The medium and hot wings are a tad bit on the oily side, but man, are they amazing. I've gone to Native New Yorker (a bunch in Phoenix, and now one in Tucson), and none of those offer anything like Rocco's. I will spend my life trying to find hot wings like Rocco's. THE CHOCOLATE CHIP COOKIES. If they are there, consider yourself lucky, they go fast. Great way to calm the nerves after some firey wings. The service is bleh. The first few times we went there, we felt not welcomed. The service doesn't do the amazing food justice. One of the servers is not very friendly (male, black hair, looks completely lost all the time). I think its just the way he is, recently he's been cool. The other guys there are pretty funny and cool, and one of the girls is a pretty cool server. Rocco is just a baller. He's created wing heaven here, and while other places focus on variety, he focuses on quality. Tip - Wednesdays is wing night with $0.25 wings, but please, don't just get 50 dozen wings, and leave 47 dozens behind. The wings are amazing, but try a salad with the hot sticks too. Also, apparently if you order other stuff you get your food faster. Go early if you don't want to wait early, like around 4:45 pm. Or go after 8 pm. Anytime in between, and you're looking for a 45-60 minute wait. This is a small place, but its a hidden gem. Try it out on a Wednesday night if you're not sure about it. The pricing is great, I'd easily pay $0.50/wing for these awesome wings. Its a pretty clean place, and the outside seating is kinda nice. If you frequent this place, the staff will be friendly. The only reason I miss this city is this restaurant.
label: POS

text: Entirely substandard Punjabi food. Get thee to another Indian restaurant (Woodlands?), and quickly. This place manages to stay afloat by offering a cheap buffet within walking distance of Vanderbilt - anywhere else and they'd have folded long ago. Indian food in America has become synonymous with Punjabi food, and Cuisine of India doesn't even measure up to the standard American-Punjabi joint. The food is all a little too oily, and the spices are faded - the food doesn't all need to be spicy/hot, but the flavors should be vibrant and fresh. The saag paneer is limp and heavily creamed without much other flavor; the chicken tikka masala is greasy and colored far out of proportion to its flavor; and the chicken tandoori is poorly trimmed and has large pieces of fat remaining. The aloo mutter was bland, the channa masala was undercooked, and the gobi was tasteless and covered in spices which hadn't been properly toasted beforehand. The few times I've come for dinner and ventured into the rest of the menu, the results were similarly disastrous (and much more expensive). I live literally 100 yards from Cuisine of India and grew up eating Punjabi food at least once a week, but I've given this place several tries and refuse to suffer through any more meals there. Sadly, there aren't any Punjabi restaurants that I've been to in Nashville that are much better. Woodlands is at least a little more palatable, but their South Indian food isn't spectacular either. Honestly, if you're in the area and hungry you'd be better off across the walkway at Pizza Perfect.

With the help of the chef/owner, I ordered the L'hollendaise which has Gouda (can't go wrong with gouda), turkey and herbs. My friend got a vanilla crepe. The cheese was melted just right and blended really well with the warm turkey...I'm getting hungrier as I'm writing this review. The coffee was delicious and strong! It was so perfect with my crepe! text: As I continue my quest for Nashville's best BBQ, I come across Nashville's own Whitt's Barbecue. I've been to this particular location a few times and I often ask myself. "Why do I keep coming back?" Deep down I think it's because I really want to like this place. Or maybe I'm just a glutton for punishment. :) First off, there pulled pork has zero smoke flavor and zero flavor in general. It's plenty tender, but so is pork that you cook in crock pot. Don't get me wrong; I'm not suggesting they cook there meat in crock pot but I'm just saying. Today, i happened to be there for Rib Day (Friday) and I thought "Maybe this could be there defining moment" Boy was I wrong. These ribs were terrible. No flavor and very tough. And when I say tough, I mean almost "jerky" tough. Plus, there lack of sauce options really made it difficult for me to eat. And coming from a dude who loves to eat, it's saying a bunch. There sides are pretty weak too. They have potato salad, baked beans, mac n cheese, slaw, and chips. I mean come on, can a brother get a french fry? There loaded BBQ potato seemed to be the popular menu item, so it could be I'm just not eating the right thing. It sad, but I might have to give up on this popular local BBQ joint.

text: This is a fish out of water story. So I'm en route to El Fuego for some 'ritos when the signage outside Chops catches my roommate's eye. The exchange goes something like this: "I wonder if that place is any good." "I dunno, but it's probably pretty fancy." "Nah dude, check it, $6 burgers!" "Hell, alright, let's go." So we enter, the both of us dressed for dinner at a low-rent burrito spot; t-shirts, shorts, baseball caps. As we cross the threshold of the second set of doors, it's quickly become apparent my initial instinct of "fancy" is about seven shades of understatement. This place is opulent! Before we're able to realize just what we've gotten ourselves into, the greeter (in appropriate suit & tie) approaches and has the same deer-in-headlights look in his eye that I'm sure the both of us maintained. I'm waiting for a line about dress codes and a quick escort to the door we'd just walked through, but was instead welcomed and simply asked, "Two?" Not one to shy away from an awkward social situation for the sake of a decent story, we follow the gentleman to our table located a few feet away. We're seated and finally have a moment to take in just how posh this joint really is. It felt like we had just sat down to dinner in an opera house--incredibly high ceiling, gigantic mural against the far wall, flowing curtains to cover the multi-story windows. I at least have the insight to take off my hat. My roommate does the same. Moments later we're approached by our waitress, Kanika, and are offered our choice of bottled or ice water. With a glance at our matted hair and my college football t-shirt, there's a subtle moment between the three of us and mutual recognition that we don't really belong there. Far from giving us any grief, I detect a slight smile creep onto our server's face and a good-humored acceptance of the situation. Resigned to fully experiencing Chops, we don't even bother looking for any $6 burgers (though I suspect we may have just missed that lunch special and were now considered dinner guests). I order a steak, my dining companion, the veal. A few of the other reviews here have commented on over/under cooked meat, I'll say that Kanika came by our table about 15 minutes after we had put in our order to reassure me that due to the size of my steak, they were making extra sure that it was cooked as ordered--medium. When she returns to our table with our food, I'm faced with what can only be described as an XXL concussion grenade looking slab of meat. This thing is massive. And curiously rotund. I can also say, quite delicious! My roommate enjoys his veal. You know that you're underdressed for an establishment when the team of not one but two people who come by to refold the napkin your company has tossed aside while heading to the restroom are both dressed far nicer than you. All of the desserts shown to us looked incredible but we were both far too stuffed to attempt such a feat. We are presented with the bill, wished a good evening, and asked to come back. Dinner didn't go at all as planned but we had an unexpectedly humorous time and some tasty food. I'll be sure to at least wear pants next time.
label: POS

text: Holy Mole. On our New Yorkers take Philadelphia weekend adventure, we stopped at the Garces Trading Company for brunch and, well, just wow. The restaurant is surrounded by a market, so you can stop in to buy some cheese, meet, desserts, wine, etc, or you can sit down for a meal. Starting with the oil they poured for our bread, everything we tasted was divine. For $25 you can get a three course brunch and, really, who DOESN'T need three courses as their first meal of the day. I know I do. I had the country pate with mustard -- REALLY good (the mustard was especially good!), the duck salad which was sort of like a nicoise salad but with duck instead of tuna. It was really fantastic. The dessert was an option of a salty chocolate tart or a lemon cake. Between the three of us, we tasted both and the chocolate was better, but both were good. I have to admit that I was ogling the pastry counter behind our seats and it took everything I had in me to not buy myself a fourth course after our meal was over. This was a truly fantastic meal, I highly recommend it.
label: POS

text: MMM...to the warm basket of assorted homemade bread that they gave us when we sat down. Compared to the other restaurants in bourbon street, this place is quiet and romantic. Sometimes you need to just get away from the noise and have a nice romantic dinner with your significant other. Appetizer: Chicken and Andouille Gumbo (Cup). Delicious yet heavy, I was already a bit full after eating that and all the bread we got. My fault, of course. Entree: Bronzed Swordfish Hot Fanny Sauce (my dish) Blackened Twin Beef Tenders with Debris (my boyfriends) Both were delicious but I prefer the swordfish because of the spicy, delicious sauce. The garlic butter, the jalapenos, the lemon juice...all of it blended so perfectly. I am stuffed! Dessert: Bread Pudding: I swear that was the 20th bread pudding we ordered in NO. It was good but didn't really stand out. I have yet to find the perfect bread pudding. 5 stars! I would definitely go here again the next time I visit.

text: I wrote a review about 2 months ago and it appears that it has been removed. I wanted to check back to see if the owners or others had comments and it is now gone. Over the years we have ordered sandwiches specifically asking for no spices/seasonings and believe me when I say they put it on every time. I do not write reviews, but this time I had to b/c after stressing that my wife had an allergy, there were still spices on the sandwich. We wound up leaving the Eagles game (parking lot) and going to the emergency room as we did not realize it was seasoned. Upon inspection, it was buried all over the bread (not on top). So we were not only charged for an emergency room visit, but also had to eat the cost of 4 Eagles tickets. When I called to discuss it with them there was not one ounce of care or concern or customer service. I did not ask for anything, just called to voice my story and it was met without care. Again, I have never had a complaint about the quality of the sandwich, but customer service and attention to detail is as poor as I have ever seen. I have visited numerous Primo Hoagies establishments (upwards of 10) and have made the same request every time, and they have gotten it right every time. Not too difficult to see the customer service and attention to detail there. Just be aware that while you get a good sandwich, there is also a lot of negative behind the scenes (and I would not say this if it was an isolated incident). As for my previous review, I am not sure why it has been purged from this list, but it makes me not trust Yelp too much right now.

text: OK, this is certainly not the best sushi I have ever had, but it is consistently good. Actually, I think it is really good, especially for the price. I think every time I have been here I have gotten their Las Vegas Roll. It is just that good. Their caterpillar roll is also delicious. Nigiri style cuts are nicely done as well. I just tried the red surf clam for the first time and it was delicious. The yellowtail on my last visit was also very good. One thing I really like about Sushi Garden over other places is that they don't use nearly as much rice for the rolls. I'm wanting my rolls concentrating on the fish, not the rice, when I go out for sushi. Many places in Tucson don't seem to get that. Another great thing about this place is that they still have the $19.95 all-you-can-eat option. I wish there was tiered pricing though, where a second person could get the same thing for say, $14.95, but that is likely just me being greedy. They also have an all-you-can-eat buffet for lunch, which appears to take place on Saturdays as well now. The choices for sushi from the buffet are indeed limited to a couple types of rolls (no sashimi or nigiri), but there are also many standards from a Chinese-style menu. It's honestly not my thing as I'd rather get the sushi I want, but judging by the crowds here at lunchtime, it is certainly a hit. And really, it is great to have the option. Seating at Sushi Garden can seem a little tight at times, when crowded, but still there is generally seating available immediately, and it is accommodating for a couple as well as for larger parties. The sushi bar is one of the longer ones I've seen in Tucson, and perfect for a "bachelor's" night out as you can sit at the bar, chow sushi, chat with one of the chefs, and watch a game (typically baseball or soccer is on one of the many TVs viewable from the bar). I used to do this here constantly years ago when I lived right down the street. Overall, there's some tweaking that I would personally like to see happen here, but that still doesn't change the fact that this is a nice place to get sushi, with many options that you just aren't going to find at other sushi joints in town. Someday, I'll get to the one by Foothills Mall and see how they compare.

text: Let me set one thing straight. This place is totally VEGAN. The owner is vegan and has told me personally that there isn't anything that's not vegan. Now, the important thing to remember is that this place is for those of us who miss hearty "meaty" meals. So if you are one those vegans who thinks even eating meat shaped food is a bad idea then it's not exactly for you. Lovin' caters to the crowd who wants home style goodness loading down their stomachs with heavy duty burgers, sandwiches, dinners, and sides. That's not to say you can't get light food here, but they really shine with the mock meats. On top of all of that the decor is cozy. So many people are turned off by the vegetarian/vegan lifestyle by having to go to some co-op restaurant and eating next to kids with dreads down to their knees, lip rings, and a "insert political statement here" shirt. The beauty part of Lovin' is that all kinds of people meet to eat here. Yes there are the above mentioned types who dine there, but more often than not it's people who are just popping in on their lunch hour. Professionals, retirees, college students, and people with serious health restrictions all come to Lovin' for some lovin'. Peg (the owner) has done more for the cause of vegetarianism/veganism in Tucson than any amount of sign waving and slogan shouting could do. I highly recommend checking this place out and look out for franchises to open in the future. Is it the best food you will ever eat? Simply, no. Is it the best meat substitution you will ever eat? text: I want to give this place a better rating but I just can't. Here's a pro/con comparison. The pro: DVD's at dirt cheap. Seriously, anywhere from 50 cents to around $5.00, lots of TV boxed sets for $10-15. The con: If you want to trade in your own DVD's for cash or store credit, you will get jack squat. The pro: A young, alternative staff (goths, punks and nerds galore!) who usually have a good, if sarcastic, attitude. I've found them fun to be around, and I even stopped in and dropped off Xmas presents for them this year. The con: A lot of fooling around and a casual attitude can lead to some customer service neglect and very long wait times if you are trading something in and waiting for it to be evaluated. The pro: They buy a huge variety of items, from phones and mp3 players to TV's, video games and systems, DVDs and so on and so on...if it is in working order and of a reasonable value to people, they will buy it. The con: Everyone and their mother brings in stuff to sell, and it seems like business isn't really booming. This means that if you go in to sell your item, they may tell you point blank that they can't do it that day because they don't have the cash available. *AND*, you can't call them up before going in to find out if they CAN buy your item that day, because they have absolutely no phone number listed. (The staff claims they literally don't have a store phone.) The pro: You can pre-shop on their website (www.webuy.com) to get an idea of whether they will buy in your item and how much they will give you for it; and also what items they have in the store. The con: The quotes on the website wildly vary from the quotes in the store. Items are generally ranked in condition from A-E, but the quote on the website is generally for an "A" item, meaning pristine condition. Thus your ipod that has some very mild wear and tear might fetch you $30 less because an employee deemed it a 'C". Of course, this is kind of moot as I'm writing this because the American version of their website has been down for over a week. The pro: If your item is not already in their system, they can contact an appraiser via email with the specs and get a quote for you in or around an hour. The con: The appraiser lowballs - every time. Also, often times if your specific item brand/model isn't listed in their system, they will offer you the system trade-in value of a 'generic' similar item, which is usually extremely low. No one wants to get a Dynex price quote for an LG flat screen TV... The pro: They offer a warranty for a year on electronics. The con: There is virtually no return/exchange policy. You can bring something back within 48 hours to exchange it for an identical item - no refunds. Otherwise you have to fork over your item and have them ship it to God Knows Where for repair. Good luck with that... One thing I've noticed that is a definite con is that items that are 'boxed' are more expensive than items that are not, often dramatically so. To give you an example, an old GameCube system unboxed costs $20, but boxed is $40. You would THINK that this would mean the boxed version comes in the original packaging with manuals and such. But it doesn't. In my case, they put a GameCube console in a box for a totally different version of the console, with no manuals - so that lovely piece of cardboard cost me an additional $20. And also, as I'm writing this, it just dawned on me that they sold me an Xbox at the boxed price and didn't even give me a box... Which literally made me drop my rating to 2 stars. Well crap. Now I'm pissed off. Follow-up review to come in the next 24 hours...

Several of us ordered drinks and some of us, me included, ordered water (what with being all dehydrated from running around like idiots). Those who ordered drinks got them; those who ordered water languished in dry-mouthed misery for an absurdly long time. We then ordered food. The scallop thing looked okay and my friend testified to the fact that the scallops, while not cooked perfectly, were at least not ridiculously chewy. The bangers and mash had good flavor and were plated nicely but came out cold (both of them), which is spectacularly not awesome when one is eating sausage. The salad never showed up at all. As I slowly went insane, sipping my water and watching my friends eat, the waitress eventually got around to telling me that she had somehow failed make clear to the cooks (or they had failed to grasp?) that I wanted chicken on my salad. This meant that they were cooking the chicken now and I would have to wait. I was annoyed about this (I don't go to restaurants to watch other people eat) but I sucked it up. When, finally, my salad showed up, it was the wrong salad. I ordered a chopped salad and they brought me a cob salad. I tried to flag the waitress to let her know and she walked away. I stood up and tried to get her attention and she just kept going. I chased her down and told her what the deal was and she looked exasperated before offering me nothing to placate my by then seething temper. I didn't eat the stupid salad. When we finally got our checks (an amazing waiting game in itself) and paid, they proceeded to rip off my scallop-eating friend by giving her only the cash part of her change and not the coins. text: I work up in Zionsville, and this place has become one of my favorite local barbecue joints over the past few years. Anyway, you start getting hungrier than you were in the first place when you pull up in the parking lot and smell the wood smoke billowing out of their vents. That lovely aroma mixes with the sounds of classic Chicago blues music as you walk inside. It's a cozy, friendly place (though service is often slow) and an excellent place to go with friends, family or more laid-back clients for a meal. The meat has just the right amount of smoke to it, and I often have a tough time deciding between the pulled pork or beef brisket, which are both good. And, if I've got a real appetite, you know I will be going for the rib tips lunch special, which is available all week. As an appetizer, the Brunswick Stew is a nice choice--kind of a spicy, dark broth with chunks of pulled pork and tomatoes in it. And, as the young lady above said, it's mighty hard to forgo the fried biscuits and apple butter--a longstanding Hoosier delicacy. I really have not found many foods I don't like there. Everything I've had has been good. However, if any of you subsequent reviewers end up trying the deep-fried ribs, please post something about it. I'm half scared to try them, but I'd be lying if I said they hadn't piqued my interest. :)

The suite was tiny and filthy, totally not cleaned and a downgrade from what I booked, and the deluxe room was actually just a standard room with just one bed. So, for the eight of us, we now had a total of two beds between the rooms. When I went down to the desk to try to straighten it out, the clerk's response was basically "too bad, so sad," and that they couldn't guarantee rooms (even with a reservation, apparently) and still charge whatever they pleased. I spoke with a manger and got the same flip attitude. She said that "Reno is an adult town" and that people generally share beds. I asked her how six people were supposed to share one bed, no matter how "adult" they are, and she just shrugged and told me it wasn't her problem. We kept the suite for the bachelor, but moved the rest of the guys elsewhere. It took an argument to cancel the other room--it's your choice to be an awful business and not deliver what you promise, but you can't make me pay for something I didn't order--but they eventually said they canceled it. And then when we went to check out of the suite, THEY TRIED TO CHARGE FOR THE CANCELED ROOM. After another argument, and about a half hour of waiting for someone to check records, they decided that they'd "be nice" and not charge for the room we didn't stay in. The hotel is dirty and the staff is rude, unhelpful and greedy. Stay away.
label: NEG

text: Substandard supermarket in a neighborhood full of substandard retail establishments. The "help" isn't particularly helpful, but the Walgreens next door is even worse. Highly recommended if you enjoy watching beer shoplifters. Otherwise, go to the Green Hills Kroger instead.

text: About everything except the food: very nice. Charming. About the food: "Mexican for Gringos". Not authentic, IMHO. Very good, and very predictable, not unlike chain restaurants. Most Americans seem to prefer that, but not me. Very mild and uninteresting. YMMV IMHO, if you want great Mexican food, go where Mexicans go. I find the best Mexican food at the the small, "hole-in-the-wall" stands and restaurants which are rarely in good neighborhoods. BTW, I didn't see any Mexicans or Latinos in SB, and I didn't look for them, so Carlitos may well be the best Mexican in SB. I get better Mexican in New England. text: This is a (mostly) brunch review.... Came in to grab a nice quiet brunch with my fiance. Unfortunately for us, SPTR had the same thing in mind, since it seemed like our server didn't want any part of talking to us. Our morning started of by walking in to the stone silence of the staff, no greeting. We sat down and asked for coffee. Repeat, WE asked for coffee, it was not offered. When it did arrive, It was cold. No water was ever offered. There were dirty dishes sitting out and it smelled awful in there. As if I had a party at my house and had neglected to clean up. Stale beer. Yuck. The food was aight. The grilled cheese was standard fare. Tomato lager soup hit a little too close to home much considering the wicked scents already wafting around. As for the side of mac n cheese, well that was cold. I would have sent it back, but our server never spoke to us again to see if we needed refills, check on the food or anything else. We've also been to the Tap Room a number of times during different parts of the day. Our other experiences haven't been as bad as this, though none were ever particularly good either. The servers, again, have always had a snide attitude. Once a beer snob server didn't want to serve me a Sea Dog that I ordered. I understand that gastropubs aren't exactly renowned for their service, nor should they be expected to, but must I feel like they are doing me a favor by taking my order? Whatever. I tried to like the Tap Room, really, I did. I gave it 5 or 6 chances in the last few years, with experiences ranging from minimally acceptable to downright awful. It just hasn't worked out. My favorite dish is the Chicken Curry, but anything on the veggie menu is tasty as well. Again, I break my prohibition against eating meat here. text: We found a pube in my husband's food. I'm completely serious and have a pic to prove it. In addition to that the service was horrible. We had to ask three times for an orange juice and the waitress never came back to check on us. We went on a Tuesday morning and it wasn't at all busy. So no excuse. The manager handled the situation well enough and immediately notified the chefs what had happened and asked us if there was anything he could do. My husband felt guilty since he had already eaten it but it was under his food so how could he know it was there. In the end they comped his meal and drink. We wont be going back, though. When the manager asked him what could be done to make 'this' better it caught my husband of guard. I've worked in management and in the food industry. Asking the customer how it should be handled in retail is appropriate, but not in the food industry; it's insulting. There should have been no question about the manager comping at least his meal, if not both of ours. The way the question was framed was to pretty much insure that the victim felt uncomfortable enough that no meal was comped. Very poor management. Most likely, he didn't believe us. However, I did see a couple of the chefs go back and use the bathroom about 10 min before our food came out to our table. As to the food, before the pube was found, my husband was content with his food. He got the French Toast with 2 eggs, bacon, and a side of hashbrowns. He said the eggs were good, and cooked to order, the bacon also came out soft as requested, but he did feel that the french toast itself was a little soggy, but not horrible. He didn't make it to the hashbrowns as he completely lost his appetite. I got the Vege Bene w/no onions and ordered extra Hollandaise sauce. The avacado was ripe, and the eggs poached perfectly, however they use a lot of dill in their sauce. At least, that's what it tasted like. In the end it was too dilly/sour for my liking and I wasn't able to get more than a few bites down. Good thing they didn't put extra sauce on it like I ordered. We got charged for it, but seriously, I wasn't worried about the $1.50. As to drinks, my husband got their fresh squeezed OJ, and it was sublime. My coffee, on the other hand, wasn't so great. I generally drink my coffee black, but this stuff was so bitter and burned tasting (Even after a new batch was made). I ended up having to heap cream and sugar into it to make it drinkable.

text: I don't especially love tea or teacart accoutrement, but a number of friends and acquaintances and random old biddies I know adore sipping Darjeeling and nibbling dainty little sandwiches; these anachronisms who belong in a parlor somewhere in the 1800s invariably pick a tearoom for a meet-up spot and I trot dutifully along. Some tea-joints I've been in are drowning in chintz & kitsch and china. The Lincoln Room, thankfully, is not. It's straightforward and uncomplicated, with a decent luncheon menu and of course, a nice collection of teas. It's in a lovely historic building on Market, if you ask they will tell you a bit about the place and it's small connection to Abe Lincoln. Their daily specials rotate, but if you get a chance try the tomato, bacon, and cheddar quiche (delicious). Their soups are also quite scrumptious, as is their croissant bread pudding. The ladies who work there are sweet and friendly, sometimes even pleasantly sassy. Its generally bustling in the small space but never too loud or cramped. I get a kick out of coming in and out of the back entrance... I get a haughty feeling that I'm "in the know, yo". It seems everyone else does too. Those older biddies who come in the back entrance ushering in a bewildered looking grammaw usually enter mid-sentence: "....told ya we could get in this way, Hilda. See, I -know-......" In the fall months, you can inquire about ghost tours of West Chester. I've never done one myself but the Lincoln Room's owner's husband gives them and he's a nice, informative chap.

text: I will NEVER go back to Cliff's, after experiencing the most unprofessional service ever. I wouldn't even give it one star. I recently brought in a sandal for repair. The thong of the sandal had come loose, and although I've had the same repair done before successfully at another place, I thought I'd bring it to Cliff's, which was closer. The man working there was very friendly and promised the repair would be done within 3 days. I paid the cost of the repair upfront, faithful that the repair would be done in a timely manner. I also left the other shoe, which was in perfect condition, with him, as he had asked to use it for reference on the shoe's construction. When I returned to pick up on the date he had promised, I arrived to find he was not there. Someone else carelessly told me to come back after the weekend. When I returned on Monday, I was informed that it was not ready and to come back tomorrow. When I came a third time, I was told it was, again, not ready, and the man complained about being swamped with work over the weekend and lamented about how he had so much to do and was there by himself. If I returned at 5 pm, he'd have it. I came back at 5 pm, the 4th time I'd come to pick it up, and he said that the shoes were not there, but at another location. If I came the next day, he'd have it. When I went FOR THE FIFTH TIME to pick up my shoes, he looked at me woefully and told me "that there was a problem." He had fixed my shoe, finally, BUT HAD LOST THE OTHER ONE. The situation was beyond ludicrous. Instead of completely owning up to his mistake and incompetence, he said that "no one was perfect" and blamed the shoe itself, saying that it was a little shoe and easy to lose track of. I am livid. Not only was my repair not done in a timely fashion, but he lost the match to the shoe, making the repair to the one shoe useless. It doesn't matter if I have the shoe fixed if I don't have the other one to match it. He gave me a refund on the repair, but it doesn't come close to amounting to the cost of the shoes. He's been "looking" for the shoe for a few days now, and he hasn't found it. It's only fair that he refund me the cost of the pair, since I've gone through all this extra trouble on a simple repair. So far, nothing. I'm disappointed that such a long-standing business could be so unprofessional and inconsiderate about the needs and priorities of its consumers. Even if they do find the shoe, I will never go back, and I would HIGHLY DISCOURAGE anyone considering going there. Customers are a privilege, and if a shoe repair place is going to be so careless with both shoes and business, they don't deserve patronage.

text: This is currently our favorite Thai restaurant in St. Louis. The store has a nice layout with the produce on display as you walk in the doors. The have a lot of wood shelving and good lighting to make it kinda classy. They sell plants and flowers, and when I visited they had lilies, and lavender plants out on display along the sidewalk. I went here to pick up a couple things and ended up getting a couple of their stuffed chicken breasted. They have a large selection of meats that are seasoned and prepared so all you have to do is throw it in the oven or the pan and you are good to go. The taste was great!

text: The place is adorable and charming. The bread and butter were perfect. Bread was freshly baked and cut, warm, and the crust was a little bit buttery. The butter was a little sweet and salty and not cold! YAY for room temperature butter! We were here at 5:30pm on a Wednesday and there was only one other table dining there. I loved seeing the cooks in the little french kitchen in the back with the wonderful french music playing. We only ordered two things because we had an appetite to save. My boyfriend got the Vol-au-Vent appetizer (Puff pastry with lobster, shrimp, crayfish, scallop, english peas and an american sauce) and I had the Vegetable tart with Jerusalem artichoke puree, oven-roasted tomatoes, wild mushrooms zucchini, frisee, beurre blanc. Mine was unbelievably good. (I liked his too but mine I think was by far the better dish) The tart was just perfect from the crust, to the little salad on the side; every bite made me want another and I think I could have eaten 5 of these. There was nothing boring about this but nothing overwhelming either. The buerre blanc just brought everything together and if I'm ever in Philly again I am coming here and trying so much more. If it ends up disappointing me next time, at least the bread and butter make me happy.

text: For the most part, I'll chime in with Melissa V.. Applebees is just not a comfortable place to go. It's too loud, and when you're sitting with friends, there's an exposed feeling that is not condusive to either conversation or to sticking around. I'm sure that's precisely what the designers had in mind, but they took it too far. It may have to do with the awful service as well. text: Do not fail to visit the Desert Museum. You'll be sorry if you leave town and then realize what you missed. This is a natural history museum that includes a zoo and aquarium. That's right, there is riparian habitat in Arizona (although much of what once was has been destroyed by humans), and you will see the plants, fish and animals that live(d) there. But the main attraction for me is the walk through the desert where you can see plants and animals in their natural setting, or close to it. If you can come here at the right season, you will see the desert in bloom, which is a magnificent sight. There is an artificial cavern which teaches about cave formation and the creatures that live in caves, as well as geology and plate tectonics. If you visit in summer, this exhibit, the reptile house, the aquarium and the riparian exhibit are shady places to hide from the sun. There is one gift shop near the entrance, but you may want to defer purchasing until you've seen the other one by the food court, especially if you're looking for clothing and jewelry items. This is one museum where there is actually a good restaurant on the premises. My server recommended the Blue Corn Pumpkin Chicken, which was excellent. I would rate the Ocotillo Grill **** for food, ** for service (it was a bit slow) and $$$ for price. Lunch daily 11-3 from October to April, and Dinner on Saturdays from June to August. Call before you go to verify opening times if dining here will be an important element of your visit. They also have the standard snack bars and food court, which are about what you'd expect (i.e. mediocre). IMPORTANT: Wear a wide-brimmed hat and use sunscreen. Even in winter you can get sunburned. There are a number of paved trails, but more are unpaved. Wear shoes that are comfortable to walk in and suitable for unpaved trails if you want to see everything.

text: I chose Tucson Orthopedic because I broke my foot on my move to Arizona and they were the only ones who would see me on short notice that my insurance company would approve. I can't say anything about the doctor because in 30 seconds, you don't develop much of a rapport. The second experience with the office is why I never went back. When I checked out the first time, the receptionist gave me an appointment card with the information for my next appointment. She told me that my appointment would be at the address on the card. So, that's where I went. It turns out that the address on the card is a non-profit group working with a hospital. They get a lot of Tucson Orthopedic patients sent there so they had a number to call, confirmed I had an appointment and sent me to another office. It was a 10 minute drive to the new office. When I arrived at that office, I was told that Dr. Landis wasn't there that I needed to drive all the way across town to the LaCholla office. I've now been driving around for over an hour. I am furious and I arrive at the La Cholla office and am told that because I'm an hour late for my appointment, I'll just have to sit in the waiting room and they'll call me when they have time. For $25, you can get a FIVE POUND burrito. If you eat it within an hour, then you get a free shirt and your picture on the wall--and a refund of your $25. If you fail to finish all five pounds of the burrito, then you still get a shirt and your photo on the wall... but they keep your $25. As of last Sunday, no one had taken the challenge yet. I had a little chat with one of the co-owners while he was making my burrito. Apparently there are several of these restaurants in Pennsylvania and Virginia. This is the first one in Florida and they're looking to expand. I asked how many customers had taken the five-pound burrito challenge up north--out of several hundred attempts, only four people have managed to down all five pounds within an hour. CRAZY!! Considering that this little restaurant is boldly attempting to compete with the dominant burrito chains, has an awesome selection of hot sauces, and promotes eating five pound burritos, I'm going to give this a five star rating. Well done, Machismo. I'll be seeing you again soon.

text: Yes Yes Yes!!! This was hands down the BEST meal I had during my recent visit to New Orleans. Everything about this place is absolutely phenomenal. Mitch M. said it best. My server encouraged me to order the barbecue shrimp - said I could sop up the sauce with warm bread. I couldn't resist. The barbecue shrimp came out in the most beautiful presentation. Next, I was presented with the most delectable looking chicken covered in what appeared to be the maple sauce, and accompanied by a potato hash slightly covered with an egg - sunny side up. I was not to keen on the idea of my potato being covered by an egg, especially since I had never eaten an egg sunny side up. However, I was quite pleased with the taste - the flavors blended together ever so beautifully. Please do not be put off my this unique combination. The chicken under a brick is to die for! You must try this. The service - Dante's Kitchen truly understands the essence of customer service. They wait on you hand and food. What is also very comforting, is that the servers all seem genuinely kind and courteous. They are constantly filling your glass with water, bringing you more bread, etc. You will be taken care of at all times. Dante's exceeded my expectations. This restaurant is definitely one of my top favorites. I will definitely make this one of my stops next time I am in New Orleans. The FQ is great, but why not drive down St. Charles (or take the St. Car) for a scenic view of the beautiful Tulane and Loyola Universities before having a great meal at Dante's Kitchen? It was unlike anything I've ever eaten both in texture and in flavor. +5 for that one. Next? The huaraches! Holy hell, those things were good. Nice flavor, even better presentation, and they were fun to eat. They were like little Mexican flat bread pizzas with a dope drizzle. The taco's were small but packed a punch too. We had the Kobe Beef tacos (srsly, Kobe Beef in a TACO???!!?), and the carnitas tacos. They were really pretty little taco delights. Then we had pork belly in some sort of Mexican format which was seriously the most succulent food I've ever eaten. I wanted more of it. There was also a duck and cheese bake that came with warm tortillas to wrap it in. At this point I was plenty full and plenty drunk as we went through about 4 pitchers of the dopest margaritas you've ever had. Blood orange, passion fruit, the El Heffe and there was one more... But wait, there was one final dish... The fried chicken. OMG. It was panko crusted and fried to perfection. It came with an amazing dipping sauce and then right there, I died. I had a heart attack. EVERYTHING tasted amazing. It was not cheap. It IS a tapas restaurant. Bring your wallet. Bring your appetite because you aren't going to want to stop eating. I will be back.

text: I admit to liking the grub at diners. Stacky's Seaside is the epitome of a typical diner. I went to Stacky's, because Summerland Winery across the street was still closed. So, my friends and I had about 40 minutes to grab a bite to eat. There had to have been a gazillion things on the menu, but I wanted a breakfast burrito. There is nothing like a having a nice hearty breakfast burrito that can fill you up and start your morning. I ordered mine with chorizo and paid a few extra quarters to add potato. After a few minutes, out came a humongous 10 inch breakfast burrito. Holy smokes! I couldn't believe it! It was incredible. What I loved about this breakfast burrito was that it didn't have rice and beans inside. It was not packed full of cheese either. This lovely burrito was all egg, all chorizo, lots of spiciness, and tons of potato slices the size of half dollars and fried like potato chips. It was one hell of a breakfast burrito! Yep, it required tactful eating so the juices from the chorizo doesn't spill or splatter on you. The next time I'm on my way to Santa Barbara in the early mornings, I'm going to make a pit stop at Stacky's Seaside in Summerland. The breakfast burrito is worth every bite.

I had to walk to the lobby which was an 1/8-1/4 of a mile twice each night to get into my room because they wouldn't fix it the first time. The next day the key worked fine. It's as if the mechanism had been turned off. The food I had was prepared for a large number of people, but I still thought it lacked flavor. Maybe lots of hotels are the same way, but I tend to avoid hotel food when I travel unless the restaurant has received notable reviews. There were none of those restaurants in Opryland. The fitness room was spacious and had a decent number of machines which are relatively new. This was the best part of the hotel for me. Also, the hotel is in the southeast part of town so if you want to go to downtown it's a bit of a drive. You are not in the heart of the city. It's in the burbs. Just slip the unbaked pizza and parchment onto the top shelf in a 450 degree oven for 12 minutes and hot baked pizza comes out, which easily slips back onto the cardboard for slicing. I drizzled it with some local olive oil, and fresh parmagiano-reggiano, and it was good to go. text: Going into Mostly Books always lulls me into a dreamlike state. The store is piled high with books and goes far back, and has the feel of someone's attic. It's one of those stores you can browse in forever. It is not for people looking for an organized, polished shopping experience. It's for people who like to rummage and don't mind getting a little dusty doing so. Most of the books are a couple dollars, and I've gotten some great stuff there- books about 1920's Paris, 1910's children's picture books, campy 70's novels. I also like their record selection, priced from about $2-10. It's usually full of those kind of basic records that are keystones to people's collections- you know, like Rumors and Blonde on Blonde. I got an album from The Move there that is definitely hard to find for $4. The trunk of old photos are 75 cents each or three for two dollars. They also have a very organized photo section with photos in plastic wrap that cost more like $2 each. The entire time we had very attentive service, people constantly clearing our plates and filling water and asking if we needed anything else. text: In my opinion, Shelby Park is the best green space in Nashville for walking or biking longer distances. There are probably at least 8 miles of easy, wide bike paths and narrow, winding trails running through the forest in Shelby Park. When I took a walk there, the trail started out running parallel to the river (which was neat), and then went into the woods. There isn't a lot to see in terms of views or land forms and the terrain is flat with some rolling hills, so I think the best way to enjoy Shelby Park would be by bike, the wind blowing in your hair (since there's not much besides trees to hold your attention, and that gets old after a mile or 2). The most interesting part of Shelby is the industrial railroad trestle bridge that soars above the trailhead near the parking lot. Supposedly it's still in use, which surprises me because it looks pretty old and rusty (and awesome). In addition to trails, Shelby park has picnic shelters, a lake, a golf course, and some baseball fields. Shelby is probably the only park in Nashville so large that if you go in deep enough, you can't see a single building or paved road.
