text: This place was the biggest joke. I don't know if the manager paid the other reviewers to say nice things. We could have eaten a better meal at Olive Garden and paid less for it. Nice ambience aside, when it came to the food, this place failed to deliver. The bread brought to our table was dried out and stale (I'd say it was at least three days past any semblance of freshness). Our antipasto salad had pieces of wilted greens in it and bland unripe tomatoes (it is early September in the Garden state, why could they not serve fresh tomatoes?). My husband's chicken parmesan was nothing but a thin frozen breaded chicken patty reheated with some tomato sauce and two pieces of square cheese melted on top (since when does mozzarella cheese come in thin square slices?). His side soup of seafood chowder was straight from a can. And the pasta he ordered with the chicken parmesan was wayyyy overcooked. It only gets worse. Having been taken in by the nice setting (although there was no one there but us at 7pm on a Sunday night), I changed my order at the last minute to one of the "specials"--lobster ravioli. What I got were seven ravioli that had some mushed up unidentifiable seafood in it (tasted more like crab than anything else). This was not "homemade" as touted on their literature. Having worked for Aramark catering for years, I'm sure this was frozen food from some food manufacturer. To add insult to injury, when the bill came I was horrified to see that they'd charged $24 for the "lobster" ravioli. Some special!!! This is a heist to overcharge you for pre-made, poor quality food. Olive Garden does better disguising their dishes--Cafe Mulino could take a few lessons from them. The dinner sucked and it sucked our wallets dry. I've never been so disappointed in a restaurant. I will never go back, and I will keep spreading the word that this place is horrible.

text: My husband and I just went up there this week for our anniversary. We arrived at check in time and went up to our room. Our first room, no joke, had silver wallpaper with pink and green flowers, black carpets, gray ripped up couch, mirrored walls and a jacuzzi with a mirror above it. The kicker was the casino lights that lite the wall that you couldn't turn off. My husband and I were appalled because this was not what we saw on the website. We went down and explained to them that this is not what we want. They nicely moved us to a newer renovated room. The first night we stayed there I didn't sleep too well because the people next to us were using their jacuzzi and it was loud. The walls were paper thin. The next night when went to sleep the people above us started to use their jacuzzi. My husband woke me up at 1:30am to the water leaking down from the ceiling. He promptly called the front desk who said they would get in contact with their engineering department. No, we are so sorry, lets get you another room. My husband waited a few minutes to see if they would call us back to move us but they didn't. He walked downstairs to get another room. The room they gave us was the same 80"s porn room we didn't want in the first place. He walked back downstairs told them he didn't want that room and got another. We got the other and this one too was "newly renovated" but you can see were they patched walls and didn't clean so well. By this time it is 2:30am and we are pissed. We can't sleep and no longer want to stay there. We decided to pack up and go. We go downstairs and the "manager" on duty says he can't comp us the night because we didn't book through them but through their spa packages. My husband said well, fine we will call them but here are your keys, we are going.The man said he couldn't check us out because their system is under maintenance and won't be able to do anything for hours. By this time, we didn't care, we just left. We drove all the way home, 4 hours away because we so upset. My husband called the people we booked the 2 nights through the next day but got the run around and was told several times that they would have the manager of the hotel call us. Its been 2 days since we left and still no call from the Peppermill. We are so disappointed because this was our 1st wedding anniversary and wanted to do something special. We now know to either go to the Grand Sierra or Atlantis. Even if they call us back and want to comp us a night, we will be asking for the Tuscan Towers (their newest) and a dinner free at the steakhouse. I do want to point out that we enjoyed the casino, the restaurants and the spa was FANTASTIC! The only reason why that place stays open is because of that spa. text: My 100th review... I never thought I would see the day. I spent days wondering if I would ever make it to ROTD rather than even think I would make it to #100. 100 reviews!!!...whew... I finally made it. Seems like such a long time ago that I was nervously writing my first review...now I feel even more nervous...okay hold on to your hats, here it is. I thought that for my 100th time that it should be extra special, you know maybe review one of the best steakhouses in and across the country. I wanted to make it the best it could be by spotlighting a place that claims to be the best of the best... Well you won't be hearing about the best of the best in my review of Morton's. I visited Morton's about 10 years in the city on a client visit. Since I wasn't technically paying for my dinner (thank you corporate card), it was a pretty spectacular experience at the time. Now that I was going to visit this place again and going to be paying my way with my own hard earned money, I was not in a position to compromise any of the important factors in a restaurant: décor, food, price and most importantly, service. I was invited to Morton's in K of P last Thursday with my friend and her husband to celebrate their wedding anniversary. Yeah I know what you are all thinking - I have no life. But it was Morton's and I thought my last experience was pretty good, so why not? So being the good little third wheel that I was, I made my way to the restaurant to partake in the anniversary celebration. The first thought I had as I pulled into the crowded K-of P parking lot around 5pm was "Why would you put a Morton's Steakhouse right smack in the middle of an enormous mall; especially next to a discount shoe store?" I continued, "You are Morton's you should be standing alone --separated from the rest...!!!!" The location seemed quite odd to me. Don't you all think so? Once inside, the restaurant seemed quiet and unassuming. We walked into a dark narrow corridor and entered into the main dining room which was barely lit. The décor seemed stale and not very welcoming or warm at all. As I nestled between the 2 lovebirds in a corner booth, I perused the menu that had been eloquently engraved with a "Happy Anniversary". Awww. I felt out of place. I needed a drink. Where's the waiter? After about 10 minutes, the waiter appeared and right off the bat, I thought he was trying way too hard to earn extra moolah on his tip. Too happy and too pushy- a deadly combination for anyone in the food service business. I ordered a Thyme Lemon Drop Martini but failed to realize that it actually had pieces of really thyme sprinkled on the top of the drink as a garnish. What??!!! Who in their right mind thought to mix thyme with lemons in a martini? yukkk, bleck, ewwwww!!! I asked the waiter what was in the drink. He said it was a "Thyme" Lemon Drop Martini. Okay, thanks Einstein. I get it. I thought he could tell by my tone and the look of terror on my face that I did not like it. Did he offer to take it back? No. Did he offer to get me something different? No. Did he offer to have the bartender make me another one without Beelzebub's spice in it? No... My night was immediately ruined (sigh). The entrees were okay; the meat cooked the way that everyone had ordered; I proactively ordered a raspberry martini to try to wash away the taste of thyme from my mouth about halfway through my meal. So let's summarize, shall we? Décor - 1 star Food - 3 stars Price - 1 star Service - 1 star What started as a pretty crappy experience for a hoity toity restaurant, ended up slightly over mediocre in the end. That is after the wait staff and fellow patrons sung happy anniversary to all three of us as we ogled the candle in the middle of the crème brulee and I made it smack dab in between the happy couple in the souvenir anniversary photo... courtesy of Morton's.... Ah memories.
label: NEG

text: I've dined at this restaurant twice and both times has an exceptional dining experience. 14 West is downtown and a good alternative to the other upscale restaurants in the area which are generally larger, louder, and more crowded. The menu changes and I was a bit disappointed to see that the dry aged steaks on the menu last year have been taken off the menu, but there are alternatives for every palate on the menu - lamb, fish, shellfish, steak, chicken, duck, etc. During my recent visit, I enjoyed a very interesting salad with prociutto wrapped duck and warm shitake mushrooms and large scallops over a cream corn concoction as my entree. The food was excellent, but a bit rich, definitely an indulgence. The wine list is very comprehensive and features only the finest quality wines. text: This is my go to place for Ethiopian in Indy. Their food is good but is quite similar to other Ethiopian places but what puts this place in my top list of restaurants is actually the coffee. They preform what the call a coffee ceremony which is $20 for however many people come so it becomes a much better deal as more people come. They bring out green coffee beans and roast them right in front of you while burning incense and then brew it in these gourds of some sort. The coffee is served with the traditional POPCORN!!! Their food is heavy and you will be surprised at how little it looks versus how much it fills you up. If you like spicy food don't forget to ask them for some of their spicy sauce. The staff is very helpful and willing to talk about Ethiopian culture if you are into that sort of thing. They also have an attached store where you can purchase spices and other Ethiopian ingredients. You can also buy the green coffee beans here and try your own hand at roasting on the stove top.

text: I just read what some of the other reviewers of this restaurant have written and I've gotta say that I feel like Henry Fonda in 12 Angry Men right now, because a lot of praise is being thrown around for a restaurant that wouldn't even be a contender in any major city (read: any major city other than St. Louis). If being a template of mediocrity is all that's necessary to receive accolades and achieve success, then I need to stop looking for legal jobs and start singing in Autotune. Anyway, here it goes. I have the switchblade; Wasabi is the table.* You know what comes next. First off, the decor here is laughable. Picture Seki's on the Loop, except with 30 foot high ceilings, no charming Japanese grandmas, and artwork that's less quaint and more LOOK HOW AZN WE ARE. When I walked in, my first thought was literally "are these people serious?!" Hilariously inauthentic artwork of every America-as-Japan cliche known to man adorns the walls. On the bright side, entering Wasabi is about as close as you can get to entering a time capsule. Unfortunately, that time is 1973. The food here has been judged by 22, but should be carried by six. The sushi rolls feature Last Week's Fish Haul in the starring role, supported by my old friend Way Too Much Rice.** Together, they put on a captivating display that compelled me to never want to visit Wasabi again. I at least was able to finish the rolls I ordered, but this is sushi we're talking about. The money was a sunk cost at that point, so it was really just a matter of not eating and leaving hungry versus eating and leaving slightly less hungry. I wish I could say something nice about the service, but at this point I don't even know anymore. I don't remember how nice or not nice the servers were, but I DO remember being really fucking annoyed at myself for actually listening to Yelp reviewers and patronizing this place instead of buying food elsewhere that actually warrants its price point. I know I'm not going to change the verdict on this one because if I had such powers, restaurants like this would go *poof* - along with bigots, Nickelback, mandals, and the word "irregardless". Oh well. Hung jury it is; Henry Fonda I'm not. * I'm not helping you if you don't get this one. ** See also: my review of Sekisui
label: NEG

text: So, I'm feeling juiced after buying a new suit, so I decide to wrap up my outstanding Kirkwood Hwy Indian joint lunches with the last one I haven't tried. I wish I had just skipped it and gone to the Maharaja down the road. I'm giving them 2 stars out of appreciation of their trying different dishes. I believe this is the former Cafe Chettinad, which specialized in South Indian. To be sure, you are given a choice of Naan or a dosa, and the dosa was the best part of the meal, except possibly the gulab jamun. The buffet offerings had some originality, including two goat dishes, Mongolian chicken, one other Chinese related dish, as well as a tofu tikka masala. Unfortunately, the execution was pretty poor. The chunks of meat were low quality, and the sauces tasted cheap. The Mongolian chicken in particular had a nasty red sauces that I'd expect only from the worst Chinese stir-fry place. The tikka masala sauce was not terrible, but the tofu chunks were too soft. I would have preferred a spongier texture, like a paneer dish would have. Alas. $7.95 may be cheaper than the places around it, but an extra $2 apparently makes a heck of a difference.

text: I believe that in the right hands, a person's hair can be the most important part of their appearance. Since I need all the help I can get, I've always paid top dollar for my cuts. But when I heard of Cutters & Co., a men's hair salon inside the Chase, I decided to give it a try. Cutters & Co. is terrible. I explained to the stylist--who, to be fair, was very polite--exactly what I wanted: 1.) barely touch the sides because since I have jet black hair and a white scalp, I don't want the scalp to show 2.) taper the back slightly 3.) trim the top 1/2 inch and 4.) my ears aren't even, so when you do my sideburns, you have to make certain. She basically buzz cut me. She buzzed the sides down way too far, chopped the top, and didn't really touch the back. Oh, and when I got home, my sideburns were 1/4 inch off from one another (I know, I'm a freak). This may have been fine, if she were apologetic, but she wasn't. She asked if I liked it, and in my best attempt to still be nice, I said "it's fine." She could tell on my face that I thought it was shit, and she could damn well tell when I said, "hopefully, it grows out a bit by this weekend, because I'm in a wedding." But she did/said nothing, because she was already working on her next client--a guy that worked at the Chase that asked her if she could squeeze him in before she left (my haircut started at 2:25, and she had to leave by 3). She took one look at my head, and said "yeah, I can do it." Great, I'm a fucking rush job. Where I normally go, it takes between 1-2 hours to cut my hair, because the places I go have people who truly care about your needs because they know that a.) you're going to tip depending on the quality of the cut, and b.) they want your continued business. I told her that my friends and I heard of this place, and that I, being the pickiest about my hair, was the one sent in to decide if this place was worth going to--so she knew going in, that I potentially had a fleet of guys waiting in the wing to come in and give her business. What if the "guys" waiting, were 70 of my fraternity brothers? I just wish she wasn't so damn bubbly. I wanted to yell at her, but I was afraid she'd cry, and I'd look like an asshole with a bad haircut. I even tipped her 30% because she was looking and smiling right at me as I paid. I wish I didn't care so much what people think. Fuck this place, and fuck that terrible excuse for a stylist. *Breath* Thanks Yelp™, I feel much better.
label: NEG

text: You know, I really just don't understand the love that everyone has for Via. I can really only thing of one positive experience that I've had there, although I'll get to that later. First off, I'd like to talk about those used bikes that they have for sale. Have any of you even looked at them up close? They are rusted, really old, and all of them require at minimum a tune-up. How convenient that a bicycle shop, which is already jacking up the prices for those bikes, is selling them. It's a total scam, seriously. When I first moved to Philly and had my first bike stole (sigh, memories...we all remember our first time), I was recommended to go to Via both for a new bicycle and repairs. I chose a Schwinn 3-speed, which looked like it had seen better days, and was assured that they were going to fix everything up, give it new brakes, and clean off all the rust by the time I picked it up the next day. 24 hours pass, and when I returned to get my bike I noticed that the rust was still there, just with a $282 price tag added on to it. To top that off, I had to slam on my brakes on my ride home and nearly got hit by a car because they were just as bad as when I had initially tested out the bike. I promptly returned it, and while the owner assured me that I could bring in my new bike for a free tune up (that's the only good experience that I mentioned earlier), I just can't bring myself to trust Via. Also, the people that work there seem like they are on mass amounts of drugs at all times. When I asked to buy a tiny wrench to help with all those little adjustments that bikes inevitably need, the girl looked at me like I was speaking Hindi and slowly responded "What...? Oh...yeah...you should be, like, really careful because...[looking at the wrench]...it's really sharp...you know?" Come on, really? I'm an adult, not a kid requiring nerf padding on everything that I own. Plus, as someone used to smoke way too much pot, I can recognize when someone is baked out of their mind. Namely her, and the rest of the staff that I saw. Definitely go to Bicycle Revolutions instead. The actual services are slightly more expensive, but the people that work there aren't pretentious, they know their shit, and it's an infinitely more inviting atmosphere.

text: I love Ron's! The service is great, and the beer selection will knock your socks off. We've been several times in the last few weeks, and absolutely everything we've ordered, whether the wings or a salad or a sandwich or their signature "ovals" (basically pizza sans sauce) has been terrific. It's worth pointing out that the bar area and restaurant are two completely different worlds. The bar is beautifully decorated, warm and welcoming, and the service is exceptional -- even when busy. The restaurant feels like a separate establishment. Still good, but tons and tons of kids and families. Which is fine, of course, but the bar feels much more sophisticated (but still casual) than the restaurant, which is a little more generic and Olive Garden-ish. If it's just you and your significant other, or you and a couple of good friends: head to the bar. If it's you and the kiddies and grandma: the restaurant is the place to go. Not in the mood to dine in? Head next door for their take-out, which features an amazing selection of beers, both obscure and well-known. Either way, Ron's is a must-stop for any and all beer fans in the area.

text: Never again! I went here against my better judgment at lunch today b/ it was expedient and I was hoping to keep it uncomplicated. BIG MISTAKE! I wound up paying for the experience. text: What a great surprise for my first visit to Indy! I popped onto Yelp trying to figure out what to grab for dinner after a rough day of travel and work. Staying by the airport, there wasn't a ton around... Luckily for me, Bosphorus was only 12-15 minutes away. Just S.E. of downtown, the restaurant is a small 15 table or so business run by a nice family. At 7PM on a Wednesday there were a half dozen parties when I got there. I decided to have lentil soup, Doner, and rice pudding with Efez Dark Turkish beer and Turkish coffee to wash things down. I thought the bright yellow lentil soup was good although could have used a pinch more seasoning for me. The Doner was flat out awesome! As a frequent traveler to Germany, I used to eat a lot of Doner and struggle to find it in the states. For the uninitiated, Doner is seasoned lamb shaved from a rotating roasting spit. Bosphorus served it with a fresh green salad, vegetables, sauce and pita. The Efez Dark was a nice beer that I would best refer to as Turkey's answer to Negro Modelo. The second one was even better than the first. I questioned whether or not I wanted to spring for dessert but the thought of Turkish coffee and rice pudding was too much to resist. I am SO glad I did; the rice pudding was a perfect consistency and flavor. Each spoonful of the large bowl was "heaven". And the coffee was "black as midnight" and "strong as love". The atmosphere was casual yet nice enough to use for a birthday party (which was the reason two tables were there). The service was attentive and pleasant without being smothering, which can sometimes be the downside of being a party of one. At the end of the day, if you like middle Eastern cuisine, you can't go wrong with Bosphorus. Great stuff!

text: CASH ONLY!!! Park on the street. Buffa's Restaurant and Lounge are moving up to the top of my list for a good burger in town. Okay not the very top but close. Buffa's was more lounge than eatery. They have free wifi and people actually use it for doing work! This is weird only because I cannot imagine a more decadent atmosphere. Smoking, drinking, and heavy food are musts at Buffa's. The front room is clearly 1930's as the sign outside suggests. On my trip it was dirty and not well kept by a very friendly and happy bar lady. A wall mounted juke box played a range of music. Jazz that was playing upon our entrance was replaced by more modern songs such as Champaigne Supernova. Patrons were friendly but they all had heaters shoved in their mouths. They loudly proclaimed their disdain for work, appeared to be regulars, and all knew one another. The major drawback to Buffa's for me is that they allow dogs inside. While some dog owners might applaud this practice I think it's disgusting and dirty. One guy's dog was up on the bar eating food. I mean, that's gross. And it makes me wonder about the food quality. We nevertheless attempted to ignore sanitary problems and ordered two Buffa Burgers. The signature burgers took a long time to be prepared--probably around 15 minutes. But it was totally worth it! The Buffa Burger was extremely thick, juicy and fresh. I was really impressed by the quality of the tomato and other ingredients--clearly fresh and purchased that day. The only reason this is not a top burger for me is that the meat was not well seasoned. This is good and bad. For me, I try to keep a low sodium diet and seasoning on beef means salt. So I liked the low salt. But I could see others needing to add a bit more of this seasoning than they might normally do. The burgers are $9 each plus extra cash for any modifications. Rare burgers were awesome here!!! Just as an FYI: beer is only in bottles. No draft beer. The bar is a full bar. Beer was $4 per bottle of Abita. Abita SOS was available for $7 a bottle. Fries were pretty good. They were crisp and tasty. Not too special but a good job nonetheless. Fries were about $3. My conclusion: don't feel bad about being left out of Port of Call. The Buffa Burger is actually superior!! One of the best burgers in town.

There were three pasta dishes - I tried the gnocchi, which I almost never do, because I was in the mood for an alfredo sauce. They were wonderful, but extremely small - only 4 gnocchi for the plate. I guess it doesn't matter much when you're getting a 10 course meal! Then there was a little orange sherbet - to cleanse the pallet, I suppose. Then we waited a little longer than i think we should have for the main course. I got the chicken parm, which came with some spaghetti and marinara sauce. It was good, but didn't knock my socks off or anything. Might have just been full at that point. Finally, they brought dessert, and each person got some vanilla ice cream, some coffee flavored thing, and what appeared to be a moose cream puff. Again, very well done. Service was extremely attentive - filling drink glasses without being asked, etc. They could be a little curt, but I think it was the stress of dealing with so many people. We got a little room in the back to ourselves - maybe 20 or 30 people. I have no idea the cost as the bill was paid for by Pfizer. So, there you go. Apparently, a good place to have business meetings or talks. Excellent food and fun if you want to do all the courses. If you get a choice, I certainly recommend the mussels. And make sure you try that bread. Maybe I'm tired. No fun anecdotes specifically related to the restaurant. Sad. Good talk, good food, good price (for me, anyway). Sign outside says 'Pizzeria and Grill' and 'Wood Fired Oven'. That always sounds appealing, doesn't it? Edited to correct spelling of 'Pfizer'. Thanks, Jeanne F!

text: Hotel Review: another listing on Yelp says that the hotel is CLOSED. Well, not unless it happened last week! Coming from LA for a conference at which my husband spoke, I scheduled the travel on Travelocity (which gave the hotel 3 stars, and travelers there rated it 3.5. I suspect ownership fabricated its own reviews). This hotel sounded quaint: "Ben Franklin room, fresh flowers, breakfast, private bath in historic downtown" ...ok. At $120 a night plus tax, I was expecting a small clean room with no frills. If the room had been $35 and had only 2 stars on Travelocity, I would have KNOWN what I was getting into. A NIGHTMARE!!!! We cab it to the front door with a grimy note saying "Check into Hotel at the Bar". Ok, a red flag # 1. The bartender looks at a piece of paper and hands us a key on a cheap keychain (from which the key fell). He opened a back door behind the bar and told us to climb to the 3rd floor. OK... RED FLAG # 2. Up we climbed some unkempt stairs and hallways that became more dilapidated with each floor. I started to feel a little sick but remained optimistic. Once we reached our floor we noticed a missing ceiling panel with electrical wires hanging down. GULP! The front door was some cheap hollow patched door I could have put my fist through. The rickety lock made my husband curse. Once inside I knew immediately we would not stay. Forget red flags, this is a total bait & switch. The walls were cracked and disgusting. The furniture had scratches and looked like someone's leftovers from a street corner. I looked everywhere for some redeeming quality. Outside the window was an awning torn into a million pieces... dirty and unrecognizable as an awning at all - I wondered why no one had removed it since the wire frame it once hung on screamed RUN!!!! I saw dirt on the floor and windowsills. The bathroom was scary. I can't imagine it had been cleaned in a long time since there was black mold everywhere. A hairdryer was stuck to the wall with a piece of plywood. Upon entering the bedroom it was noticely visible that the mattress was bumpy and uneven. Like a dark and dreary dungeon, the "Ben Franklin Room" at The Society Hill Hotel has an incredible view of a 3 foot space between buildings that was the dirtiest location in Philadelphia. On the dirty window stuck a grimy file folder label which read in pen "Do Not Open Window!". We opened the closet and on the floor we found a disgusting window air conditioner. We didn't bother turning it on. After my husband found a sign which read "Not responsible for Theft" he made a comment about being shanked in our sleep by a crack head. He was furious, and I felt responsible. Why Travelocity? WHY?!!! Back down to the bar to return our keys and refuse to stay. The bartender explains that the restaurant is separate from the hotel, and that we would have to come back tomorrow as no one from the hotel was there. Then why did the bar hand us our keys and then accept them back when we left? And why is it that for two days Travelocity tried repeatedly to contact the hotel with no answer? And why is it that our credit card was charged for the entire 3 days for which we had booked? We could not cancel. We could not reach anyone. We had to find another hotel to stay in at the last minute. Everywhere nearby was booked. We took a $60 cab ride to Laurel, New Jersey and stayed in a Beautiful HYATT 2 bedroom suite with a full kitchen. We were quoted $149 a night, and they reduced it to $99 to make up for the cab ride. The Society Hill Hotel is a scam that will be reported to the BBB of Philadelphia. Our credit card will eventually refund us the money, but it will take a few months. PLEASE! Do yourself a favor and do not stay at THE SOCIETY HILL HOTEL. I cannot speak for the food, drink or anything else at the "Bar - Restaurant", but I have some advice for them: Do not take keys, give out keys, share the same name or serve breakfast for the hotel if you are not affiliated. Personally, I do not believe the claim that they are not the same since every aspect was linked to them. I believe it is just how they avoid unhappy customers and rip them off. I feel so bad for the people who show up and do not have the money to go somewhere else. Always check YELP first.
label: NEG

text: I have a problem. I have been thinking about the vegetable samosas from Desi Chaat House a lot. It is causing a serious interruption in my daily functioning. Open mic nights always add a bit of apprehension, those two minutes by an awful comedian can seem like an eternity. And though there were a few thrown in there, most had me literally laughing out loud. text: The End has long lived in the shadow of its larger counterpart, The Exit/In, which can be found just across the street. While you probably won't see the enormous touring acts that often grace The Exit/In with their presence, The End is an absolute must for popular local bands, and you can often catch comedy shows and DJs if you keep up with their schedule. Probably the most exceptional feature at The End, however, is the sound. Run by Bruce (you can't miss him), the mix at this little dive is possibly the best in Nashville. Speaking as someone who has played and seen shows all over the city, I have to tell you that you won't hear a more unadulteratedly clean and pure board mix anywhere. Being tucked right in the middle of Elliston Place makes for a good evening, and you can always skip down to the Goldrush or the Corner Bar for a shot if you're sick of swilling cheap beers. The End also has a nice but somewhat busted little patio for smokers. The door on the men's restroom, however, has never seemed to fully shut. text: I ate at PBandU about a month after it opened. We were a group of four adults and a 1-year old. This was one of the most disorganized, poorly-run restaurant experiences I have ever had. I love supporting small businesses and I love the fact that they are making their own peanut butters, but PBandU needs some improvement before I'll give them another try. The decor is very clean and modern, bright with graphic decor on the walls. Despite having a large space for seating (as well as a large toy room if you turn the corner behind the counter), there were very few tables and chairs. One of the employees carried out a few extra chairs while we were there, to accommodate the crowds. Luckily, most other patrons cleared out shortly after we placed our orders, so we had a table to sit at - however, the peanut-shaped tables aren't really baby- or highchair-friendly. Speaking of ordering, what a confusing process! There was no clear indication of where to go to place your order. We ended up standing at the far end of the counter, where we had seen other customers place their orders. Four or five people were crowded at this end of the counter, scrambling to make up the sandwiches. Eventually, a woman (who turned out to be the owner of the restaurant) looked up and asked if we'd been helped yet. When we said we hadn't, she took down our sandwich orders on Post-It notes, then set about making each sandwich individually. 30 minutes later - yes, half an hour, to make a peanut butter sandwich - I finally had my lunch. When they called me to the counter to pick it up, I moved along to the cash register, which seemed to surprise them, as they assumed I had already paid. So I could have gotten a free sandwich. Not that the prices are bad at all. If there is one thing going for this place, it is the prices for the amount of food you get. My peanut butter, banana, and Nutella sandwich was so rich and sweet, I couldn't even finish it. Which brings me to yet another issue: why can't they sell half-size sandwiches? Especially if they are trying to appeal to parents and children, there is no kid-size meal available. PBandU has the potential to be a really fun place, but at the moment it's disorganized and inefficient. My suggestions for improvements: - Clearly indicate where the line for customers to place orders starts, then move them along to pay. - Make the sandwiches assembly-line style, rather than having one person make each sandwich from start to finish. Someone toasts bread; someone spreads the peanut butter, Nutella, fluff, jelly, etc.; someone adds other toppings; someone plates the sandwich and adds chips, drinks, etc. - Instead of using regular-sized jars of spreads with plastic knives sticking out of them, maybe use some sort of peanut butter gun for speed and accuracy (especially when making items like "ants on a log"). - Utilize space better, both behind the counter and in the seating area. - Considering the limited menu, offer other types of jelly or other nut butters besides peanut.

text: So our travel book said that NOLA was the place to be for Christmas and, even better, that there wouldn't be crowds in town like during other holidays. When we arrived, it definitely was not overwhelmingly crowded though we were clearly not the only ones in town for the holidays who weren't visiting family. I say all this because, as an out of towner, it was difficult to make dinner reservations a few months ago for Christmas day dinner. We looked online and used the nola.com Reveillon Dinner restaurant list as a place to start. Several restaurants were already booked that we called, so we opened up Yelp and started to make more calls. Several of the most highly rated places like Bayona weren't even serving a Christmas dinner. The Upperline was also not open. So the reviews on Yelp looked pretty good for Cafe Adelaide so we called and made a reservation. Their web site (with the Swizzle Stick Bar) looked quirky so we weren't turned off by the fact that this restaurant was in the Loews Hotel. Typically, unless you're dining at a 5-star hotel restaurant, you're not in for a great meal, but because of the reviews for Cafe Adelaide on Yelp, I thought we would be in for a good meal. We arrived a bit early for our 7pm reservation and were seated in a corner near the restaurant entrance. The hotel service people were outfitted in the exact standard issue hotel uniforms you would expect and many of the busers and even a couple of the servers were clearly high school or college age working a seasonal job, which is generally not the sign of a great place either. Oh well, it was open on Christmas. Our server was an adult, dressed in a non-uniform suit, but the whole time he seemed nervous and not particularly warm. He reached his hand really far out to clear plates as if to stay as far away from us as possible. Granted, the tables were way too large, but still, bizarre. He was accommodating and deferential, but not as professional as what I expect at a nice place. We started with cocktails from the Swizzle Stick Bar--I a Cary Grant and my husband a Sazerac--after perusing the cocktail menu. Surprisingly though, we were never brought a wine list before ordering our dinners and our entrees came out so fast that we were still finishing our cocktails with our meals. Again, not fine dining timing though we paid fine dining prices. We both had the filets mignon with potatoes, green beans and a large shrimp. The filets were fine, but seemed somewhat over-rested and were not very warm. The green beans were advertised as served in a balsamic reduction, but really the beans had been stewed in that sauce so that they were more like canned green beans. Did I mention that these entrees were $36 each? We're willing to pay for a good meal, but for the lackluster quality this was waaaay too much. We tried to redeem the restaurant with desserts--"Creole" Cheesecake (topped with freeze dried raspberries--Why???? Aren't raspberries good enough fresh?) and the Strawberry Shortcake. Neither were earth-shattering. I had an overly strong coffee before we left and went to enjoy a great night at the Maple Leaf Bar. If only we had eaten somewhere else. Come here for a cocktail and eat somewhere else unless you enjoy awkward service and mediocre food at upscale prices. I almost forgot, if you go, don't forget to check out the wood paneled walls. They were lovingly painted to resemble a zebra skin pattern, but again, on WOOD panels in a nice brown wood color, ALL over the walls. Classy? Not so much.

text: First, I should preface that I am by no means a carnivore or expert in anything steak or steak-related. In fact, until Del Frisco's, I hadn't had steak in more than 10 years. I'm not a fan of the rubbery, over-cooked version my mom used to make me as a kid. That being said, my husband was hell-bent on checking out Del Frisco's for his birthday dinner. I was hoping there would be some non-steak/veal/pork options for myself, but sadly there were no chicken or pasta dishes and the lobster was like $100. To appease my husband, I decided to give steak a try again and ordered the beef tenderloin or beef medalions, which were like little cubes of steak. It was served with their special mashed potatoes. After that meal, I'm proud to say I'm back to eating steak. It was one of the best meals I ever had. The beef was so tender it practically melt in my mouth (I couldn't bear to ask for ketchup at a steak house and I'm glad I didn't!). The beef came with a warm brie sauce (which I strongly suggest you order on the side). I'm not a huge fan of brie, but the combination worked quite nicely as a dipping sauce. The mashed potatoes were to die for. However, the side of mushrooms were cold and forgettable. I also ordered a salad wedge which was cold, crisp and quite good. The bread didn't seem as special as everyone made it out to be -- but it was quite good. Soft and warm and definitely devoured. My husband got the seafood soup, which he loved. And the 12-ounce filet mignon, which was also good. He got a side of onion rings, which were so huge he only ate two or three, but they were good too. For dessert, I thought it was a nice touch that they gave us a $10 piece (or slab -- it was huge!) of butterscotch cheesecake on the house, when I mentioned it was my husband's birthday. It was SO GOOD. The butterscotch and what tasted like a Heath-bar type of crunch on the crust, was to die for. Now, for the service -- EXTREMELY attentive, almost overbearing, on the night we went (it was still fairly early evening on a Friday night and there weren't many tables). People were constantly checking on us and asking how our meal was and were we having a good time. We felt like VIPs or something. It did get a little annoying but I appreciated the attentiveness. My only complaint was that we were seated on the main floor, and it looked like there was no separation between the bar area and the dining area. As it was happy hour on a Friday, the place was booming with bar-goers who seemed to filter out into the dinner crowd...there was no buffer there, and it was quite loud. That is something they should definitely fix. But really I don't have any complaints, except the restaurant is very pricey. But for a special occasion or even just a nice dinner out when you've saved some cash, I highly recommend Del Frisco's. As I said, it was one of the better meals I've had and completely restored my faith in red meat!

text: Brunch at Luke left me with mixed feelings. We were greeted by a hostess who looked at us as though we had just killed her cat, and our waiter seemed like he had a thousand things he'd rather be doing than waiting tables. They weren't particularly busy, but our waiter seemed occupied with doing anything but his job. I don't always like my job either, but after the third time I'd asked for a water refill and was absolutely parched, I had to wonder what he was up to when he kept vanishing. Despite the terrible service, my food was delicious. The Bloody Marys had just enough kick. I ordered the fried oyster, bacon and avocado salad to start, and the oysters were perfection (although the dressing was a bit heavy). My entree was the Croque Madame, and the crispy edges were heavenly. The middle got a bit soggy with all the cheese and a little much mustard, but overall I was happy. One of my dining companions had the Crawfish Bisque, which was one of the worst things I've ever eaten. Imagine a cup of heavy cream mixed with pepper. No crawfish flavor, terrible seasoning and entirely too heavy. Nothing like what my grandmother used to make. The same dining companion had a particularly unfortunate meal, as she ordered the crab omelet. All I can say here is that cucumber, crab and eggs do not belong on the same fork. The third diner in our party had some better luck with the seafood gumbo (good, not amazing), a nice crab salad and some sort of onion bacon tart thing that was divine in small portions, but a bit heavy overall. Fries were served cold. Not lukewarm, cold. I thought it might be an off day and was ready to forgive the bad service until a bartender popped open a bottle of champagne and the cork grazed my head (I was sitting about 20 feet from the bartender in question), and no one seemed to care. Our waiter resurfaced at the end of the meal to ask how things were, we told him we were finished, and no less than 20 minutes later he returned to again ask how we were doing. Check please? He wandered off not to be seen again for 10 minutes, and we entertained ourselves watching the hostess wander from her post then sprint back across the restaurant every time the phone rang. Professional. Really. Add some bizarre, disjointed decor and the overall atmosphere almost ruined my food. I've eaten at a few other Besh restaurants and have never been disappointed until now. I want to believe that this was a bad day, but as the best service we received all day was from the valet at the Hilton next door, I don't see myself returning.

text: What can I say about Reid Park? Except that I love it. This park has so much going on. Not only does it have a zoo, swimming pool that is opened year round, golf-which I believe is a driving range, tennis, classes, and a great walking/running/biking path around the entire park. This is seriously one of my favorite parks to go to. It's three miles around the park and the path is paved and also divided so that way people don't run into each other. Lots of families along with lots of runners. The park is always bustling and this is one of my quick ways to get a great work out in. They also have playgrounds in the park along with a dog park as well. I love walking/running here there are people of all different sizes which is great and they are all there for same purpose to lead a healthy life. Its a flat path but great for workout partners I definitely recommend it! We went after it was dark so it was nice and cool while we were running remember to bring your water bottle! I am planning on walking/running this more during the week and trying to get hopefully in a daily routine of it.

text: Wow. Just, wow. I'd sooner go to any of the generic Thai places in the city (the stand in The Reading Terminal is a favorite) than visit this place again. I've walked past this place many times on my way home from work, and decided to try it one afternoon when I was craving some Thai. Big mistake. The service was pretty average, cashier seemed friendly enough and was kind of cute. I always get pad thai, so I branched out and got the Singapore Noodles with chicken and a can of Thai Iced Tea. (the same one you'll find at most of the small Thai places in the area.) I got my order very quickly, within 10 minutes of ordering. I had high hopes for this place. I got home, opened the container, took a bite, waited to be dazzled, and.....nothing. Absolutely nothing. It's almost as if they gave me plain noodles cooked in salt water, a few pieces of chicken & salted veggies, and more salt. No sauce. The flavor ranged from super bland to super salty. I tried to spruce it up a bit by adding some low-sodium soy sauce, just so I could stand the flavor long enough to get everything down and not waste my $10. Acceptable. But then, I reached the bottom 1/3 of the container where I found another "what the hell is this doing in here?" flavor.....noodles slathered in butter. At that point I just had to throw in the towel and order pizza. Never again.

Yes, here our canine friends can enjoy the outdoors without worry to fences or being distracted the UPS truck stopping and making a delivery down the street. Of course, you must keep your dog on a leash. Queeny Park is a great place to get out and into nature for a little while. The bartenders are always super friendly. The interior is perfect for dates to small/medium sized groups - intimate, a little dark, clean lines, albeit a bit smoky (welcome to NOLA!). It's right on the streetcar line and a short walk from some Magazine Street craziness, if you crave something different as the night goes on. They're still trying to sell a 2005 pinot in their tasting room? Gives you some clue. And $55 for this? Way overpriced. I love their sister winery, Lafond, up in Santa Ynez. text: Supper is one of my new favorite brunch spots in Philly. I've been to Supper for dinner previously, but recently stopped by for Sunday brunch after it made Philly Mag's Restaurant Club Brunch Guide. We went on a Sunday around 12:30pm. They were pretty booked up with reservations (they take reservations for brunch!) but we managed to score two seats at the bar. The eggs benedict was one of the best I've had and even better than the one my husband makes (which is pretty damn good). All sides are separate, so order the cornbread hush puppies if you know what's good for you and the duck fat fingerling potatoes. Yes, my friend, fried cornbread + potatoes + duck fat = heaven. Service was good, and the freshly squeezed orange juice was delightful. Brunch at Supper is slightly more chic (ie. this ain't Honey's hipster scene) but comfortably casual nonetheless. Final thoughts... A great place for Sunday brunch especially when you can plan ahead and make reservations. Food is fresh, well-made, and offers twists on the standard brunch staples.

text: I've read people's reviews saying that this is the "best pizza in South Philly," but I'm going to go ahead and say that this is the best pizza in the city proper, hands down. Although I'm not a fan of traditional Chicago-style deep dish pizza or Sicilian pies, LaRosa makes the perfect cross breed of the two. The buttery, thick crust is (as my dining partner described it) "a buttery pan pie, like what Pizza Hut was going for, but perfected and respectable." Enough said. Who isn't a sucker for a crisp, thick and flaky crust? Add to that any combination of gourmet ingredients of your choice for one hell of a delectable pie. I mean, I couldn't stop myself from eating so much that I felt sick from being overstuffed after the experience. The pepperoni is full of flavor, sliced between too thin and too thick, it's perfect. I highly recommend the white potato, rosemary pie - even without their delectable, home made sauce, this one's a flavor party in your mouth that goes unmatched. Fair prices for an absurd amount of delicious food, that's my kind of establishment.
label: POS

text: If you've read my other reviews, you know that I'm not one to full out hate someplace, or give vague reasons why I don't like something. SO...I do not hate The Delachaise, but I do have several specific reasons why I did not have a good experience there. 1. It is small and not well equipped to being a restaurant, staff-wise. 2. There was smoking allowed indoors, and no ventilation. 3. We had to literally argue with another party to get a table outside, when we had been waiting for over an hour. *4. The service. If you're interested in hearing about the service, please read below. We sat down at our table (finally) and had to go up to the bar to order food - there was a waiter, but it looked like he was just there to deliver the meals. And talk on his phone. Our food finally came! Yay! It was 10:00 or so, and we were all really hungry. So, anyway, our food came. No - wait - everyone else's food came and my stomach continued to growl. I waited for about ten minutes before going up to the bar to inquire about my missing grilled cheese sandwich, and when I did, bartender A told me he'd check on it. I stood there watching him not check on it for ten more minutes, before asking the other bartender. I was told by bartender B, that because so many people order the grilled cheese, the oven was backed up. "It'll be out in a few minutes." Mmm Hmm... So I waited for another fifteen minutes and went back in again. Me: "Hi, I still haven't gotten my sandwich." Bartender B: "You still haven't gotten it? Hang on..." When he came back, he told me that it was on it's way out. I was almost in tears at this point I was so hungry and frustrated (I know, silly, but true) and said that I thought it made sense if the sandwich was on the house. He had no idea what I was talking about, and asked me if I had changed my mind about the sandwich. "No, I still want it - the rest of my table has already had their food for over a half and hour. I think it should be free." I went back outside and waited for an addition ten minutes, before going in again with my fightin' words ready to go. Still no sandwich, but bartender B went and found it (piping hot) in the kitchen and gave it to me. I settled my tab at the bar with bartender A, who had no problem taking my sandwich off the bill, and everything was - ehem - fiinnne after that. Not the end of the world, but I expect better from people who earn their wages in tips and work six feet from the place where the food is cooked. The wine was good - I had the Malbec, and people I was with had beers and scotches, all of which seemed to satisfy them. Alcohol is definitely this place's forte - they should probably leave the restaurant business to people who know what they're doing.

text: I'm really of two minds about this place. On the one hand, I like the idea that you can have a fried egg as an option on your burger and the hand-dipped shakes are to die for. On the other hand, the beef itself isn't that good. The patties are generous and a single burger is plenty of food, but the beef really isn't that good. It's not that it's inferior meat, it's that it's lean/fat ratio is too lean. A really good burger is first the lean/fat ratio and then how it's cooked (flame broiled being the best). Fatburger's burgers are, ironically, too lean. Basically, the more fat, the more flavour. Too much fat though and it's too greasy to eat. Fatburger's particular mix is simply too lean for my taste; I feel that I get a lot to chew but it doesn't taste juicy or beefy enough for me to think of it as really good, and since these burgers are on the pricey side, it's not worth the money. The thing too is that there are way better burgers for less in town: Red Robin, Milestones, Rodeo Burger. I really wanted to like this place (Did I mention you can get them to put a fried egg on it?), but a burger is about beef and beef should be about flavour. There just isn't enough of it for the $10/$12 they want for it.

I wasn't terribly impressed with the pesto sauce - it wasn't very flavorful. All in all, they may have a few kinks to get over - but if you want quality pizza in South City, this is a true hidden gem. My guess is that they will only continue to improve over time. I can't wait to try the strombolis and calzones. I have a distinct feeling that the more traditional italian-style fare will knock my socks off. Our waitress seemed a little bit... what's the word? Oh, stoned. But that didn't really bother me. She wasn't the greatest but she wasn't terrible - and I was eating pizza and drinking wine, so I really didn't care. The interior is cute x 1,000, and I'm looking forward to trying their take-home products (pasta sauces, etc.) I love the bigger-city feel of this joint. I'd love to see them put a few tables outside! text: I ate there last night for restaurant week as a party of 7. The only reservation I could get was for 9:30 PM. At 9:25 we checked in and were told that it would be a few more minutes. We dropped off a few bottles of wine and asked that the white be chilled. We returned at about 9:35 to check the status of the table and were told the table was still not ready. They asked us to wait in their cramped hall with no ETA on the table. At 9:55 I asked the hostess the status of the table and she could not give a straight answer - all she said was that she couldn't rush the other table and they couldn't say how long. We were finally seated a little after 10. Then we were made to wait for bread, water, and menus. When they brought the bottles of wine - the white and champagne were warm (we would have been better leaving them on the cold sidewalk). The meal was OK - and very welcomed as we were starving. When the bill arrived we were a little shocked to find that 20% gratuity had already been added -service was nowhere near deserving of that. Each person at the table put credit cards in to pay and the waiter came back and said they only took 2 credit cards per table. We told them that that information is not written anywhere and they argued that it was restaurant policy. The hostess came over to explain the same thing - however she said that they don't accept more than 2 cards per table because the credit card fees are so high. We went back and forth with her for a bit and then the manager came out - apparently he never heard the term 'the customer is always right." We asked him to split the bill into 'separate' tables so we could each pay on the card; he said he wouldn't do it that one person can charge on their card and get money from the rest or that we could go down to the ATM to get money. We asked him why he takes large reservations but doesn't tell customers the policy. He didn't waiver and we weren't going to either. He finally took the bill with all the cards-we assumed he gave up and was going to divide it. But No, rather he charged everything to my debit card - he said "You made the reservation, so I charged it to you - they can pay you." I refused to sign the slip - which didn't matter because it's a debit card and the money was already withdrawn. The manager threatened to call the cops - which I still don't understand because we PAID the bill through his fraudulent and deceiving manner. We argued and I took the bill and left the unauthorized slip on the table. He followed us out with a bunch of busboys-still not sure why. Almost to hold us there until the cops arrived - still not aware that he'd already stolen the $$$ from us. He continued to argue with us on the sidewalk but we got in cabs and left - before the police arrived. All I can say is that I've worked in the service industry and concessions can always be made - no matter how hard it is. I have dined in a plethora of Italian BYOs in the city, as well as many upscale restaurants, and have NEVER in my life been treated in such a way. Don't waste your TIME and MONEY on this place - we live in such a great city for restaurants - the mediocre food isn't worth the terrible treatment. I can say I will NEVER be back - even if they give the food for FREE!!

text: One might assume that Indianapolis is incapable of offering fine cuisine in the Italian realm, however, we all know what can happen when we ASSuME. Sangiovese proves wrong all naysayers, providing an ideal blend of relaxing atmosphere, great food, courteous and informed staff and live entertainment. You will struggle to find better Italian food anywhere in Indiana, and now the locally-owned, northside spot is reaching out to a nightlife audience, as they have already established two regular weekly events (Flirt Wednesdays and Tantivy Thursdays) featuring local DJs, a sexy crowd, and in some cases, live art and fashion events. The restaurant also provides some of the best outdoor dining in the city. Here in the Midwest, dining enthusiasts race to the restaurants that feature decks and rooftop dining during the few months of the year where it can be comfortable to eat outside. Sangiovese's deck seats at least a few dozen tables, and is not adjacent to any busy street or noisy clutter. In fact, quite the opposite is true: the deck, located on the backside of the restaurant, faces a secluded section of the White River and provides a spectacular view, particularly as the sun sets during evening dining. This is another example of one of Sangiovese's best qualities: you can take a date, a group of friends, or your parents and be equally comfortable with the atmosphere and the service. As if eating, drinking and dancing weren't enough, Sangiovese also offers catering services and delivers (minimum order required) anywhere in the greater Indianapolis area. If you're a business needing a lunch catered, be sure to give them a shot. Located in between Keystone and Allisonville on 82nd Street. Do yourself a favor and grab dinner at Sangiovese. Stick around on Wednesday or Thursday for DJs (starting at 10pm). One meal at this place and you'll be booking your next reservation!
label: POS

text: Royal Tavern has been on my list of places to try for a while now, so when we were searching for a place to grab a beer and quick bite too eat on a sunday evening, I was eager to check it out. The menu provided a solid selection of vegetarian and vegan options. I was starving and ordered the tempeh club, my boyfriend and friend both ordered the grilled cheese and soup. The beer selection was varied and we ordered MaredSous 8 (always good to see one of the less popular belgians on draft) and Arrogant Bastard. The soups (Potato and Butternut Squash) arrived first and were rather watery- I understand they were vegan, so that explains the lack of cream used...) My tempeh club was good, except for the fact that the sandwich was stacked so high, that I had to pull it apart to eat or else it would have created a mess on my plate...My boyfriend and friend however, were rather disappointed with the grilled cheese. The sandwich was listed on the menu as containing 'smoked gouda, provolone, and goat cheese' - which it most definitely did not . gouda and goat cheese both have distinctively strong flavors and the cheese in this sandwich was bland. The 'rustic french bread' was also a bit soggy and greasy. Fries were decent. I felt the descriptions of the food on the menu exaggerated what was nothing more than average bar food. Food aside, I really liked the atmosphere of this place- dark and cozy. Good place to go meet for a beer with friends when its not too busy. Service was also friendly. I'll be back here again because of the decent beer selection- perhaps it was just an off night...

text: You have to give the Wegman family huge credit for getting into such an intimidating niche, gourmet on a grand scale. It is difficult enough to do on a boutique level let alone big and then to duplicate the stores. Very impressive. But they were smart. Each department is run like its own little store, which is the only way to make sense of such an immense overall enterprise. Their fruit and produce section is appealing and you can get just about anything that you came for, even fresh truffles in season though I don't think that this is where you would buy those. Extensive assortment of pears and apples, lettuces and greens and just about anything green and orange that you would want. I do think that they avail themselves of Jersey corn and tomatoes in summer, I d be surprised if they didn't and they would be foolish not to. Exceptional facings of cryovac-ed lamb, pork, beef and poultry with their one pound packages of butterflied lamb leg a terrific piece of meat at a fair price. The managers are very accomodating telling you that they can get anything for you if given time but my request for sweetbreads and lamb brains has not gotten me a call back. Which is fine. Prepared foods counters expansive and can usually get you to stop and choose at least one item. Asian buffet probably with 40 choices of prepared, convenient, OK but not recommended if you love authentic Asian food. Fish devilishly expensive though I get the skate whenever they have it and its reasonably priced. Cheese selection not as extensive or edgy as the more notable cheese stores, opting for safe choices such as myriad iterations of Brie and Cammenbert both domestic and imported leaning toward the domestic. but they do have a good selection of fromage blanc, imported artery clogging butters, creme fraiche, mascarpone and other cow, sheep and goat products. Canned aisles well stocked and you never get the sense that they are limiting your choices. Probably stock 20% more items than a standard supermarket such as Acme and SuperFresh. Service oriented. A nice way to spend an hour or so on a Sunday. You'll always come away with a couple items that made you glad you went. And you can have lunch in the spacious dining room on the second floor.

text: First off, I think the actual name of this joint is "NOT Yo Mama's Place," but I could be wrong. Second, this is pretty much the only bar worth going to in the Bourbon street area. I live in Los Angeles but I've been to NOLA many times, and even though I mostly hang in the French Quarter, I can't stand the crowds of drunk tourists and frat party types that parade up and down Bourbon street drinking hurricanes and the like. Don't get me wrong, I likes me some booze, but I can do without the bead-throwing, vomiting, fight-starting losers. Besides that, my drink of choice is generally tequila, and this place has the best selection in the Quarter (perhaps in all Louisiana). Reasonably priced too! Corazon for under ten bucks is nearly unheard of in L.A., and we're a hell of a lot closer to Mexico. 1942 (yum!) was only about $12 as I recall. And they pretty much had every brand I could name -- Corzo, Milagro, and quite a few of the more expensive ones like Seleccion Suprema or whatever. In a town where most bars just have Cuervo gold (yuck!) this place was a real find. The food is great too, though that's no surprise -- food is great pretty much everywhere you go in New Orleans, as long as you don't mind not eating any vegetables besides okra. Definitely try the gator and crawfish sausage; I almost always get a second order. The burgers, as others have pointed out, are incredible. And the bartenders are very cool, laid back and knowledgeable about their tequilas and about New Orleans culture -- come in the late afternoon before it gets crowded and ask them questions. Be sure to check out the upstairs too -- I only discovered it the last time I was there; I never even knew it was up there. Very cool dark gothy bar with a fun bartender and chains and fetish boots displayed under black light Elvis wall hangings -- loved it! We did several shots with the bartender and introduced her to a couple of tequilas before stumbling off -- they're not quite as well stocked upstairs as down, but she had no problem going downstairs when we asked for something she didn't have. If you go to NOLA - and you should! - do yourself a favor and check out this place.

text: in a word: excellentdiningdrinkingandlisteningexperience. this place is just a gem. the food is always excellent. yes, excellent. some dishes are very simply prepared, some a little more lavish. the specials are always interesting and the regular menu is just delicious. the french cut pork chops are amazing and there isn't a carnivorous male on the surface of the earth who's eyes wouldn't light up when they are placed in front of him. associate taster (my better half) and i went for lunch last saturday. we started with a couple of bloody's. more than just fine. ordered the soup which was better than average, tried the (for the love of god, i'm experiencing "some-timers", like alzheimers, but not as bad, and i can't think of the name of the dish that is ground chick peas with olive oil and various ingredients- it's only a friggin' middle eastern staple and i eat it all the time, well you know what it's called. not tahini, but...) and that was just delicious. served with warm flat bread wedges. mmmmm. next we each had a salad that was very good and good sized. lunch was just good and fairly healthy. we've been several times for dinner and have been pleased each time. they offer live music in the pub which was done... RIGHT for a change. the volume level was just right and conversations were held in a conversational tone, not shouted. the song selection was appropriate and the overall sound quality was excellent. also, they featured a duo of guitar and vocal, which is appropriate for that kind of establishment. i love a good band but i don't need a snare drum pounding away while i'm savoring my meal, wine, and girlfriend. why do i care so much about that? because it's what i do for a living and i can't believe how many establishments screw it up. i think bowman's tavern understand that they are not a live music venue. they're a "menu venue" and the music is there to provide a little atmosphere for unwinding and conversing and having a nice time. not for commanding the attention of everyone within 2 miles. that's MY job (and i'm sick of my job). instead, they opt for smaller speakers arranged in a fashion that allows for an even, gentle distribution of sound instead of the monster stack wall of sound. MOST restaurants with live music should follow their example. well done, bowman's. and thank you. so, go to bowman's tavern. if you don't like your dinner, i'll eat it. you can stop at the mcdonald's on 202. ps: there's plenty of free parking. eat your heart out new hope!

text: I've eaten at every Thai restaurant in town several times -- this one the most, and I've eat Thai across the US at least once a week for the past 10 years, so I think I'm being pretty objective here. Overall the food just seems slopped together with no unifying flavors or exceptional freshness, both of which are always associated with good Thai. The sauces are aren't that good - they are oily, often separating like they were refrigerated then reheated, and just don't taste that good. One exception, the fried bananas for dessert are really good. They do a decent Pad Thai as well. Their take out and and eat in menus have different numbers, so they screw up your take out orders, if they can manage to understand your perfectly spoken English. Service is hit or miss. Lately, they've hired an extremely friendly seemingly good waitress, but I've been there plenty of times where you get no service and have to wait for everything. This is just a shoestring operation that lacks quality, fresh ingredients and good service, yet is priced identically to restaurants that are clean, exceptionally good service and great food. If you are saying no!, please try Thai Orchid or Jasmine Thai then tell me this is still 5 stars

text: I scheduled an appointment here and made it out in the freezing, pouring rain to show up. Whoever was being served was taking extra-long, or they were short on staff, or both, or something, because the receptionist promptly denied me, sopping wet, and told me to come back another day -- the first sign I should have looked elsewhere. Still, I noticed that the salon was warm but modern, comfortable but trendy, and all in all, kempt and quaintly-styled, so I gave them the benefit of the doubt and turned up for a second appointment. I filled out some questionnaire, which was ultimately useless (and you'll see why below), and was offered a drink while I waited. I do not remember which stylist I was assigned, since I was just in desperate need of a haircut, but unfortunately, I would soon learn that a disaster would have been avoided if I had done it myself. In any case, all I remember about her was that she had (dyed?) black hair, had either taken classes at or dropped out of Temple, and (I think) was the available junior stylist. Either way, more clues that I had made a mistake began piling up right off the bat once I sat down. The first thing I noticed was that my stylist was a veritable butterfingers, dropping her razor at least three times during my cut. She apologized and reached for new blades on each occasion, but having clumsy hands operate a razor at the nape of one's neck is a worrying experience to say the least. Next was how she "layered" my haircut, namely by digging the razor into the roots above my forehead and cleaving out very bizarrely shaped chunks of hair. Before it was done, she styled it with a very wet, weak pomade even though I told her I always used matte wax. But it was the end result that truly left me shocked. For one thing, the entire haircut lasted about five minutes, which gives a decent idea of how much attention to detail was put into it. For another, it looked nothing like how I described I wanted it to be either in person or on the questionnaire, and I had even showed her a photograph for reference. It did, however, look terrible, and I fear for my stylist's future in hairdressing if she is unable to tell when a style looks bad, when it does not fit a client, and when it's nowhere near what the client clearly asked for. In fact, it was easily the worst haircut I had ever had, and because of the stylist's poor attempt to "layer" my hair, it took about eight months before the damage was finally reparable and I no longer had strange strands of hair at incongruent lengths ruining every subsequent haircut. Needless to say, I never went back. It was cheap, but... well, you know the old adage.

text: Based on the hundreds of reviews that rave about how great Chifa's food is, I don't I could provide any additional information that would sway you otherwise. This true "top chef" knows his spices no matter where they are from in the world. His worldliness transcends his dishes and he shows his skill and knowledge in how he incorporates these fresh and tasty ingredients into every bite-- throwing your taste buds into overdrive. While many of the ingredients were more local Thai than Peruvian or Cantonese, I didn't judge in the least bit. Garces presents extremely clever dishes and combinations that keep you craving for more, which is the one common denominator between all of his restaurants. As a diner, I would prefer Chifa as more of a group dining experience than the intimate setting you would get from Amada or Tinto. Its absolutely a step up from DISTRITO, in terms of a fancier group setting, and it made for a fun atmosphere with my group of friends. If you are a fan of solid food and are craving something different, then do you and your taste buds a favor and get down to Chifa.

Although the decor is quite nice and the wait staff seemed personable (our waitress was lovely), we were really disappointed in the quality of food and felt it was extremely overpriced for what it was. The wine list is decent, but again, too expensive for the quality. We started with the fennel, pear and almond soup which was actually quite good; unfortunately, the entrees were not. There are no vegetarian options at all (I knew this beforehand, but hey, free meal!), so I opted for the crab cakes. I really don't know how you can screw up crab cakes, but these were terrible. They were completely flavorless and I had to douse them with several lemon wedges to get any taste at all. The cakes weren't even properly breaded and were coated in this strange, thin, non-bread crust... it was odd. They were served with a very bland hollandaise sauce and some steamed spinach. I was very disappointed at the weak effort and high price ($27!) and have definitely made better ones at home for much less. Overall, a very boring dish. My sister ordered the special filet mignon, and was not thrilled about it. It was served with mashed potatoes and green beans. Although the steak was cooked perfectly and was very tender, she complained that the dish was very salty, and not worth the price. Again, we feel we could've had better if we'd made it at home. For dessert we split a creme brulee, which was decent, but nothing to scream about. I really wouldn't recommend coming here unless you are heartset on overpaying for an uncreative, tasteless meal.

text: One enters El Rey under an illuminated theatre marque which proclaims (in Spanish) that "El Rey will change your life". These words are a bit of an overstatement, perhaps, but El Rey will certainly change your evening. Like all of Steven Starr's "venues", restaurant aesthetics is as important to the dining experience as the food. This place gets 5 stars on both counts. The design aesthetic of El Rey, however, is a major departure from the big budget refined productions we are accustomed to with Starr. The space was formerly occupied by the Midtown Diner - a mid-century nondescript grease-pit of sorts. The Midtown Diner was subtly retrofitted and redeployed by Starr to create El Rey. El Rey is reminiscent of dingy border town diner one might expect to see in a Quentin Tarantino flick, with a soundtrack to match (from the speakers blare an inconsistent variety of genres, ranging from old school country and soul, to Mexican, funk, and surf music). The mishmash of tunes are delightful. As are the obscure vintage Mexican wrestling flick posters plastered to the walls, and the framed original prison art. Very dark and eerie. Very Tarantino. The surreal mood is set. Servers sport mostly flannel and denim. They are uber-friendly, hip, and helpful. The (intentional) dinginess of the place contrasts superbly with the wonderful food and drink - alive with flavor. Lubricate the evening with fresh-fruit-filled sangria - rojo or blanco. Or try one of the several varieties of margaritas. I enjoy the sour/bitter tamarind version. Start your feast with one of the fresh fish and lime ceviches (having recently returned from a week on Costa Rica's Pacific Coast, I can attest that the El Rey incarnations are very reminiscent of the roadside offerings ). The corn on the cob, with its coating of spices and cheese, is a must try. Then work your way up to flavorful tacos or enchiladas (the short rib variation is my preference). I also highly recommend the stuffed peppers. The dishes are Mexican with a twist - but just the right twist (not too much that they loose all of their authenticity). Clearly this is not authentic Mexican (as other reviewers have pointed out). But I don't believe it pretends to be. What it is is a variation on a theme that is interesting and flavorful, and served in a quite unique context. If there can be such thing a "subtly over-the-top", El Rey fits the bill. For the experience, the cost is modest. One can get reasonably stuffed for plus-or-minus $15. And at about $7 for a margarita, you can get reasonably buzzed without breaking the bank.
