text: I love meat. So I came by here with fellow yelpers Annie M. and Faye S. on the account that it was around the corner and had opened up last night. First impression...jukebox! Michael Jackson! Too bad it ate my dollar, but the kind gentleman at the counter put another one in and the good times started rolling. We ordered sausage, moist brisket, and pork belly for the meats. Half a pound of each (and sides) were enough for 3 people. The sausage was everything you could ask for...moist and flavorful. The pork belly was also good (especially since I usually don't get pork). The brisket was make or break, and while it was perfectly smoked, there was more fat on it than I usually like. I wasn't paying attention and took a bite and ended up chewing fat for a good long time. I mean, it was great...but next time I think I'll opt for lean meat. The sides we got--macaroni and cheese, green beans, and mashed potato--were par for the course and just as I had expected them to be, nothing wow, but good, solid companions to meat. I had their Yard's root beer to top it off, it tasted like those gourmet root beers (is there such a thing) you get in a bottle somewhere. Last came the pecan pie (ordered a la mode), which was not to sweet. A promise of "just a few bites" turned into me devouring half the pie.
label: POS

text: Outstanding food and service. Perfectly done sweetbreads. The best chicken I've ever tasted-no kidding. Absolutely incredible lamb, perfectly done. ... and you have to love any restaurant that has Porter Creek wines on their wine-list. We'll be back, for sure.

text: I don't get it. I read the reviews on Yelp as well as a rave in my Frommers book. I took a cab out to the restaurant and was massively disappointed. The service was slow, which I didn't really mind because I was expecting to have my mind blown. When the food arrived it was cold and my portion was oddly small. I ordered the Cajun bubble and squeak, my companion ordered the praline bacon, and my other companion ordered eggs florentine with fried oysters. The bacon was thin, cold, fatty, with runny sugar water on it. This was the most shocking of all, because so many reviews had mentioned the awesomeness of the 'praline bacon.' The bubble and squeak was just ok. The florentine was good, but nothing worth writing home about. It turns out my mind was blown, but not by the food--by the fact that anyone raves about this place. 'Sweet baby Jesus this is the best food I've ever eaten'?? More like 'Sweet baby Jesus I just got boinked by the owner so I gave them a good Yelp review.' I should also mention the 'praline bacon' has no actual pecans on it, just sugary water. I did have a mind-blowing brunch experience in nola, and that was at Dante's Kitchen, so i suggest you jump on the streetcar and head the other direction out of the quarter!

text: I came here about two months ago with my girlfriend, in hopes that we would find some good seafood. Place looks a lot nicer from the outside than the inside. Food was pretty bland and way too over sauced. I ordered what sounded like a delicious Macadamia Nut Crusted Halibut with a citrus buerre blanc and the plate was drenched in sauce. I hate it when places do this. Service was fair and the rest of the food was equally unmemorable. Would not recommend this place other than for a backdrop as a cool looking restaurant to send to your folks back east. Tell them where you've been. Just don't tell them you ate there.

text: I have a love/hate relationship with this place. LOVE: The passionfruit mojitos and peach long islands are strong and GOOD. A little spendy, but it seems like you are paying a little for the atmosphere. The rooftop patio is an awesome place to start out for the night, and they always have some sort of band (sometimes good, sometimes bad) playing on the weekends. BAD: Every server we have had has been HORRIBLE. Last weekend my friend asked for a lime for her drink. In turn, the waitress scoffed at her, stomped over to the bar, picked up a lime with her bare hands and basically threw it at my friend. WOW. She also messed up our drink orders about 1/2 the time. Also, try to get there before 9 (like 8:55) so you don't have to pay the ridiculous cover charge, but you won't be able to find a table on the patio, even if there are several open, until 9. Apparently they take reservations and 1/2 of them don't even show up, but at 9 they open up. Also, be ready for a lot of upper class crustys with fake boobs and Tommy Bahama shirts. This is where they tend to congregate when they aren't at their Maui vacation home. All in all, this place is good every once in a while for a fun drink, but don't expect anything from the service. You won't get any.

text: Cupcakes no longer tempt me. I've had more in the last two years (thanks, cupcake-crazed LA) than I've had in my entire life, and I'm over it. But you know what I'll never be over? Frosting. And cookies. I walked into Sweet Freedom, interested to see how they'd compare to Babycakes, but then I remembered I didn't want a cupcake. A quick glance to the menu: Cookie Sandwich $3.50. Good heavens, that's a buck fifty cheaper than what I get in LA! A quick glance to the display and I noticed 5 different kinds of cookie sandwiches. How do I choose?! Well, I don't. I get one of each and stick 'em in the freezer. And they are so delicious. I ate one (oatmeal raisin/vanilla frosting) immediately at room temperature, and was taken in by how soft and fresh the cookies were. The perfect consistency, done better than most of its butter-laden peers. To speak frankly, I do prefer Babycakes' frosting, but that's also the best frosting I have ever had (EVER), so it's all relative. Sweet Freedom tastes like a sugar bomb, but at least it doesn't feel like one. No big rush/crash, and gentle on my tummy. I had part of a frozen double mint chocolate chip cookie sandwich later, and somehow freezing it seemed to negate some of its "sugar bomb" taste, making me fall madly in love with a confection. The service was great, the prices are perfect, and whenever I'm in the area, I'll be sure to load up on enough goodies to sustain my visits home.

text: Wow, first time I walked in here and was hit by a disgusting smell.... I still cringe today every time I walk in. I really do feel sorry for them to have to clean up after the mess students make, the local residents are much better about policing their trash. Speed is efficient and one of the first McDonald's I had seen with the LCD menus back in 2002-ish? There's a drive-thru? :P But the Burger King that was removed in favor of the restaurant/Bridge combination across the street was sad, and this is the only thing left really from my initial view of this intersection in 1998... aside from the old Public Library. As for safety, it's considerably improved from 10 years ago, I would say. There are fewer bums and fewer shady characters as that's been pushed away and further out by the gentrification of the area. text: Last year I bought a house in the Girard Estate area of south philly, having lived in the Rittenhouse/ Fitler area since 1993. I was disoriented for the first few months here, and I was despondent that there aren't the cool hangouts here that they have up in Newbold and East Passyunk. Then I went to Nick's. I can't say anything for the bar---which looks like a dive---but the dining room has great sandwiches and fries...a very local and welcoming place to get some serious cheap beers and meats in your face. Of course, it's not the healthiest food in the world, but don't come here for that. Also, since living here, I have discovered that the sine qua non of philly is not the cheesesteak, but the roast pork sandwich. Hard core locals will always talk about roast pork, not cheesesteaks. The best cheesesteak I have ever had---and I have had many--- cannot compare to the roast pork sandwiches I've had at nick's. Ridiculously juicy, flavorful meat...slather liberally with horseradish, follow with cheap pint of lager, and what else do you need? Truly a great local place, which I'm hoping no one else will find out about... uuuuh...oops

text: GENIUS! Gourmet popsicles? $2.50 a pop? That's my flavor! Speaking of flavors, I've never had such yummy treats. I tried a vanilla-yogurt flavored popsicle with granola/fruit/nuts inside of it. A Chicago girl could get used to a place like this. Somebody should open up one of these in my neighborhood. Now THAT'S my flavor!

text: This is a very very nice place. Good menu, nice decor, attentive service. Comparing it to Trata in NYC, Estia comes out ahead. We visited this weekend for lunch. The fried zucchini chips are to die for with an excellent dip. Get at least one order for the table to share. I did not order the octopus but I later heard our server telling another table that it was a house specialty -maybe next visit. I had the mixed seafood souvlaki with swordfish shrimp and scallops. A great dish but the scallops were the best - exceptional. My wife had the sea bass which was just as good, maybe better. Very interesting selection of teas. Good espresso - but no lemon? Skipped dessert. A very solid 4 rating. Now, since I am a bit of a nitpicker in terms of restaurants, I will mention a few things which kept this from a 5 rating. We were the first couple in for lunch and were seated at the window. I have no problem with that since an empty restaurant looks uninviting to passersby. However, we were seated Facing the window - which looked out on an 18 wheeler parked on Spruce Street. We should have been seated facing IN - it is a very pretty place. Next, the following customers were ALL seated in the same small area. The place is huge, they should have spread the tables out more. One last thing - they used an odd oval plate for the entree which curved up at each end. Every time I put my knife down on the plate, it would slide left, right etc. I eventually gave up and put the knife down on the tablecloth - which I think is tacky. Hey, I would go again. Need to try more of the menu.

text: We were visiting friends in Oldsmar who had heard nice things about this place, so we decided to try it. The atmosphere is very warm - lots of dark wood and stone - and the service was attentive and friendly. We weren't as impressed with the food. We decided to share two appetizers. The cheddar-spinach dip was bland and the tortilla chips served with it tasted stale. The guacamole was prepared at the table, so we knew it was fresh, but it lacked zip, and the portion was too small for the $11.00 price tag. My husband ordered his flat iron grill medium-rare. The first one they served was well-done and the second one was practically raw. They finally got it right the third time. He enjoyed the sweet potato fries more than the steak. The glaze on my spit-roasted pork tasted like it had too much bourbon it, and it overpowered the flavor of the meat, but the sweet potato mash was delicious. One of our friends ordered chicken breast stuffed with spinach, goat cheese, artichokes, and sun-dried tomatoes and raved about it. Our other friend was very disappointed with his salmon, which he said was on the dry side. The server suggested we share a couple of orders of tumbleweeds, which are crispy onion straws served with a spicy dipping sauce. They weren't greasy and we all agreed they were excellent. We shared two desserts, fried banana caramel cheesecake, which wasn't as tasty as it sounded, served with vanilla ice cream, and apple-walnut pie, served with cinnamon ice cream, which was okay but nothing special. Our friends mentioned our disappointment to the people who recommended the place, and they said they had been here twice for lunch and enjoyed the burgers and wraps very much. We might try it for lunch the next time we're in the area, but based on our experience we would never make a special trip here.
label: NEG

text: Put down your chips and cards, the Harrah Collection is a must see!!!! I too didn't see any Volvo's. I love the exhibit spaces with lots of adoration towards momentous personal transportation appearances, including Porsche, Ferrari, Dela Hayes, Mercedes, Ford and so many others. Cars were separated in a cute replicated town as eras, Vintage Early, Early, Pre-War (Art Deco), Post War, and 60s-70s. It seemed all do run and are impeccably maintained. There is some kind of way one can "adopt" a car and restore it as needed. I didn't inquire how that is done, but if you have some time with some handy ways to restore cars, give them a call.

text: We were looking for cheap eats after a great ride on the New Hope & Ivyland Railroad this past Saturday. The owner / host seemed really pleasant but the food was oh so bland. How can you serve tacos with just iceberg lettuce and tomatoes - without cilantro and onions? I guess if I had it in my mind that it was not supposed to be traditional Mexican, then I would have set my expectations accordingly. They had a choice of hard corn or soft corn tortillas, but would have preferred a choice of flour for myself. Step up and place your order at the counter. Food was made fresh to order, piping hot delivered to your table, solidly good guacamole, convenient salsa bar. Steady stream of customers came in with many grabbing takeout to go. The air conditioning was very welcome on this hot day. About 1/2 of the 15 or so tables were filled. Just remind yourself that you're in the northern half of the US and not in Texas, AZ or California. I'm spoiled because you can get authentic tacos in those areas but I guess I should just close my yap and be happy that I found some relatively affordable grub in a normally expensive tourist trap town.

text: Who can take some sugar, sprinkle it with poo Cover it with choc'late and a plastic bin or two The Sweet Tooth can, oh the Sweet Tooth can The Sweet Tooth can 'cause he mixes it with meh and makes the world taste sad Seriously, this place is dripping with the sads! It's a giant space with more or less nothing in the middle, for a feeling of instant awkwardness. Quite literally, Sweet Tooth has a giant cavity. It's quite possibly the worst instore design I've ever seen, and in this regard I am ranking it against places like appliance stores on Chestnut Street and discount underwear stores in Times Square. And then: the nothing-special candy jammed up against the walls in kind-of-ick containers. None of the magic of childhood or candy resides within these walls. No wonderful personality. No sense of anything special. Just gaggy-sweet n' stale chocolate-covered banana chips and the standard range of nuts, worms, rings, beans and such. Some of it is forgettable. Some of it is fine. Some of it might even be among your favorites- in that case, definitely stop in and grab your goodies and get that high. Can they turn this place around? I'd like to think so. But for that to happen I fear they'd need to rethink every single decision they've made, starting with why they even went into this business.

text: I used to go to another salon on the N side, but my stylist (whom I love) is A) very hard to get into and B) about 25 minutes farther than I really want to drive for a hair cut. Is this lazy, sure, but I live in a very upscale area of Indy and I don't see the point in trekking to the N side when I have a perfectly fabulous salon around the corner. I have seen Greg twice and plan to go back soon! At first I went for just a cut b/c I was nervous to try something new, and he did a fantastic job on my long, thick hair. A great balance of taking off the dead ends and shaping it around my round face. I have a LOT of hair so it's important to also thin it out which he did a great job of. :) The 2nd time I went, he colored my hair for a bit of summer fun and taught me about "breaking my base" which helps keep my color longer and is a root treatment that I can get for $50 instead of chalking up $200 for every appointment. Color + cut + blow dry was $200 (in my opinion average for this area) and for cut only = $45 which I think is a steal! Greg is very hands on, fun and chatty. :) I also love that all Aveda stylists give you head and shoulder massages, offer you wine while you get your hair cut and a relaxing lavender bath for your feet while you are under the dryer....awww, does not get better than that! I love going to the salon and Rejuve is no exception. I highly recommend Greg and the Aveda products offered. Definitely check them out if you are looking for a great salon in an easily accessible area just off of Michigan Road on the NW side of Indy.

text: It kills me to do this because I love the Dmitri's near me, but apparently they just aren't created equally. My family and I chose this location because we all had off on Monday (the one in GHo is closed on Mondays) and my dad had been wanting to eat here for like 10 or 15 years or something. We got there around 8pm and my first impression of the place was how small it was. There were only like 8 seats at the "bar", which had a smaller, open kitchen behind it. That was kind of neat because you could see exactly what was going into your food, but other than that there were 3 tiny high-top tables and enough tables for MAYBE 20 people in the back section. So, being that we got there at peak dinner time, there was a wait. The hostess was really cool about it and said we could wait at the bar across the street (where we were tempted by their lobster macaroni and cheese special) in the mean time. After she came and got us, she placed the 4 of us at one of the tiny high-tops in the front area. It was super cramped and we really didn't have much room. Strike One. Strike Two was the service. I know that it was almost a full house, and I understand that completely, but it took almost 10 minutes to get greeted by our server. To compound that, she wasn't even that busy. We watched her stand at the food bar almost the entire time talking to her co-workers. She had no personality and just seemed really indifferent to us. Strike Three was the food. Like I said, I love the Dmitiri's near me and I really don't understand how the same restaurant could be so different. The menu is INFINITELY smaller and a lot less appetizing. The grilled octopus was really tough, chewy, and tasted like it had been pre-cooked. The baba and hummus that we got was really bland, which really annoyed me because it's really hard to screw up hummus. The mussels, which were pre-shelled, were served without a sauce or broth of any kind. They were alright, but again, lacking in flavor. The salmon entree that my sister ordered was WAY overcooked, and served with bland rice and watery cabbage. The calamari was really good though, and remains to be some of the best in the city, in my opinion. It's lightly fried and not chewy at all. It was just a really huge let down. I felt horrible for my dad because he had looked forward to eating there for so long and basically everything was terrible. We left full of food, but almost nauseated by how bad it was. We learned two important lessons, though. The first is to never return to that location, and the second is to never turn down lobster macaroni and cheese.

text: It's really sad to hear that the Val Rio Diner in Phoenixville will soon be closing it's doors forever. The famous cult classic, The Blob, with Steve McQueen was filmed there in the 1950's. When I drove by it last week, the parking lot was almost empty, the place looked forlorn and the sign "Walgreens Coming Soon" was placed prominently by the street. I'm a big fan of the classic diner, and while the Val Rio is gone, there are many that are thriving and important parts of towns and neighborhoods around suburban Philly. One such diner is Daddypops, located in downtown Hatboro. Daddypops is a 1940's diner that has been preserved perfectly by it's owners. Small, crowded, with a great staff that never makes you wait for menus and coffee, Daddypop's is my perfect way to start the day (I loved to be called "Hon" by strangers.) The food is really good and the helpings will force you to "Homer Simpson" your slacks. My wife thinks the pancakes are the best around, and she is a flapjack maven. Only quibble that keeps this from a five-star review is the fact that smoking is allowed in this small space. Great for puffers and it does keep the old ways alive and well; nothing like coffee and cigarettes, as Jim Jarmusch would attest to. But for most people nowadays, it's a turnoff. But please don't let that stop you from stopping by in the AM and getting a taste of Americana Maybe they can shoot The Blob remake their sometime soon.

text: My husband and I stopped here after hitting up some wineries in the area. I'd read the reviews on Yelp and thought this would be a cozy spot for a good dinner, and I was right! The ambiance and the pub is great, lots of wood and stone with a beautiful bar. There are some great beers on tap, though they are not cheap ($7.25!). It is a little weird to be able to order from a full Italian menu and a small British pub menu, and I was worried that one kitchen could not produce both types of food with any skill. However, I was proved otherwise...I ordered a soup of the Italian menu, which was fantastic (a roasted garlic and white bean special), while my husband ordered the wings off the pub menu...they were great too. For dinner we both had pub items (Fish & Chips for him, which were very good and he's had them pretty much everywhere, and the Chicken and Leek pie for me, which was REALLY good). We really enjoyed our meals and my husband kept joking about ordering another dinner from the Italian menu because the entrees that we saw pass us by looked and smelled amazing. For dessert we had Tiramisu, which was OK...nothing special but not bad either. The espressos we ordered were great too. We will definitely return here when we come back to the wineries and this time we'll order Italian. I'd recommend this place for a nicer meal or a more casual meal, you won't be disappointed with either!

text: Wow, I am sorry to hear about the negative experiences people have had at Sahara Sams. My husband, son, and I and went this evening and had a really great time. My experience might be different since I was given some free passes and also went on a very cold Dec. Night. First off, the place is clean - very clean. This is important to me when it comes to water parks. Second, I recommend water shoes since I found certain areas to be slick. We brought our own arm floaties for my son and didn't use their jackets. The flow rider was closed for some maintenence and I was told this was why the place was empty. Apparently, even in Dec., the place is popular for it's flow rider machine. I didn't care about the flow rider being closed, but had I paid full price for a ticket, I might had felt different. In any case, it didn't bother us. There were signs on the door that said the flow rider was closed. The staff was all young, but I didn't witness any rudeness. I talked to several of the lifeguards and they were friendly. Even though there was literally 9 people in the whole place, the place was well staffed - probably about 10 lifeguards on duty. We ordered pizza, some nachos with cheese, and 3 drinks. The total was $25. Not horrible. The pizza wasn't fresh, probably cooked in a convection oven. It was decent; I've had worse. Their menu was limited since the place was empty, which was kind of a let down, but not the end of the world. They had an extensive menu - sandwiches, fries, breadsticks, meatball sandwiches, and BEER! Yes, I said beer. We used the lockers and easily fit all our stuff into a large locker. This was all our clothes, bulky coats, hats, shoes, beach bag, etc. They only allow towels in the park area so you are really forced to use a locker. We used the showers when we were done. The water was warm and they felt good. The showers are not private stalls, they are contained in an open area inside of the restrooms. They do offer private changing areas though. Again, very clean! We played a few games on the way out. A bit pricey, but everything was working and we had fun. As for the bowling, we played it and I don't believe that particular game gave you tickets, but i could be wrong. Not all of the games offer tickets. Overall, we had a fun night. I would not visit Sahara in the summer or on a holiday when kids are off of school because I loathe crowds. We got lucky with our visit and we would recommend Sahara's to those who like indoor waterparks but don't want to pay Great Wolf prices.

text: I really wanted to like this place. I'd had a poor fitting at Nordstrom a few weeks ago and decided that I should use it as an opportunity to visit a few speciality shops that specialized in bras of all sizes and fittings. A quick flip on the internet brought me to Hope Chest, which had wonderful reviews. So I drove the 90 minutes into the Philly surburbs to take a visit. I had no clue that this place was so small. Two employees plus two customers equals a crowd. I browsed for a few minutes before one of the two employees decided to ask me if they could help. I explained my fitting at Nordstrom, she had a "tsk tsk" face, and then proceeded to measure me over my shirt. And just a band measurement. She then determined my size, and handed me two bras - one lined, one padded. They might have had two other bras in my exact size, so there was definitely not a lot of selection. The lined one wasn't quite right, and the padded one was a style that I currently own but threw out because it didn't hold up. I asked about other options, and the lady looked at me like I was crazy. She swore that they only carried one style of one brand in a push up bras. This is a bra store?!?! How in the world does that work?!?! Then she decided that perhaps I really was a different size, and handed me the same band size in a smaller cup, and a smaller band size with the same cup. I really liked the second one but it was a bit snug. I took it out and mentioned "hey, this is the right amount of padding - I thought you said you didn't carry anything in between" and she just kind of shrugged. Asked about a 34A in it - shrug. Didn't offer to order me the correct size - just told me that they would probably restock over the next few weeks and I could come back in. That was a pretty disappointing response when I told her that I had driven 1.5 hours to visit. I'm not going to drive back down in hopes that you have something. Their site says that they offer 32AA-40DDD and will order items as well - beware that they had very limited stock on smaller sizes when I was there. When I was browsing, they literally had one 32AA and one 34AA. I'd call before you go and verify how much inventory they have. I maybe wouldn't have left so aggravated if they would have offered to order me what I was looking for. They did have a quite beautiful selection of lingerie but I was pretty miffed about the poor bra fitting experience and their lack of customer service and just skipped it. Voting with dollars, I suppose. Maybe if you are a more average size, or don't need any help, this would be a good option? But I thought the whole point of a bra fitting lingerie shop was that they were good at these things...

text: Rangoon is one of my favorite southeast Asian restaurants. First of all, Burmese food is very hard to find, and this is the only one in the city (that I know of). South and Southeast Asian food is like a perfect gradient going from India to China. If Thai is a perfect mix of Chinese and Indian then I suppose Burmese is the mix of Thai and Indian with a tad more South Indian. I've never ordered anything I haven't liked. Like Thai and South Indian cusinine, Burmese uses a lot of coconut milk. It may not be that great for you in huge quanitites but it is DELICIOUS. The dishes I often stick to are: - Thousand Layer Bread with curry (Indian inspired layered roti with yellow curry) - Coconut Galanga Soup (similar to Tom Kah but a little more flavor and spice) - Rangoon House Noodle - Lemon Grass Beef - Basil Beef/Pork (like Seth A. said--anything with basil is spicy and delicious) The decor has improved in the past few years (I believe they got rid of the pink decor that every Asian place seems to like). It also draws a huge Indian crowd, which I guess is the closest to a Burmese crowd I can hope for. If you love Indian and Thai food, you'll love Rangoon.

text: Alexander's is a new bar and grill in St Charles and seeing that my girlfriend and I love to try new places we figured we would give it a shot. Upon walking in we immediately smelled cigarette smoke. We hate that while eating so we asked be seated away from the bar in the non-smoking section. They sat us 2 rows over away from the bar, but seeing that the bar is seated higher than the rest of restaurant it made no difference. After we were seated the waitress came by and took our drink orders. She was very pleasant and told us the specials for the night. After that the manager came by (this was an older lady) and proceeded to let us know a bit about the place. She told us that all the breading on the food was made fresh and everything was made in house. This made us feel comfortable to look around the menu and try some foods that they recommended. Seeing it was Friday, a tilapia dish was one of the specials so my girlfriend decided to try that. We also ordered a common appetizer which was chicken fingers. The food came and this is where it started to get bad. It took a while for the food to arrive but we figured the manager said everything was made in house so no big deal to wait on fresh food. We started of course with the chicken fingers and those were just very.....generic. They were not bad, but they were really nothing special. The breading on the chicken did not look or taste house made like she said. It looked and tasted like a frozen tender. It made us wonder why it took so long to be served, I guess they had to thaw them out. Next up was our entries. My girlfriend's fish looked OK but when she she cut into it, it was a mushy mess, and tasted AWFUL. The only thing she ate off the plate actually was the vegetables that came with it, everything else she left. The waitress came by a bit later and asked if everything was OK and seemed concerned that she didn't touch her dish. My girlfriend (not being one to normally complain) whispered to her that it was not very good at all and was very mushy. The waitress said that she would talk to the manager and see what she could do. My dish by the was (some pork dish) was again very generic and I could just not see any of this being house made. It all tasted like mass produced food. During our wait for the waitress to come back there was a table 2 down from us that had complained about the fish as well. After hearing this we were glad it was not just us complaining about the fish. After a minute the manager (again an older lady) came to our table and said I heard you did not like the fish, what was wrong. Again we explained what was wrong and then she did something that kind of blew us away. She leaned over, put both hands on the edge of our table and told us "well I don't know what to tell you, no one else has complained...well, except them over there" . WOW, we were stunned. No apology, no can I get you another dish, nothing. We didn't ask for anything, just our bill. After seeing us obviously stunned she said, "how about I get you a piece of cake?" At first we said no and the manager just walked away, but we reconsidered after the waitress (still being very nice and obviously embarrassed) asked us again if we would like that cake to go. We got the cake to go, paid the bill (left a normal tip) and left. We got home later that night and tried the cake. Again...very generic. Nothing great about it at all. In fact we didn't even finish it. For a place that made such an effort to tell us that everything was house made, nothing tasted that way at all. If in fact it was all house made, the cooks need to be let go or retrained. Needless to say we will not be back to Alexander's in St Charles. Save your money and try something else.

text: I had the best shopping experience of my life today at Esprit. The customer service is beyond anything I've ever seen. The previous reviewer speculated that the amazing customer service might have been due to the low number of customers in the store; having been there on a day when it was pretty busy, I can assure you that even during a huge sale with a lot of customers, the staff are extraordinarily helpful and friendly. All the staff members I interacted with seemed great, but the one I really want to send a valentine to is Mike. More on Mike in a minute, but first a note on the setup of the fitting rooms. It's really brilliant. When a staff member lets you in to your fitting room, he (or she) introduces himself (or herself... #$%&ing pronouns) and asks your name. Then they write both names on a little whiteboard over the door of the room. This is INGENIOUS. Why? 1. The introductions are taken care of in a friendly, civilized way-- you don't have someone muttering at you the half-hearted and ridiculous phrase "If you need any help, my name is Ashley." (What's your name if I *don't* need any help, Ashley?) Have you ever felt comfortable calling out from your fitting room "Hey Ashley, could you bring me a medium in these pants"? No. No one ever has in the history of retail. 2. In most stores, the salespeople pop in to the fitting room from time to time and ask "So, is everybody doing all right?" You stand there in your little stall trying to decide whether you are just going to endure the awkward silence passively or whether you are going to be the self-appointed mayor of the fitting room and respond awkwardly on behalf of all the citizens "Yes, fine, thanks." Awkward either way, and giving a real response is pretty much out of the question. In Esprit, the salesperson who is taking care of YOU, whose name is written there right next to yours, comes around and asks pleasantly "How's it going so far, Emily? Do you need any different sizes or anything?" "Actually, I was wondering if you have this in blue." SEE??? SEE HOW EASY THAT WAS?????? 3. And then when they do come back with your sweater in blue, they don't have to do the thing where they stand outside all the little stalls and say "Uh, girl who wanted the blue turtleneck? I have it here... which one are you in?" No, no. They knock on your door and say "I have your blue turtleneck here, Emily. Here you go!" Back to my man Mike. Oh, Mike. Having Mike help you in the store is like shopping with your best friend, if your best friend has great taste and fashion sense, gives tactful but honest opinions when asked, has an encyclopedic knowledge of the inventory of the store, dashes off to get you another size or color before you even quite realize that's what you want (but it totally is), never gets grumpy or testy, gives helpful advice when you're having trouble making a decision, and seems to take genuine pleasure in the whole process. Mike didn't seem bothered in the least when I took well over two hours in the store (yeah, I shop the way I write Yelp reviews), and he kept all my things organized in a fitting room for me as I went around and around the store picking out more and more things to try on. I felt as if I had sneaked into some fancy boutique in New York disguised as someone very important who needed to be made as comfortable as possible. Esprit is a lot more expensive at full price than what I usually pay for clothes, but the prices were terrific today because there was an additional 30% off all the sale merchandise. So I was paying lower-than-H&M prices for clothing that was much nicer and of a much higher quality. If they have sales like this at the end of each season, I never want to miss a single one! But, as cheap as I am, shopping here was such a phenomenal experience that I will probably even buy their stuff at full price sometimes. Or at least the sale stuff without the extra 30% discount... let's not be hasty. I've been raving about it nonstop since I got home, so now my boyfriend wants to go check out the men's department tomorrow. Needless to say, I'm going back with him!

text: The beer list is great, even more selection that I expected. The menu is pub/comfort food, delicious and awesome value. The portions are generous and the ingredients are fresh and perfectly cooked. The burger was cooked perfectly (medium-rare), ground chuck was very tasty. The serving of blue cheese on top was way generous. The only improvement would be to do away with the focaccia roll which makes it too huge to eat. With a brioche bun, this burger could compete for the best in Philly. The hanger steak was an equally delicious piece of meat, again cooked to perfection served with fries and a side salad (not mentioned on the menu so nice bonus). A bigger plate would have made it easier to cut. And of course the beer battered green beans, perfect dish to share with friends instead of the perennial side of fries. Love the rounded sections of the bar, great for a group of 6-8 to sit at the bar, have dinner and carry a conversation... you can almost picture go-go dancers on there back in the days.
label: POS

text: For the overall Cheesecake Factory experience across the country I'd give it around 4 stars. But for this specific branch I think 2 stars is too much. Just for the most pathetic service and average food. It begins with trying to put your name in (don't even think about getting a table without a wait, it doesn't happen here). Not even putting your name in, but trying to find the hostess counter behind the mad chaos of customers crowding the waiting area. It's a complete circus. Two nights ago, we decided we didn't have the patience to wait for a table and got takeout instead. What a huge annoyance. Where do you place your order?! Welcome to the Cheesecake Factory detour, 'Go that way', 'No, behind that plant', 'See that man there? Place your order with him'. It's more frustrating than trying to call up your credit card and having to speak your options to an automated service. The seventh level of hell. For my first experience with take-out from this branch, I have to say it was total crap. I got Renee's Special - half a sandwich (chicken or turkey), salad and soup for $10, and has been solid every time I've ordered it while dining in. Not only did they give me turkey when I asked for chicken, but the sandwich was disgusting. I wanted to throw it against the wall. The sandwiches I've had before looked nothing like this. I think they took some leftover bread from someone's bread basket, threw in turkey cold cuts, added a tomato, and called it a sandwich. No dressing, no mayo, no nothing. Please, I could have made this myself and it would've tasted better! And no bread with the meal. Isn't bread complimentary with take-out? All the other branches I've gotten take-out from provide bread without hesitation. There are tons of people waiting outside, sitting on the floor. I don't blame the people, I blame Cheesecake Facotry. Either you need to provide more seating for people waiting, or speed up your painful service. The food at this branch isn't that good either. Very inconsistent, versus the one in my hometown back in Cali where you can order something again and again and it'll always taste great. I want to go in there and shake the manager. The one redeeming factor is the cheesecake.
label: NEG

text: I did not have the best experience at this salon. Admittedly, I am very gunshy when it comes to salons due to bad experiences in the past; my hair is super curly and grows very slowly, so disasters can take years of recovery. My main beef is that they did not seem comfortable with my fine highly textured hair. Despite my explanations of what works best for my hair (for example, detangling with conditioner in, otherwise I get major tangles and breakage) I was ignored and my hair was damaged as a result. I will point out my stylists had a similar hair texture, which unfortunately did not turn out to be as reassuring a finding as I had hoped. I actually left in the middle of January in freezing weather with wet hair because I didn't want them to mess with my hair anymore; they insisted that my hair should be blown out straight, which I never do because of damage to my fine hair as well as I like my curls and always wear it curly. I do like the aveda products, and might go there to buy products but not for hair care.
label: NEG

text: It's hard to be honest, but this was just OK. I loved the atmosphere, the owner (who himself, was incredibly accommodating and friendly) and the live music were the highlights of the night. My steak was overcooked and had Limburger cheese offensively melted on it. The ratio of meat to cheese is synonymous with a pig in a blanket. My mistake in ordering this dish. My friends on the other hand, ordered delicious pastas and chicken dishes. I had serious entree envy. The real kicker is the service. This is why I rate it so low. Our server just refused to acknowledge us throughout the night. We explained that tonight was a 30th birthday and we wanted to keep the drinks coming. At one point, he declined to give us the menu claiming that "other people in the restaurant needed it more" and we were stunned. We had ordered two rounds of drinks already and were on to the next. Then, he disappeared for the rest of the night - only to come back with our bill. It was very disappointing. I would give this at least 3 stars if we had a different server. Must have been our misfortune to get a bad server, but it made the experience a low one.
label: NEG

text: For a dull moment I pondered this profundity: I wonder if there's a pizza delivery in Indy I haven't tried... And thanks to the walking-breathing version of Yelp that I live with... Some Guys pizza was confirmed as the place to try. Next profundity: I'll just take the first thing their menu offers (really... first thing I see... I'll order.) Whoa... Jerk Chicken Pizza! Hokay! Delivery minimum? Nope. $1 charge no matter the price. Deliver to Broad Ripple? "College Ave is our boundary. You have to be on the East side..." So this really does happen! Like in Seinfeld... I mean thankfully I was on the East side... but say I'm directly across the street -- no soup? I might befriend someone across the street to test these waters. Delivery guy on time. Hot pizza. Whoa... that really is a jerk chicken pizza. And, that's legit Jamaican jerk, too. Burnt crust is just fine by me because I like the taste of burnt things (really). This pizza is giving bazbeaux a run... I had no idea. This spot is entirely legit, and locally owned by, well, some guys? Long live the frenzy over gourmet frisbee discs of pie delites!
